lines: Once all of this was settled, Lady Alwena could finally take the rest she deserved.
Her role at the Round Table of Brizh had rekindled her legend... and since then, young knights in search of a master worthy of the name would never cease to come knocking at her door.
Once all of this was settled, Lady Alwena left the Tower to enjoy a well-deserved retirement along the Grestian coast.
Her years of faithful service had built her a remarkable archive of anecdotes about the knights of the Round Table of Brizh, which she was, they say, always ready to share over a cup of tea.

lines: Kitty, kitty, please... come down. The head cook won't be pleased to find you up there.
The girl is trying to coax down a kitten curiously wandering amongst the kitchen's spice shelves.
Oh! Your Grace. Have you come for a drink? Or perhaps a snack?
There's not much to snack from it.
I said no animals in my Tower.
Your Grace?! What are you sa--
Of course you wouldn't eat that tiny ball of fur.
... Perhaps I love these little creatures too much for my own good.
I'll find it a good place for it to stay. You won't find him here again.
You have to admit he's quite endearing...
Look at those little black paws!
I know you said I couldn't bring a cat but...
May I keep it, Your Grace? I swear that it will behav--
OH! No, kitty, don't play with the flour bag! OH, no, come back here, please!
If you clean up right now, you can keep it.
Of course. Only if you promise to smile like that each day.
Thank you so much for letting me bring a cat here.
I named him after you, you know?
No, Sovereign, get away from this flour bag at once!
You know my name is not "Sovereign", right?
... Good luck cleaning up the flour.
Do I have something stuck in my teeth?
... Good luck cleaning up the flour.
Oh, of course, Your Grace! The floor will be as clean as a whistle.
angelica_affinity_1.prev: Kitty, kitty, please... come down. The head cook won't be pleased to find you up there.

lines: Oh! Y-your Grace, it's you. I'm terribly sorry, I thought you were
I'm sorry I was joking, Lady Angelica.
Ah. I-I heard a scream before you came from the corridor.
.but it must have just been the wind.
[font_size=18]I'm sure I heard some screams, though...[/font_size]
I'M THE GHOST OF THE TOWER!
[shake rate=20.0 level=5 connected=1][font_size=40]AHHHHHHH NO, PLEASE, NO! I'M TOO YOUNG TO DIE![/font_size][/shake]
Oh no, the cute little fellow is sleeping peacefully in my room.
He's growing up into quite a charming little pumpkin!
I hope that one day you will speak of me in those terms.
Oh, you want a vegetable nickname too! I'm sure can think of something...
... Ahem. What were you looking for here?
I heard a scream before you came out of the hallway, but it was
I'm sorry I don't live up to your expectations, Your Grace.
Yes, I'm afraid of this sort of thing.
. The Tower is a bit scary at night. The wind whistles so strangely through the windows of our quarters...
It was making such odd noises last night, and I confess it kept me from sleeping a little.
... There are these scary stories Uncle Arlin used to tell me when I was little.
I think they still terrify me today.
Sir Arlin did such a thing?
I understand why you might be a bit fearful.
Our nights are always haunted by something, aren't they? For me, it's you.
And the scaredy-cat is leaving, Your Grace.
Well, I suppose he just wanted to spark my imagination.
. A-and it worked, in a way, but he had no ill intentions, Your Grace.
... Anyway, they're just made-up stories, aren't they? And last night, it was just the wind too, wasn't it?
. just in case, let's go back to the Great Hall.
Is everything going as you wish?
Having seen you coming, the young girl moves away from the window.
.... Whenever I'm feeling a bit down, I always look for that little spark that has kept me going all this way.
... Maybe you could try and find yours?
I guess it's because my name is Sovereign.
Let's talk about you instead. What are your reasons?
Yes, I guess that's a pretty good reason.
. I'm certain that if you look closely, a good reason always finds its way to the surface.
I guess it's quite simple for me... I dreamed of being a knight for so long, after all.
The path was full of obstacles, but lately, I feel like...
Everything's fine, thank you for asking.
I must say my latest quests has really energized me...
Thank you for allowing me to remain a knight at your Table, Your Grace.
.[/font_size] I feel like I've truly made progress.
... Yes, that's it. I feel like I'm getting closer to my ideal, thanks to the missions you entrust to me.
Even if I know the road is still long before I can equal my role model...
Indeed, don't get overexcited. There's still a *long* way to go.
She goes back to the window.
I've always been passionate about the stories of Shamrock of Clovermont, one of the greatest knights from the reign of the former sovereign Candid the Kind.
They were a knight who always followed their heart and their ideals, while remaining true to their friendships.
.in a way, I want to live up to his legends.
. to become the knight the little girl I once was would have looked up to.
. sorry, I hope that doesn't sound too silly.
Are you *genuinely* impressed, or is it just because they're family?
Is making their sovereign's heart beat one of Clovermont's secret techniques?
then in that case, here's a line that will become part of my own legend.
. I am genuinely impressed that such a knight is part of my family.
... But I'll impress you too, you'll see.
Are you having blood pressure issues, Your Grace?
Bent over one of the flower beds in the garden, Angelica picks flowers with her right hand, gathering them into a large bouquet in her left.
Hey! Does *biodiversity preservation* ring a bell?
I have a bouquet for you too.
I...a-are you implying that I'm going to die soon, too?
You shouldn't sneak up on people like that...
No worries about biodiversity. I only pick flowers that grow back very quickly.
To be honest, I was planning to place flowers on the grave of our late comrade.
... I really think we need to honor all of our own who don't come back.
. nothing would break my heart more than seeing comrades fade away into general indifference.
It's part of life and the job, I know that, but.
.in my eyes, their sacrifice deserves our greatest honor.
You're right. Everyone should decorate their graves with flowers.
I understand, but we can't mourn our dead forever. We have to move on.
Your words bring a sad smile to her lips.
Wordlessly, she offers you a flower. As you reach for it, its gentle scent fills your senses.
. it won't happen again, Your Grace.
As long as I remain your knight at your side, I'll devote my whole being to preserving every life.
... I don't want to suffer any more losses. I don't want to have to honor any more graves.
. I'll do everything in my power so I never have to pick other farewell flowers again.
Her words are draped in a solemn silence, as her eyes burn with the fervor of this promise.
Then the wind rises, carrying away her oath and the scent of the flowers.
angelica_affinity_4_knight_dead.prev: Bent over one of the flower beds in the garden, Angelica picks flowers with her right hand, gathering them into a large bouquet in her left.

Thank you so much, Your Grace.

lines: With bowed shoulders and lifeless eyes, his voice is only carried by a frail tremor
Aren't you supposed to protect your subjects, Your Grace?
Her loss is a gut-wrenching grief, a weight I shall carry forever.
His too-short night can still be heard in his hoarse words.
. Let us strive to remember that she... passed in the line of duty.
She was a knight beyond reproach, and her name shall remain etched in steel.
I don't understand the meaning of a-all this, I.
W-why offer oneself up like this for your throne?
She had her whole life ahead of her...
Lady Angelica remained a proud knight of the Round Table for many years.
She was remembered as one of the most remarkable knight of her time for her loyalty and integrity.
It seems she had finally become the model she had always dreamed of being.
Lady Angelica could never accept the Sovereign's decision to wage war against the Empire.

Venerated as a heroine by the people, she regularly put the reign of Bretania in peril.

lines: Say... I keep hearing Uncle Arlin talking about a famous 'Golden Key' lately.
It's funny, because a few moons ago, I saw the exact same thing! A golden key decorating the wall of a gentleman who invited me for tea at his manor.
It shone much brighter than yours, actually.
It's a strange coincidence, don't you think?
I knew it would make you smile.
. why are you staring at me like that?
Actually, I was coming back from a quest and I got a little...confused in the Almor Forest, near Enberg.
I had no idea where I was.
Fortunately, this man lived nearby and invited me into his home.
And did you manage to get in using his directions?
Well, uh...as for getting lost, yes, I'm actually becoming quite a pro at it.
But a kind stranger offering me a snack? Now that was a first.
. No, he just offered me a snack.
After that, I hit the road again, and I felt like I walked for miles, as if time itself had warped.
And suddenly, I stepped out from the edge of the woods and found myself right in front of the Tower, which is.
... It could have been clever to be able to find this place again.
... I imagine that it was just a decoration.
Oui, Your Grace. A very shiny decoration.
It's really nothing to make a fuss about.
Yes, I saw that big key there but.
surely it can't be the one Uncle Arlin keeps talking about?
If it were necessary, I think I could find the place again.
It's strange; I'd be completely unable to point to it on a map, but I feel like my feet would know how to lead me there.
.wait. You don't want me to go back there and snatch that big key from him, do you?
No, just ask this man nicely.
... I'm sorry, but this man opened his door to me and offered me tea. There's no way I could do such a thing.
Who knows, maybe I'll even get some cakes out of it.
Forgive me, I'm a bit...somewhere else.
Her reddened eyes stare at you sadly.
Your silence seems to depress her even more.
for a friend to just be gone like that.
Y-your Grace... Does it truly not affect you at all?
.this life wasn't what I was expecting. I fear that if such things continue to repeat themselves...
I'm sorry to see you hurting Angelica.
It's part of the job, unfortunately, we need to accept it.
She leaves without saying a word.
You know we have some strange things goin' around our dungeon...?
But then we ended up with a rather strange case. A sort of... little devil.
And this kid with horns saved two of our knights, so... we're a bit reluctant to turn him into little cubes.
It's probably a trick. Kill him.
Take the time to talk to him.
We'll take precautions, but I think it's a good idea.
Would have been nice to learn more, but I understand that it could be dangerous.
... Rather grim keeping a kid like that caged up, don't you think?
anveld_grievance_cute_demon.prev: You know we have some strange things goin' around our dungeon...?

lines: Bigger than ours... heading our way...
They're going to overrun the city! We tried to evacuate the civilians, but...
... United against the undead? I'm almost excited, truth be told.
Our dungeon is inhabited by all sorts of strange creatures. Not very vicious ones, mind you
. Just demons, undead creatures, and a few ancient Gods sealed underground.
But this time, we found something different during our last expedition.
Barely fifteen years old, if that. The thing is, she must have lived her entire life in the dungeon... we're not quite sure what to do with her.
Educate her. Teach her etiquette. It's not complicated.
Entrust her to scholars. They'll know how to help her make the connection between the dungeon and life above ground.
Throw her back into the dungeon.
Oh. Force a child to live in such a different environment...?
Not bad, she'll be able to teach the scholars a lot about the depths of the dungeon.
Why not. It would be a chance for me to go back down into the dungeon and discover it differently.
I like the idea. Thanks, Kiddo.

I'll send you the cream of the crop.
find new scholars. Preferably more intelligent ones.
Lady Belladonna will undoubtedly be able to help you.
A wonderful partnership! Hope our kids can learn from it.

Your resident witch? If she's a slightly sharper knife, why not.

lines: There are many creatures in the dungeon beneath Anveld. When I was in my prime, I fought them valiantly, never giving in.
Until a lich emerged from the depths, spreading death in its wake...
That was when Lady Alwena and I put our many years of training to good use. She fought like a devil, all the creatures in Anveld's dungeon feared her.
The subject of your conversation seems to have ears everywhere, as footsteps echo in the hall.
... It was [i]you[/i] they feared, Sir Angrand.
Oh, Lady Alwena, what a pleasure. I understood that you became the intendant here.
Indeed. It's a pleasure to see all these young recruits working so hard.
The lich has returned, Lady Alwena... it has come back from the dead. Once again.
Again? That's at least the sixth time now! Or maybe the seventh...
Anyway, it's here for the eighth time, and we could really use a helping hand.
I must have a few knights who enjoy playing knucklebones.
Alwena, would you like to return to service? For old times' sake?
We should get rid of it for good. Find its source.
As long as it doesn't slow me down in my work...
Just like the good old days!
That's clever, we never thought of that.

lines: ... Our local scholars are getting on our nerves a bit.
Back in my day, they worked themselves tirelessly, and they never complain when an artefact exploded in their hands...
Perhaps because they had all died by the age of thirty?
Are you suggesting they had the courtesy to pass away before becoming a nuisance?
Anyway, now they're on strike. Apparently they want more staff, more 'humane' working hours, all that nonsense, you see...
Take care of the people you work with.
Have them do a little training in the dungeon. To stretch their legs.
Listen to their grievances, make some concessions, but absolutely nothing about wages.
Tsk... everyone complains about nothing these days.
Ahhhh, just like the summer when I was twenty... So many memories.
anveld_grievance_scholars_conditions.prev: ... Our local scholars are getting on our nerves a bit.

lines: I'll be the greatest knight this land has ever known!
I have SO MUCH to tell you!
There's so many things I want to ask you about!!
One thing at a time, for Gods' sake.
It's true that I tend to speak fast...
... T-today, someone smiled at me and shook my hands whilst I was out in the streets!.
It made me feel all funny.
It was when I was outside this morning!
Actually, I was strolling through the streets of Brizh on Columbus's back, and.
. I met a gaze full of genuine appreciation at the market...
... it made me feel all funny.
...It was so sincere. It was as if they really wanted me to be there!
. I was there, as a royal knight!
.has ever looked at me like that before.
Behind him, Colombus lets out a little whimper.

And the best part is I can stay with Columbus every day here!
You'll get used to it. It's not that big of a deal.
Was life tough on the Islands?
You know, before coming here I was a mercenary for the Islands.
Most of the time I was tasked with protecting convoys, escort work, that sort of thing...
It was often rewarding and I enjoyed any diplomatic missions but.
... let's just say things didn't go very well with my crew.
...Anyway, I never really made friends over there. It was kind of lonely...
And then at home, all the attention was hogged by Gotfrig or Rorik.
Since I'm the youngest, I wasn't of great interest in matters of regency, you see...?
...I guess that's why I never felt like I mattered until I came here...
I don't know why I'm telling you all this!
You won't hold it against me will you...?
I don't want to come across as a drag!
It's a little bit too much.
I'll learn to watch my tongue, trust me, Your Grace!
Feel free to tell me when I talk too much, okay?
Everyone tells me I talk too much, yet...
He gathers his two clenched fists in front of him with enthusiasm.
...Know that I'll do everything in my power to become the greatest knight in the world!!
It was the spark I needed, like a real boost!
I want to reignite that little flame in the eyes of each of your subjects, alright!?
He bursts into a sincere laugh.
You spot your young knight immersed in a book filled with vivid illustrations of island landscapes.
Are those pictures of the Basalt Islands?
You lean in slightly to leaf through the volume beside him.
As Sir Ari flips the pages, you discover white‑sand beaches framed by wooded ridges and lush valleys.
Have you seen this, Your Grace?
. Even though it looks like somewhere in Basalt, it's actually an island off the coast of Southbay.
. It does look similar with those forested hills overlooking the shore, but in reality it's an island off Southbay.
It's called Djinn Island, a tiny forgotten slice of paradise, apparently.
Oh yes, I know that island.
You know so many things, Your Grace!!
He lowers his voice, as if making a forbidden request.
Do you think you could send me there someday…??
One can't know everything, Your Grace!!
He dives his bright eyes back into the book and seems to find a particular kind of calm.
A clear water, free of ripples.
Ahh, not really, I have to say...
Ah, I have to admit I don't like it that much...
I have a hard time concentrating under normal circumstances, you see?
Everything's a bit too much of a blur in my head.
Discovering new horizons, other islands to explore... it's always a great joy!
You know, I've been roaming the Basalt Islands since I was a child.
But over time, everything started to look the same...the same rocks, the same coconut trees, the same breeze...
just a little escape in these books, I guess.
The Basalt Islands seem incredible to me.
I understand...it's the same from this Tower everyday.
Which is your favourite coconut tree on the Basalt Islands?
Ahhh, maybe I've just become too jaded...
Perhaps I just need...to change my perspective a bit, Your Grace?
A little life away from the islands...
Yes, that sounds dreadful, Your Grace.
You don't even have sun and sand to warm your feet.
But I'm not saying that to be mean!
After all, you have... a superb kitchen here!!
It's true. Over time, those familiarities become almost comforting.
It no longer gives me any pleasure.
There's a particular coconut tree that stands in a tiny deserted cove on Popota Island.
I've taken my best naps on its trunk, Your Grace!
His sight regained its full sparkle.
Isn't what's familiar a bit comforting?
If only I could experience those same joys on a beach...
I don't know what came over me!
Learning to draw comfort from these small things is a conscious effort!
No, you shouldn't think that way, Your Grace!
You can find comfort from that which surrounds you already!
Much more than on any idyllic beach!
After all, we're never happy without deciding to be, right?...
I've known that for a long time, and yet... I have to keep reminding myself.
Sometimes my mind darkens like... rain clouds appearing out of nowhere in the sky, and I forget...
All joy slips away like sand slipping through my fingers...
...Make sure to hold onto all the small joys in life, Your Grace.
As he returns to his book, he suddenly seems light, soothed like a sea breeze.

lines: Guess I'll just have to try to become a Count, then...
Any chance you're taking a break from being a Sovereign?
You finally did it, Your Grace.
. the ancient counties of Bretania are finally united under a single banner.
I must admit, I'm at a loss for words.
While I never doubted your virtues, I didn't expect to see you achieve such a feat with such... disconcerting speed.
He discreetly wipes away a tear with his sleeve.
I could spend all night singing your praises, but there is something else I must discuss with you.
The [b][color=986b3b]Golden Key[/color][/b]... this object, which legend claims reveals itself only to a worthy Sovereign, and which alone would allow us to unlock the Tower's full potential...
Now that every corner of Bretania answers to our command, sending a squad to hunt it down across the land seems only fitting.
Let's go in search of the Golden Key.
It's a pity to see you dismiss such a possibility out of hand, but... [font_size=18]so be it...[/font_size]
... Your wishes are my command, Your Grace.

lines: I do not hide my astonishment regarding the hooded individual who appeared before you earlier today...
You seemed to foresee his intentions with absolute certainty.
I already knew that the man had meant to kill me.
He seems to be struggling to adjust to this iteration of reality where you state the facts with such disconcerting clarity without any input on his behalf.
If that is your judgement, I trust you.
Though it is unfortunate that we were deprived of a demonstration of the Tower's anti-regicide blessing system.
Let us hope the opportunity arises again...purely for experimental purposes of course.
I won't deny my concern regarding recent events. An assassination attempt so early in your reign... it is utterly beyond reason.
Finding out more about this man's motivations or origins would probably have eased my concerns, but alas...
... he remains perfectly silent in his cell.
. But I suppose I should be less surprised. This sort of thing happens in every reign.
Am I nothing but a tool of dark power in people's eyes?
This one felt a bit personal.
I'm afraid that any soul that sits upon the throne inevitably invites the wrath of those who reject the authority of another...
Reasonably, Your Grace. It seems far too early for anyone to have formed an opinion of your rule and decided to act in such a reckless and open manner.
But let us be optimistic. I am convinced that with time you will prove yourself worthy of your reign and dispel any misplaced grudges against you.
Perhaps you'll even prove that there is a certain advantage to leaving you alive.
What a tasty idea, Your Grace.
arlin_cooking_start.prev: What a tasty idea, Your Grace.

lines: Just as I feared, the Angelor Empire has set its sights on us.
But drawing the wrath of tyrants is the inevitable fate of every accomplished ruler, isn't it?
However, it must be admitted that this new emperor, Arthur Pendragon, does not live up to his predecessor's reputation. He has presented himself with a... surprising semblance of empathy.
If, of course, he's being sincere...
Well... may Bretania emerge from this ordeal more powerful and united than ever.
arlin_emperor_reaction.prev: Just as I feared, the Angelor Empire has set its sights on us.

lines: Sir Arlin remained in service to the sovereign of the Tower until his death, faithful to his very last breath.

arlin_ending.prev: Sir Arlin remained in service to the sovereign of the Tower until his death, faithful to his very last breath.

lines: I was looking for you, Your Grace.
. a few clarifications to bring to your attention.
Did you know that while this Tower's magic keeps your illness in a dormant state, it also prevents its spread...?
Thus, there is no risk of contagion for your peers within these walls, even in the event of.
I'm highlighting this out of pure.
. concern for public hygiene, of course.
. It is not as if I had witnessed anything justifying such a clarification.
A forewarned Sovereign is worth two, are they not?
It is heartening to see that your story is already inspiring the greatest artists, isn't it?
After all, the people of Brizh have waited a long time. Your ascension is a breath of hope that I'm sure will only grow with time.
I don't know if I'm comfortable with all these expectations.
Cast aside your doubts, Your Grace.
I firmly believe that a people who have waited so long to be guided will know how to forgive any potential.
Great. I'll be the new *icon* of divine right.
And your circumstances are certainly unique to any Sovereign that reigned before you.
We have known a century without a crown, after all.
I myself grew up with tales of the old monarchs, but I never knew them beyond the pages of books...
Your arrival is the only horizon my generation has patiently hoped for, in the shadow of this sleeping Tower.
How was Brizh organized before that?
What would you have done if I hadn't arrived?
... To my great dismay, I was the favorite for the royal selection.
. but as is plainly obvious, the doors of the Tower remained closed to me.
Lack of a crown, I suppose I would have ended up as the Count of Brizh...
Even though the local nobles were doing their best to organise themselves, the pressure to find a regent figure continued to grow.
From the outside, it would have looked as if we were holding our own
. but to me, it felt like suffocating under the weight of the whole world.
And if things had continued that way...
His voice trails off into a long sigh.
arlin_hildegard_grievance_reaction.prev: It is heartening to see that your story is already inspiring the greatest artists, isn't it?

lines: Come in, look what I'm pulling out of the oven right here.
Small cakes carefully arranged on the table fill the room with a warm, spiced fragrance.
... I used to love cooking for my children, when they were younger.
. I'm quite certain they eat absolute rubbish nowadays.
He gazes at the biscuits with a gentle nostalgia.
If you would like, Your Grace, I could certainly prepare little treats for our knights from time to time.
A good cookie shared is worth a thousand words, isn't it?
That's actually how I met my wife.
Take your rightful place upon this throne.
Many labours lie ahead, to be sure, but the Tower has awoken under your reign.
Rest assured that it will soon regain its former splendour and magic.
It seems the ancient power of the Tower awoke last night, shrouded in all its majest...
Centuries-old legends indeed tell that this edifice expands in step with the growth of its ruler's reign, reflecting his power.
... Yet I had never been able to witness this glorious spectacle in my lifetime.
This expansion could also, perhaps, give us the opportunity to bolster our ranks. I recently heard word of a young man from Kutnar, whose talents as a groom are highly praised.
A recruitment that, I must admit, would relieve me of certain time-consuming tasks... erm, a minor detail.
I won't hide my emotion when I think of the entire journey walked beside you.
Seeing the culmination of our efforts fills me with deep pride.
Persevere on this path, Your Grace.
You have triumphed brilliantly over every obstacle set in your path these past moons... It has not been easy.
Wreathed in its sovereign magic, the Tower radiates an unprecedented power today.
Alas, I find I cannot fully rejoice.
As I feared, word is spreading of our formidable expansion and it is beginning to stir unease amongst our neighbours.
As it stands, a confrontation may well loom in the growing shadow of your reign.
If only we possessed the legendary [b][color=986b3b]Golden Key[/color][/b], this threat may have been quickly swept away, but.
. I fear we must make do with our own strength.
That said, there's still time to swell our ranks while we can.
I've heard that one of Bretania's greatest warriors, whom I personally admire a great deal, retired to Southbay a few years ago. Why not contact him to secure his services?
Regardless, you must sustain your noble efforts, Your Grace.
Thus, the legend of this Kingslayer is therefore real.
Tell me about the ruler whose downfall they caused.
... What do you think their intentions are?
Hard to say... It is said this entity was responsible for the death of the former Sovereign Ermen the Wise, but its motivations remain blurred.
Ermen the Wise... the most brilliant mind to ever grace this throne.
... Without wishing disrespect to you, of course.
Ermen were respected for their intelligence and their keen sense of diplomacy... but their few detractors saw in them only a mind too cunning, even devious.
Alas, regarding the reasons for their fall... the Kingslayer's motivations remain blurred.
Was that the case for the Kingslayer?
History has not revealed much on such an occult entity, preferring to stick to a manichean reading of its actions.
A conclusion that does not satisfy me.
I like to think that, perhaps, this being only perceives the exercise of power through its darkest aspects...
... One thing is certain, Ermen deserved a far more dignified end.
From here, you may issue actions that affect the world beyond these walls.
Invite notable individuals to your court... Or send aid to villages struck by disaster, for example.
But it seems you have already sets things in motion!
I noticed the little note you attached, concerning a Knight from the neighbouring county.
You have no memory of writing such a note.
This young man seems promising. We should invite him without further delay.
A wonderful start to our Round Table.
... I'm not quite sure if there's anything available [i]right now[/i], but, well... it never hurts to check.
And if nothing else, you may always admire the map.
A fine piece of cartography, if I may say so myself.
The words of the prophecy were true.
I am Sir Arlin, guardian of this Tower's remains.
And I have waited all my life for the blessed day when someone would finally pass through these doors.
And what a surprising choice from the Gods.
. well, a choice [i]marked[/i] by fate, with all due respect.
But I see you have already donned the traditional garb that befits the crown. As custom dictates, the anonymity of this attire shall be your protection and your salvation.
You may not yet feel it in this.
Within these walls, its magic suspends all affliction from its Sovereign, and your illness shall no longer progress.
The Tower also multiplies tenfold the strength of the knights who serve its Round Table. Its power depends on the size of the kingdom it governs, and...
. our territory is limited to the county of Brizh.
But here begins the rebirth of Bretania.
. For only through the Sovereign and the might of this edifice shall we rally our neighbours under a single banner.
The further our influence spreads, the more the Tower shall awaken... and the more complete it becomes. More knights may take their place at your Table to share in its strength.
Now, pray tell me, Your Grace.
. how is it that you came to this place?
I had to flee my village because of the Empire.
I was attacked by the Empire, then my steps brought me here.
. So the Empire is currently attempting to invade Bretania?
After all these years of relative peace?
It is more than urgent than ever that we forge allies against this threat.
For if they learn that the ancient White Tower of Brizh has awakened.
. The very one that described your arrival here.
An artifact said to be capable of uniting the kingdoms, unlocking the Tower's full potential.
And who knows, perhaps curing you permanently?
It's merely a legend, but after your arrival I'm open to the wildest mysticism...
Greetings, Sir. Let's not waste any time – I'm already familiar with this place.
A-ah... and you are quite sure you already know [i]everything[/i]?.
. I mean, even regarding the [b][color=986b3b]Golden Key[/color][/b]?[font_size=18]
Years spent crafting his grand introduction speech, only to see it reduced to nothing by a single interjection on your part.
He takes the blow with dignity.
arlin_reaction_skip.prev: A-ah... and you are quite sure you already know [i]everything[/i]?.

lines: Well then... what a peculiar situation.
This man's reputation is not unknown to me.
He is said to be the eyes and ears of Bretania's criminal underworld, as well as a...sharp connoisseur who would take an interest even in equipment deemed obsolete by most.
Although I'm not particularly keen on the idea, having his services could.
Let us say the kingdom's resources could well use this kind of boost.
arlin_talk_about_rupin.prev: Well then... what a peculiar situation.

lines: Ah, Your Grace... I wished to speak with you.
I have no desire, of course, to question your decisions, but I would like to suggest the utmost caution regarding your new recruit, Sir Tarcus.
Sir Tarcus is indeed a formidable knight, but as I previously mentioned, some of his methods are harsh.
I simply fear he might try to establish a [i]certain[/i] approach to the regency, by your side...
Why demonize him like that? Give him a chance.
Perhaps such a man will open up... unexpected perspectives for us.
He fidgets from side to side with unease.
But... perhaps I am being too pessimistic?
Let us hope instead that Sir Tarcus opens up... unexpected perspectives for us.
arlin_tarcus_recruitment_reaction.prev: Ah, Your Grace... I wished to speak with you.

lines: Y-you will get to the bottom of this, Your Grace, I... I believe in you.
He tries to reassure himself, but you have never seen him so feverish. His voice trembles like an out-of-tune vibrato.
. It is terribly painful for me to endure this ordeal...
... I still struggle to realize that we must investigate our own, the very ones we are meant to protect.
And that my niece was targeted.
His words trail off into a sob.
And what a loss... what a tragic loss.
What a relief to have wrested our Knight from Victoria's grasp, Your Grace.
After some tearful delusions, he regained full lucidity shortly after his return to us.
Do you intend to reinstate him to the Round Table immediately?
What a relief to have wrested our Knight from Victoria's grasp, Your Grace.
After some tearful delusions, she regained full lucidity shortly after her return to us.
Do you intend to reinstate her to the Round Table immediately?
I need to think about it.
No. This event hurt me in an *indelible* way.
I... I'll pass along the message.
arlin_victoria_plot_charmed_knight_retur.prev: What a relief to have wrested our Knight from Victoria's grasp, Your Grace.

lines: What a strange challenge presents itself to us once again, wouldn't you say, Your Grace?
The name of that formidable warrior, Victoria, resonates far beyond our lands... it was inevitable that a Sovereign beyond her control would eventually pique her curiosity.
As I have mentioned, we must act, for it would be no surprise to see her join the ranks of those eager to witness our downfall...
I worry on what she will demand of us to join our ranks.
. But what else could you have done?
To go on a crusade against her, even with the most elite of your knights, would be nothing short of a suicide mission...
He sways uneasily from side to side.
A-anyway, now that we are seeking her favour... you must be devoted to the cause.
Do not think of deceiving her...
You acted for the best, Your Grace.
Let us hope that fate proves merciful.
Getting rid of her will be no easy feat, but... did we really have a choice?
I dare not imagine the price she would have demanded to submissively join our ranks.
You acted for the best, Your Grace.
Now... prepare yourself with the utmost care.
...And then, at that moment, all the knights of Ermen the Wise rose and...
Seated in the great library, the Drakovic heir is joyfully recounting tales of ancient Sovereigns to the little dragon curled up on his lap.
You watch them for a few moments before the tiny dragon turns its two small pupils towards you, revealing your presence.
I was narrating my favourite stories to.
You haven't given it a name yet?
I want to take my time. That's important, don't you think?
For now, it will be "cute little dragon".
The baby dragon's tail whips the air in discontent.
-he's not evil or something, you know... w-well, as long as he's eaten, I-I guess... haha.
-I want to find him a name that reflects his... inner strength. The power that shines in his eyes.
Well, when I say strong, I don't n
Many heroic stories are associated with courage. Or wisdom. Or even fear...
Even if Grandfather is going to tell me off... I
-I mean, normally, our family has a tradition of...
. of devouring the heart of a dragon so that our true power may burst forth.
. to kill such a wonderful being...
I know I should have, but.
-I'll never be as powerful as Grandpa. I
It is not physical strength that makes you a hero. You're taking care of a dragon.
I suppose my *slight* hope of making something of you was misplaced.
Be who you want to be.
The tiny dragon stretches out to its full length, feeling safe alongside Arron.
-yes. Even though I haven't done much yet... [font_size=18] actually, I was supposed to give him his first bath today, b-but he squirmed,[/font_size][font_size=16] uh, anyway...[/font_size]
The tiny dragon straightens up slightly, as if annoyed by your words.
-I'm sorry I can't meet your expectations, but...
The tiny dragon curls up on the lap of Drakovic's heir with complete trust.
I'm glad I can finally stop.
. pretending to want this path paved with destruction and a thirst for power.
arron_babydragon_affinity_3.prev: ...And then, at that moment, all the knights of Ermen the Wise rose and...

lines: -did you wish to see me, Your Highness?
I want you at my Round Table.
I wanted to recruit you, but... it's not possible yet.
No. I never want to see you again.
As your footsteps carry you to the training ground, an irritated voice interrupts the rhythm of exchanges and parries.
For goodness sake, you don't have anything other than these training dummies?!
You're mocking me! Give me someone who can take a beating if you want me to improve!
If you don't like it, I'll go elsewhere.
I am the heir to Drakovic. The most powerful of all your counties combined.
I could make short work of the other knights or any of your enemies.
Provided I can refine my techniques. How can I make progress without a moving target?!
Calm down. I won't throw soldiers to a wolf like you.
I'll find you some useless soldiers.
Become a proper knight first, then we'll talk about it.
Keep this up, and your pathetic little kingdom won't get very far...
Drakovic is worth much more than this.
I KNEW you would agree with me.
-I... I am your finest knight, Your Highness.
-I... I ate the heart of a dragon. N-No one in your Table has ever done that before. I am unique. I am perfect...
arron_dragonheart_affinity_1.prev: As your footsteps carry you to the training ground, an irritated voice interrupts the rhythm of exchanges and parries.

lines: Ah, Your Highness... you are here too.
He rolls a small glass container between his fingers, creating a soft, tinkling sound.
I was just feeling a bit peckish. Being a ruler is hungry work.
You don't know about it?... These pills build muscle in no time.
Normally, it's one per week, but one per day is even better.
His eyes look you up and down with disdain.
You are literally just sitting all day long...
I'm on a draconic... er, draconian training regime.
Red meat, supplements, eggs. Lots of exercise and some running at night. An occassional hunt of the local fauna in the area certainly helps.
I'm already a better knight... A hero that history books will praise again and again.
Are you sure this is good for your body or your mind?
Why are you loitering here, then? Get back to training. And quickly.
Do you want to become a carbon copy of your Grandfather?
I AM NO LONGER THE PITIFUL CHILD YOU ONCE KNEW.
I'm ashamed of the weakling I have been.
And I will prove it to you.
He gulps down a few mouthfuls of his drink and vanishes from the kitchen, slamming the door behind him.
The shy and anxious child is definitely no more.
I promise you'll never regret taking me under your wing.
He downs a few tablets and vanishes from the kitchen, evidently embracing this transformation he considers his [i]better[/i] self.
. Nothing to do with him! He's broken and useless. He couldn't even beat your knights.
I have no interest in being an imitation of that disappointment.
He was always too soft with me. Why do you think it took so long to reveal my full potential?
No, Your Highness. I'm becoming stronger by the day.
I'll be better than he ever was. You will see for yourself soon...
He swallows a few gulp of his drink and disappears from the kitchen.
arron_dragonheart_affinity_2.prev: Ah, Your Highness... you are here too.

lines: I want you at my Round Table.
I wanted to recruit you, but... it's not possible yet.
I never want to see you again.
I will not disappoint you, Your Highness.
You're not worthy of my power.
...You know why I'm here, Your [i]Highness[/i], don't you?
This kingdom has become absolutely pitiful. I have no idea why the old man entrusted me into your care. How he even let you beat him.
This Tower is nothing more than a circus with your clowns running around.
I return to my rightful place in Drakovic...
arron_dragonheart_leaving_roundtable.prev: ...You know why I'm here, Your [i]Highness[/i], don't you?

lines: Arron never left the Round Table to ascend to the throne of Drakovic, contrary to his grandfather's hopes.
He continued to act as a knight, and his reputation grew over the years.
He eventually became known as the "Dragon Knight" of his time.
Arron eventually left the Round Table to take on his role as count of Drakovic, to his grandfather's great pride.
His terrible fits of rage made him deeply unpopular.
And yet, the people continued to respect the strength of the House of Dragon.
Arron never left the Round Table to ascend to the throne of Drakovic, contrary to his grandfather's hopes.
The obligations tied to the title of count proved just as overwhelming, just as out of reach as those of knighthood...
He eventually withdrew, choosing a simpler life among the dragon stables of Drakovic.
arron_ending.prev: Arron never left the Round Table to ascend to the throne of Drakovic, contrary to his grandfather's hopes.

lines: Usually so withdrawn, the young Drakovic now stands before you, glowing. But that isn't even the most curious part.
Indeed, a tiny dragon flits about on the young knight's shoulder.
. well, I mean, everything's fine. H-he's nice.
I managed to calm the dragon, as you asked me to. I looked after its little one for ten days and ten nights, and finally, it...
. it asked me to look after him! To show him the world! Can you believe it?!
I t-took care of the egg and...
C-Can you be-believe it?! I'm going to take c-care of it and help it g-grow and...
[font_size=18]Breathe in. Breathe out. You can stand up for yourself, Arron. It's important...[/font_size]
P-please, Y-our Highness. I'm asking you to let me take care of him.
Of course. It seems important to you.
Out of curiosity, how many kilos of meat does a dragon eat once it reaches adulthood?
Your words surprise him for a moment, but a gentle, confident smile spreads across his lips.
I hadn't thought about that, uh... [font_size=18]I'm sorry...[/font_size]
I-I'll work hard to feed him, Your Highness.
I'm just teasing you, Sir Arron.
You're right, I need to trust myself more. That little dragon depends on me now.
Yes. I'm... I intend to fulfil this role to the very end.
Two reptilian pupils fix on you... You don't recognize the person standing before you anymore.
S-Sir Arron, what happened to you?
I did that bloody ritual that the old man kept harping on about.
[i]Eat a dragon's heart[/i], he said. [i]You shall become a man, a real one[/i], he said.
And he was right. I owe him at least that much.
I'm FINALLY what I was born to be.
You can stop sending me on dirty jobs. I need blood.
I need to prove my heroism and strength. After all, I am now the most powerful of your knights.
Calm down. You're not a hero just because you're suddenly more powerful.
Glad to see the anxious kid is no more.
What do you know about it?
I'll prove you wrong. You'll see.
I got rid of that unbearable skin.
I will not disappoint you, Your Highness.
D-did you ask to see me?
I wanted to give you this.
The new dragon heart you recovered... I was thinking... maybe this time...
It is rare to see the heir to Drakovic come out of his lair to address you in this way.
The dragon heart you recovered... I was wondering...
[font_size=18]... it's important, Arron. You can do it. Even if it's scary...[/font_size]
I... I would like to have it... if t-that's alright?
I-I mean... it's important for... I... there's a ritual to become a true dragon knight, like my Grandfather, and...
Oh... um... I understand. It's valuable...
I-if you ever find another one, let me know... please?
...All that's left is to do this bloody ritual... I hope it'll be alright...
Ah... I-I'm sorry. The dragon egg... I...
I would like to take care of it. If... if you don't mind?
Oh...um... I understand, I'm not...well...I mean...trustworthy, I suppose...
... I always wanted to look after one, rather than fight against them.
The young heir flinches before you, less dragon and more a frightened hatchling.
-I was planning to come and see you, Y
That is, if it was p
-possible and, um... if it wasn't too much trouble.
You're a knight, speak with confidence.
. I don't know if I can do it, but I'll do m
. Thank you, Your Highness.[font_size=18] I'll have already been yelled at fifty times by my great-great... ahem, excuse me.[/font_size]
-I wanted to, uh... formally introduce myself.
-I am Arron of Drakovic. Youngest heir to the great Dragon Knight, Aragon, whom you have, um.
-I have read many stories about him and the previous knights. It is hard to believe the adventures they actually lived and experienced. The deeds that made them [i]heroes[/i]...
He shifts from one foot to the other.
-realistic, I'm more of a footnote in a history book, you see.
-But rest assured, I know how to fight! What I mean is, one doesn't just improvise being a hero like that...They all were already exceptional people.
Not all heroes wear capes like your forefather.
-to be honest, I doubt it. I don't have Grandpa's stature.
-the heroes never proclaimed themselves as such, I suppose.
I'm here. Ready for your orders any time. Perhaps I would be better suited to more menial work?
. If you're having trouble with dragons, that's, um...
-thank you for listening to me, Y
. Oh, I didn't know that detail of the story...
In a remote corner of the library, you spot Drakovic's heir pouring over ancient scrolls.
Your footsteps on the cold cobblestones draw him out of his reading.
are you l-looking for something in particular?
Stories about the former knights of this Tower.
-their exploits are recounted in numerous history books or f
-fantasised about in heroic tales. I bet you've heard of them all!
Like the story of Melior the traitor, the strongest knight to have ever lived!
Or Dagon the Red, the first dragon knight who left the Empire to serve Herod! The founder of Drakovic!
And my favourite... the snail knight who served Arneb the Mad! They say he couldn't finish a quest in less than 3 cycles!
-Your Highness... [font_size=18]I've been rambling on and on...[/font_size]
B-but anyway, I was reading about the knights...
-Sovereign could get lost in their o
. hmm... it demystifies you a bit...
S-sorry! I was just reading about these knights...
-what does it mean... to you... t
. for years, I was brought up to be a [i]hero[/i].
But no matter how many times I read and reread the exploits of the knights of old, I just can't seem to grasp what it means to be one of them...
It's about finding that glimmer of hope when all seems lost.
It's having a lot of muscles.
It's the art of embellishing situations.
It's about being the right person, in the right place, at the right time.
-mean being able to push our limits or o
-I don't know if I'll ever be able to...
[font_size=18]I mean, even at our Round Table some aren't exactly...[/font_size][font_size=18] well...[/font_size]
-but I'll try to, um...build up some muscles.
heroes like the ones history tells us about don't l
-I suppose one can only shine when the stars tru
-truly align. A c-courageous person will remain forever un
-But thank you for your answer. I will contemplate further on what you've told me.
-answer isn't that simple. And that it's probably different for everyone?
-I will think on it further during my next missions. T
I'm l-leaving, Y-Your Highness. I-I don't feel like I be-belong here. I-I t-thought I would be a-able to o-overcome my...limitations but.
. there are too m-many things that...
T-thank you for t-trying. D-despite everything.
And such was the end of our story...
In an unexpected turn, the Sovereign offered their hand to the Emperor who, against all odds.
This bold move left a strong impression across the counties of the Empire.
One by one, every count rallied to the new kingdom... and not a single one was ever considered independent anymore.
The kingdom and the Empire were one; an unprecedented fact in history.
The dominion, now known as Bretanor, stretched to the four corners of the world and was recognized as one of the greatest nations history had ever known...
But could so many different peoples and cultures remain under the same yoke?
. That, for the future, seemed far less certain.
audacity_ending_cutscene.prev: And such was the end of our story...

lines: It looks like the Tower has finally awakened for good.
No more candidates in a trance screaming dubious incantations at its doors or relentlessly drumming on its walls...
To tell you the truth, I still can't quite believe it... But here we are.
The man before you looks like he'd stand frozen forever, just to prove he's [i]that[/i] loyal to you.
If you permit me, Your Grace, I would be delighted to inform you of what to expect in the coming days.
No need, I'll just go with my gut feeling.
W-well... I suppose fate knows better than me.
Your Grace's most astute instincts shall guide our way. [font_size=19]What could possibly go wrong?[/font_size]
Your new subjects are quite eager to have someone in charge again and will come to you for help and guidance on various matters.
Some of these requests may require you to take action, and the knights you've recruited at the Round Table will help you do that.
Be forewarned, though they may serve you, they may not feel inclined to carry out your every order. It would do you well to learn their preferences to avoid future headaches.
Well then, that is all for now.
Let me introduce you to your very first knight.
She is on her way and quite capable.
[font_size=18]She also happens to be my dear niece.[/font_size]
But... I take no responsibility for her punctuality, whatsoever.
Ah! I am terribly sorry, I got lost on the way here.
I am Lady Angelica of Clovermont, Your Grace.
Welcome to the Round Table, Lady Angelica.
I have a feeling you want to ask me about a cat? Permission granted.
Before you ask, no cats. But I can have your room rearranged.
But I am your only knight, Your Grace...
Yes, which objectively makes you the best. Please, continue.
I-I mean, thank you. That's great!
I mean, yes. I understand. No cats. But thank you for fixing up my room.
Whilst we have just met... I must trouble you with a request. Just a [font_size=18]small[/font_size] one, really... but I couldn't sleep a wink last night.
Do you think I could bring a cat to lighten the mood a bit?
My dear niece, you told me your request was of the utmost importance!
But it is! Just a [font_size=18]tiny[/font_size] cat? I mean, until the dusting and arranging are complete...
Something can be done for the room. But no cats.
Of course. Someone will assist you to make your room more comfortable as well.
Oh. Maybe the stables will be more comfortable instead...
I will not keep the rest of your audience waiting.
At least, I will be able to sleep, I thank you for that.
Oh! Thank you very much, Your Grace.
I will name the cat after you!
I should not keep your audience waiting and take my leave, then.
... During our annual zoological seminar, an adorable little rabbit ([i]slightly[/i] overcharged with magic) triggered an ice explosion that is currently freezing all of Avalon.
We managed to reach the rabbit with considerable help from pyromancy, but the creature has since transformed into something considerably less cute and...unapproachably terrifying.
I'll sending my best knights against this killer rabbit.
Oh. T-Thank you! I'd rather not freeze to death.
Your Grace, we need someone who isn't afraid to get wet for a good cause.
And who can swim better than you, preferably.
Rabid seaweed sunk a transport carrying a valuable artefact in the great lake surrounding Avalon.
Her gaze carries the warm patience one reserves for the blissfully uninformed.
Anyway, if you had someone willing to dip their toes in the water...
I have knights who are very skilled at finding artefacts.
There must be a way to get it back without getting wet.
Well, if they're smarter than all the witches of Avalon, then with pleasure.
avalon_grievance_lost_in_the_lake.prev: Your Grace, we need someone who isn't afraid to get wet for a good cause.

lines: Your Grace, as you know, Avalon is dotted with lakes and teeming with all kinds of mystical creatures.
Someone recently claimed to have spotted a huge creature emerge from the lake at dusk, and now there are wild speculations.

...Sea unicorn, kelpie, an ancient primordial being awakened after centuries of slumber... [font_size=18]Personally, I lean towards the "too much elderflower liqueur" theory combined with "a large branch falling in the water", but, well.[/font_size]
I have knights who are good with animals.
I have knights steeped in mysticism.
I have knights who run alcohol checks.
Oh. Glad you share my theory.
avalon_grievance_nessy.prev: Your Grace, as you know, Avalon is dotted with lakes and teeming with all kinds of mystical creatures.

lines: Your Grace...One of the ancient spirits of the forest bordering Avalon Lake has awakened.
Need some help to appease it?
You'll know then that playing with a spirit for days and nights on end is the classic method for getting it to share its power with the surrounding lands. Haha.
...So, any ideas to entertain an old forest spirit?
Our merchants will find the ideal distraction.
I can send you some bored people.
Capture pixies and force them to play with the spirit.
I suppose, for the right price, people will volunteer to suffer with anything.
The idea isn't bad, but it's a bit abusive, don't you think?
avalon_grievance_spirit_of_the_forest.prev: Your Grace...One of the ancient spirits of the forest bordering Avalon Lake has awakened.

lines: The water is murky. The once crystal-clear lake has turned into a milky sludge... impossible to see our own reflections in it.
Our scholars must have a chemical solution to counteract that.
Have you tasted it? If it's good, sell it.
Local fishermen can help you adjust the quality by adding some seaweed and fish.
We should investigate a deeper evil beyond the lake.
...It's true that I could perhaps ask my colleagues...
Thank you for volunteering [i]yourself[/i] for this.
Will we be able to choose the fish?
Investigating the lake's origins might also prove worthwhile.
Oh. I wouldn't say it's ideal for us to be distracted from our research by such [i]minor[/i] incoveniences. But if we must...
She was the centrepiece of our annual mystical creatures showcase. Elegant with a pearlescent white coat and immaculate mane... I won't even begin to describe the hysteria since her disappearance.
Our groom is kind with animals, he will be able to track her down.
I'll send out a search team right away.
Take a white horse, dye its mane and stick a fake horn on it.
...Mmm...perhaps...from a distance, without too much light...
Oh, thank you. My apologies, the people in charge forgot to place a tracking seal on her.
Oh, that charming young man who tends to your noble steeds?
I promise, I'll send him back...
yes. I suppose that's the most...
You don't really look like what I had...
The woman to your right is the spitting image of Lady Belladonna, a few years on.
There is a peculiar scent of magic lingering here.
. Ever thought to open a window?
We are representatives of Moonvale, Your Grace. Following your...
unusual management of our recent crisis, Lady Medea has designated us as your points of contact.
Though as far as I'm concerned, I still don't trust you with even the [i]slightest[/i] level of responsibility.
Her voice is soft, but her words sharp. She seems genuinely convinced that this is a perfectly polite observation.
... Understandable, given that you couldn't even manage the simple task of making your way to us.
Hecate. Finest witch and alchemist in all of Pinemaze.
what am I saying? Of all of Moonvale!
Gloria from Avalon. Of course, you are already familiar with our mystical city and the beauty of its enchanting lakes so I won't dwell on the subject.
Let us cut to the chase. To celebrate this [i]formidable[/i] alliance, our next grand Congress of Magic shall be held on your lands.
You'll no doubt prove generous with subsidies, won't you?
We have no additional budget for this.
From a business perspective, I suppose this will benefit everyone.
I can subsidise a course in humility for you, if you'd like?
Oh. I see. You didn't set aside some contingency for unexpected expenses?
It's an excellent way to raise the standards of your people.
However, we'll need to tailor our speeches to their level of knowledge.
O-oh, with pleasure! It is always good to learn from others, after all.
I'm Torfa, emissary of the volcanic isle of Popota.
The name's Cinderbeard, hailing from Tortosa Isle.
Quite the crossing to reach ya!
... Personally, I arrived on the back of a griffin.
Actually, I've been waiting for my colleague to arrive for days...
And what a sight upon landing!
I mean, it's still surprising to see a coastal town without a single palm tree on the horizon... Nothing but those hulking, shapeless grey dwellings as far as the eye can see...
... I had time to stop there on the way while waiting for you, and it's true.
... I imagine so, if you have a penchant for despair.
Originally, we mostly came 'round to shake hands.
. but seeing this dreary landscape gave us an idea!
... Why not organize a maritime twinning event between Grest and the Basalt Islands?
Exactly! You'd be showcasing our fine sandy beaches and coconut trees... and on our end, we'd celebrate, er... your local specialties?
[font_size=18]Word has it they make a mean soup in Grest...[/font_size]
I have a better idea: unlimited soup for the islanders.
Guess we shouldn't give the impression that the fish is fresher elsewhere...
... Does that mean you reject [i]our[/i] culture?
Despite our differences, here in Beaconsbury we are excellent hunters.
Whether the prey has feathers or fur.
Smaller than a mouse or taller than three men.
Nothing can stand in our way.
The problem is not the Beast itself.
Magic has never been something we're good at.
We avoid Pixies, and there aren't many other magical creatures we need to hunt.
... Well, it seems we'll have to manage on our own, after all.
They wake up with a start, a shadow looming over them that vanishes with a sinister laugh.
How awful. I'll send someone immediately.
The animals around Beaconsbury are dying.
It comes from the water that springs deep within the forest.
It could be a creature, a poisonous plant, or even...a criminal act.
But a completely mad old nobleman has barricaded himself in his mansion for several days.
In Beaconsbury, hunting without a permit is forbidden... And his permit was revoked a few months back.
We would like to improve our hunting equipment.
Clearly, their repeated failures to drive away the Beast are due to their equipment. Or perhaps because of the bad weather? An external cause, for sure.
You're the "hunting experts". Work it out yourselves.
Take this to repair your equipment and buy new stock.
Our blacksmith can take a look at your equipment.
The Hunters of Beaconsbury thank you.
beaconsbury_grievance_hunt_materials.prev: We would like to improve our hunting equipment.

lines: Do you have any good ones?
How *else* do you think we tracked down the Groveshire Beast?
But the effects are definitely there.
It's a miracle that no one was injured.
I'll send a team to assist in finding the culprit.
That's no different from usual, isn't it?
I know some very good scholars who can look into the drugs.
She glances behind her, as if to check that she is not being followed.
She seems to be wondering which is worse. Her problem or negotiating with you.
We haven't seen them in years.
She seems annoyed from needing to explain in such detail. In her right hand she clutches at a strange apple to seemingly calm her nerves.
They sow discord. Frighten the game.
Hide our knives and replace them with these silly apples. Hells.
I'll send a knight to negotiate with them.
I'll send a knight to exterminate them.
Invite the children to play with them.
She throws the apple at your feet.
Yer Grace. That little she-devil of a fighter sailed into Grest, she did, lookin' to ink a deal on our salt, aye.
Aye, first off, I be sayin' they're fishy; no salt in their butter, mind you. That don't fill me sails with faith, not one bit.
Above all, we need salt to preserve our game meat, Sir Roland. Salting other foods is a luxury.
Aye, just goes to show, we be swimmin' in treasure and don't even know it, savvy?
We need salt, but Grest is a remote village.
Just three short days from the Tower, and the same from Beaconsbury. Not much.
And the wildlife there is mostly hostile.
Ye get used to it with the tides. Giant crabs ain't such bad shipmates.
Aye, mayhaps this ain't the best trade route in the world. But we have a lovely little village. And salted butter.
The roads will be improved and made safer.
I don't interfere in this type of business.
Here's a helping hand. Grest is responsible for improving the roads, Beaconsbury for making them safe.
Ah, now we're talking. You'll be able to experience "real" butter now.
I hope you don't use that to bake your cakes.
Then our taxes will not interfere with your treasury either.
We should be able to join forces, indeed.
True. And we could teach ye the ropes of churnin' true butter.
Aye, a handful of lads be itchin' to chart new courses, 'n this here's the tide to make it happen.
And these new courses shall include Beaconsbury?
I thought your boats were only useful for fishing, but that suits me fine.
I'll tell 'em to stow some proper butter down in the hold, as a bit of lagniappe.
What could possibly be a compelling enough reason to tear [i]me[/i], the great Witch Belladonna, away from my long-awaited holiday?...
But...I must say, my curiosity is piqued.
A faceless leper managing to open a door that even the greatest mystics have failed to budge by a single inch over decades...
Oh, you know. It was *just* a matter of having a pure heart.
What a charming little fairy tale....
I heard you were the best witch in the whole kingdom.
Do you think I spent twenty years inhaling frog fumes for fun?
You're the best in the whole kingdom. I'd love to work with you.
I can craft elixirs that will enhance your knights in any discipline.
Make the quiet ones stir up the crowds.
Her voice takes on a honeyed velvety tone.
So show me this little world of yours, [i]my dear[/i], and I'll provide any potion you need for your Knights...
... Only if you pay me what I'm worth, of course.
... Before I can start, you'll have to find me a nice spot in this dusty Tower.
You certainly don't waste any time getting down to business... I must say that sharp mind of yours is rather appealing.
You have finally swept away the Kingslayer threat with a brilliance that hardly surprises me. After all, your knights were well‑equipped...
A new energy seems to course through this Tower since dawn... do you feel it?
Beyond its mere physical expansion, I mean.
I can sense its power brewing. The path you forged beyond our borders has allowed me to order new ingredients for my potions.
Do stop by to peruse my new wares.
Would other alliances bring you new ingredients?
Would I have the pleasure of watching you concoct your potions one day?
That's a very intimate question, you know?
A witch's secrets are revealed only to her most devoted disciples...
... That said, if you insist on learning a few tricks of my hand, it isn't impossible that one day I'll grant you a privileged welcome in my back‑room.
Don't keep me waiting too long...
I will do my best, [i]dear Sovereign[/i].
She lets out a little laugh.
In any case, keep weaving alliances with our neighbours, and perhaps I'll be able to reveal my most.
After all, every trade route that opens up is a boon for finding exceptional components.
Though they're not all of the finest vintage.
Thinking of the trinkets that came from Almor still gives me chills, Great Gods...
Note also that, as a native of Moonvale, I have a keen eye for anything originating from those lands. Over the years, I have become familiar with even their most obscure properties.
It would therefore be extremely beneficial for an alliance to be forged between your two counties...
... Provided you prove worthy of their good graces, of course.
It seems that you will have to face a danger far greater than anything you have encountered before, Your Grace...
I have the best witch in the kingdom on my side. What could possibly happen to me?
I do not want to scare you, Your Grace, but it's going to be tough.
Let's be honest: you have me at your side, me-the most powerful witch on these lands, far surpassing many others in Angelor.
She lets out a laugh that contrasts with her worried expression.
Do you therefore have the gift of always coaxing a smile from me even in the worst moments, my dear...?
I won't pretend to be modest: I am indeed the most powerful witch in these lands, far surpassing many others in Angelor.
despite this, I doubt our chances of success.
Despite this, I wouldn't be so confident if I were you.
The lands of Angelor are teeming with energies and mystical creatures that take root only on this soil.
And Merlin, the emperor's close advisor, is a wizard whose name transcends legend... so let us not underestimate their formidable occult powers.
... But I will do my utmost to lend you my hand, Your Grace.
belladonna_emperor_reaction.prev: It seems that you will have to face a danger far greater than anything you have encountered before, Your Grace...

lines: The witch Belladonna remained a sorceress in Brizh for some time.

Having become the Sovereign's trusted advisor, it is said that her esoteric knowledge was generously passed on in the privacy of her back room, when she was not busy studying the secrets of the Tower.
She advised the ruler while studying the secrets of the Tower.
It seems she never revealed some of her discoveries...
The witch Belladonna didn't find home in Brizh for very long.
She eventually made her way to the Empire, hoping to unlock the dark arcana that, it is said, would allow her to undo any curse.
belladonna_ending.prev: The witch Belladonna remained a sorceress in Brizh for some time.

lines: The young woman pays you no attention, too busy tidying up her table.
You watch for a few moments as her meticulous gestures unfold, choreographed like a perfectly rehearsed dance.
I am preparing for my visit to the annual seminar of the Moonvale Great Academy of Magic.
She fills a small bottle with dried sage.
This year I have the honor of being invited to chair a conference on the theme of sisterhood's undulating rituals.
Alas, no... and I fear that even if you could have traveled to attend in person, it wouldn't have been possible.
This conference will be open only to witches.
Some of our practices are meant to be passed down within the intimacy of our female circles...
But don't read that as discrimination; witches simply have an approach to the discipline that our male counterparts can never fully grasp.
After all, even as the practice spreads today.
The most skilled mages on Earth are women, right?
She delicately gathers dried raspberry leaves into a neat bouquet.
... I imagine we have a more...visceral relationship with the discipline-a kind of reactivity that isn't easily mimicked.
That explains why, historically, women have been the pioneers of these practices.
I must say it's delightful to see so many women working for you, Your Grace.
You possess, at your disposal, talents of great rarity.
... And let's admit it, all those strong‑bodied women are also pleasing to the eye.
It's a shame witches don't have that kind of physique...
I'm sure there's a spell to strengthen your muscles.
She shortens the distance between you, her gaze conspiratorial.
I'm not badly endowed under this cloak, either.
The silky curve of her thus exposed shoulder captivates your gaze like a hypnotic spell.
You'd never have guessed, would you?
But believe it or not, grinding ingredients all day at my alchemy table ends up being a real physical workout...
A spark of challenge lights her look.
Would you like a private demonstration in my back‑room?
A-ah... you should focus on preparing for your seminar instead... (Lower your eyes.)
What a lack of flair, Your Grace...
What a pity; I'm sure the experience would have been.
... But fine. Your wishes are commands.
The touch of her hand against yours brings a gentle warmth as she guides you with a decisive step toward the back‑room.
For hours, you are the privileged witness to Lady Belladonna's gestures, as her 'potion-making' ritual takes a... singularly carnal turn.
Her expert hands engage in the intimate motions of a mesmerizing dance, deep within vessels you would never have dared to dream of.
Her short breath, her every curve used with a fervor that becomes a gentle invitation to finally taste the most forbidden brew.
You struggle to catch your breath, still reverberating from all the mystical knowledge revealed to you in the intimacy of the back‑room.
. among the most instructive, wasn't it?
Feel free to come see me again, my dearest sovereign.
I have two or three more things I'd love to teach you.
She goes back to her task.
belladonna_full_romance.prev: The young woman pays you no attention, too busy tidying up her table.

lines: Well, Your Grace. I learned with horror that this renegade, this specter who calls himself the Kingslayer, came to your door...

. But I refused to acknowledge it.
You should put all your talents at my service.

It's nothing. The outcome would have always been the same.
Alas, you are right. I fear no foresight could have turned such a baleful will from its path.
In any case, I remain entirely at your disposal.
A little occult assistance will not be wasted in ridding you of this abomination.

You seem to have eased her concerns, at least for now.
belladonna_kingslayer_reaction.prev: Well, Your Grace. I learned with horror that this renegade, this specter who calls himself the Kingslayer, came to your door...

lines: I'm delighted to see you allied with the lands that raised me, my dear.

belladonna_moonvale_ally_reaction.prev: I'm delighted to see you allied with the lands that raised me, my dear.

lines: ... Your Grace, do you not find the request made by my colleagues from Moonvale strange?

belladonna_moonvale_arrival_reaction.prev: ... Your Grace, do you not find the request made by my colleagues from Moonvale strange?

lines: [i]Your Grace, I... I... it is you I speak with yes and not that creature?[/i]

[i]At first, it took the form of a dog, then of a wolf. Enough to reopen the recent and deep‑seated wounds left by the Groveshire Beast's passage.[/i]
[i]But the creature did not stop there.[/i]

[i]The creature tearing our village apart with fear and mistrust. And it seems to have no intention of stopping. There is a mounting number of people accusing people of crimes the other claims to have not committed. [/i]

belthorn_grievance_emergency.prev: [i]Your Grace, I... I... it is you I speak with yes and not that creature?[/i]

lines: [i]Ah, Your Grace. I am delighted to see you again.[/i]

Here's something to keep you going while your lands recover.
We already killed the Beast. Isn't that enough?
A small reduction in your taxes might help.
[i]Thank you. We will be able to start the fragile process of rebuilding our estate.[/i]
[i]Enough that our coffers will remain empty and unable to feed your taxes.[/i]
belthorn_grievance_help.prev: [i]Ah, Your Grace. I am delighted to see you again.[/i]

lines: Arnold sheepishly shuffles forward towards you. You have never seen him as embarrassed as he is now. And with good reason. The colour of his clothes are...

[i]Will I become like that honking man who occasionally wanders through your corridors, emitting that unpleasant odour?[/i]

Fairies, once again. Well, I reckon that to be the case.[/i]
[i]Several others think it may have been the children who were trying to help us with our work.[/i]
[i]There are some who suspect "industrial sabotage" and that it was orchestrated by Gavault.[/i]
[i]Very well, I take note of that, Your Grace. Meanwhile, we will try to confirm this was not an error on the children's part nor a plot by Gavault.[/i]
[i]Very well, I take note of that, Your Grace. Meanwhile, we will investigate both the fairies and Gavault in the meantime.[/i]
[i]Very well, I take note of that, Your Grace. Meanwhile, we will investigate both the fairies or whether this was an error on the children's part.[/i]
[i]Your Grace! YOUR GRACE! SOUND THE ALARM![/i]

Feeding on our most precious tools, our most priceless looms![/i]

[i]But our looms will still be eaten away...[/i]
[i]The money from the seminars will cover their loss I guess...[/i]
belthorn_grievance_looms.prev: [i]Your Grace! YOUR GRACE! SOUND THE ALARM![/i]

lines: [i]Your Grace. My heart is glad to see you again, but my voice is trembling.[/i]

[i]Our invaluable cotton and silk craft production has slowed. As we are still recovering from the Groveshire Beast's attacks on our livestock we are forced to spend coin on importing supplies from neighbouring counties. As our coffers dwindle, only now do we realise we cannot rely single handedly on our cotton and silk trade alone.[/i]
[i]It pains us at the thought of diverting from our craftmanship. But what else can we do?[/i]
Why not go hunting like your friends from Beaconsbury?
Tourism? Invite people from across the region to marvel at the history and craftmanship of cotton and silk.
You have your voices? Why not organise a singing competition?
[i]I must [b]strongly[/b] reject that idea. I'd rather not invite the wrath of a certain woman over there.[/i]
[i]With all due respect I must decline that idea. It would be akin to revealing all of our trade secrets.[/i]
[i]What did I hear? You can't be serious, surely...?[/i]
[i]W-wait! That's actually a good idea. Our best singers could travel to the other counties, while the rest of us work on the remaining stock and look after the animals and...[/i]

Scholars can record your voices onto small, thin discs that people can listen to again and again.
Perhaps you should go discuss this with the Belthorn people first.

[i]I will remember this when we're famous.[/i]
belthorn_grievance_sing_star.prev: [i]Your Grace. My heart is glad to see you again, but my voice is trembling.[/i]

lines: [i]Your Grace. I greet you once again, hoping to bring delight to your sweet ears.[/i]
[i]As you are well aware, our exquisite silk craftsmanship, requires a long and delightful manufacturing process. [/i]
[i]However, the clever and slightly mischievous fairies that inhabit the forest near Belthorn are currently in a... "playful mood" - shall we say.[/i]
[i][b]Benevolent[/b]? If I may ask, Your Grace, what children's stories did you read?[/i]
[i]They decided to enchant the silk threads that compose our latest creations.[/i]
[i]The enchantment in question...dissolves our thread when exposed to a gentle drizzle or even a light splash of water. All that remains is this irritating powder.[/i]
He is holding a small bag filled with as strange multicoloured dust.
[i]Some of our most important customers found themselves as naked as silkworms under the beautiful spring rain.[/i]
I'll cover the sales of your silk and find a solution to break the spell.
Explain the situation to your customers. Perhaps someone will be able to help you?
Perhaps the fairies simply wish for tunics of their own?
Let's wipe them out and use their bodies for silk.
[i]Would Your Grace really do such a thing? Your words are a sweet melody to my ears, and I am sure they resonate with the hearts of my colleagues.[/i]
[i]What a preposterous idea that emanates from--[/i]
[i]...well the thought of making such miniature robings is quite intriguing...and it likely would amuse them.[/i]
[i]Thank you for the idea, Your Grace.[/i]
He drops the bag of powder, which crashes to the floor.
[i]Admittedly, this solves our problem but this is quite barbaric.[/i]
[i]Ah, I see. You [b]hear[/b] our sweet voices, but choose not to answer our call.[/i]
belthorn_grievance_vanishing_clothes.prev: [i]Your Grace. I greet you once again, hoping to bring delight to your sweet ears.[/i]

lines: [i]Good day, Your Grace. A pleasure to see you again.[/i]

... Even if we are capable of managing on our own.
[i]Now that we are allies, some of our requests will be directed to you. Particularly those that threaten our valued craftsmanship here, in Belthorn, and--[/i]
... Beaconsbury's hunters remain your main contacts, Arnold.
[i]Beaconsbury's hunters failed to hunt down the Beast in time to save our herds, Blaine.[/i]
For lack of information on your part.
. I shall be [i]delighted[/i] to see our new [i]Sovereign[/i] at their best.
Are you questioning the orders of the Count?
[i]Thank you for humouring Blaine. Beaconsbury is fiercely proud but a victory in this hunt should convince them.[/i]
[i]I advise you to play the game a bit more with her next time.[/i]
belthorne_beaconsbury_first_grievance.prev: [i]Good day, Your Grace. A pleasure to see you again.[/i]
