lines: A new bank has opened in the town.
Unhappy with many others, a few of my merchants invested their money without checking first.
And overnight, the bank disappeared. All that remained was an empty building and a note saying that they'd really pulled the wool over our eyes.
They've probably left some clues. We'll investigate.
I'll put the scholars on the subject, they'll be able to track it down.
I'll send a knight, but the money will be kept. Tell your men to change jobs.
Ah, very good. These guys will pay up.
brizh_merchants_false_bank.prev: A new bank has opened in the town.

lines: We can't do our job with such excessive taxes being imposed on us! If you don't take action, the merchants of Brizh will be forced to close down...
I'll take care of it. Taxes shall be reduced for the Merchants.
I'm afraid this is not possible.
It's the least you can do...
brizh_merchants_grievance_less_taxes.prev: We can't do our job with such excessive taxes being imposed on us! If you don't take action, the merchants of Brizh will be forced to close

lines: The rain has been falling relentlessly for days, and our crops are submerged. Markets have come to a standstill, and our losses are piling up... We need help to stay afloat.
This isn't going to improve the Tower's cafeteria...
brizh_merchants_grievance_need_funds.prev: The rain has been falling relentlessly for days, and our crops are submerged. Markets have come to a standstill, and our losses are piling u

lines: Our local products are being crushed by competition from neighboring imports... Your policies should allow us to compete on a level playing field!
Let us reduce your taxes to preserve your profits.
Let's think about a strategy to optimize our markets.
Thanks. But I hope you'll do more than just [i]think[/i] about it...
brizh_merchants_import_policy.prev: Our local products are being crushed by competition from neighboring imports... Your policies should allow us to compete on a level playing

lines: A carriage builder has brought out a magnificent work of under the orders of a well-known nobleman. The kind of carriage that only big shots like you would go out for a ride in.
The problem is that it's design is near identical to another carriage that has been under construction for the past six months by one of his competitors.
Perhaps work with scholars to create a system of concept ownership to avoid this in the future?
Not your problem either if the copy has design flaws that lead to accidents, I suppose.
brizh_merchants_industrial_secrets.prev: A carriage builder has brought out a magnificent work of under the orders of a well-known nobleman. The kind of carriage that only big shots

lines: There's this guy, don't know what to do about him.
He sells mops. But the thin' is, not a stick with little frills at the end.
He uses hair. From dead bodies. Or from the rubbish bins of hairdressers.
In fact, people are wondering if he isn't [i]behind[/i] the corpses.
Any proof? If not, it's just a creative hobby like any other.
Arrest him on the spot and launch an investigation!
I suppose it's just another business.
The right decision, Your Grace. It was a shady business. Wouldn't do our community any good with the rumours.
brizh_merchants_mop_merchants.prev: There's this guy, don't know what to do about him.

lines: The man hands you a dozen dice. You throw them.
Yep, it's not me. Same for you... It was confiscated from a odd scholar from the Academy.
Form a partnership and sell them?
Ah... good point. I hadn't thought of that.
Tsk, I hope he hasn't shared the recipe with his lil' friends.
Never liked sugar. It's thin, it's a pain to transport, it dilutes.
But there are these two guys who have fun every weekend bakin' the supposedly best cake in the whole lands.
As a result, all these petty noblemen are doin' the same thin'. Now, stocks are empty. That's clever..
Work with farmers and scholars, find an alternative source of sugar.
The two pastry chefs will be arrested.
Too bad. If no sugar, then no sugar.
Do you really think they'll be able to get a solution out of their own pockets?
And you'll also arrest all those petty noblemen who do the same, perhaps?
Well, [i]no sugar[/i], [i]no sugar[/i]. And no money, for sure.
brizh_merchants_sweets.prev: Never liked sugar. It's thin, it's a pain to transport, it dilutes.

lines: Do somethin'. Magic, rituals, whatever, but do somethin'.
The city is full of petty thieves. They are stealin' all our stuff.
... Perhaps by charging more honest margins...?
I'm going to ask the scholars if they have a system for locating lost objects.
I'm going to hire more security guards.
... Do you even know somethin' about margins? Tsk...
How much will all this cost us?
As long as we're not payin' for it.
brizh_merchants_thieves_in_the_city.prev: Do somethin'. Magic, rituals, whatever, but do somethin'.

lines: One of those bloody noblemen is mocking us.
One of my guys sold him some magnificent works of art from all over the kingdom a few weeks ago.
The transaction went smoothly, but while transporting the money in a downpour, the bags emptied. The money vanished in an instant.
Soluble counterfeit money? Clever. It's his victory.
A scam, plain and simple. Jail him.
You'll get some of our artworks as compensation. We've got too anyway.
Are you aware of the extent of the losses?!
I hope so. They can't fool us that easily.
brizh_merchants_vanishing_coins.prev: One of those bloody noblemen is mocking us.

lines: I come on behalf of the nobles of Rozenn, Your Grace.
Let's be frank, swallowing your... prerogatives is an exercise in moral gymnastics, given your [i]"origins"[/i].
If you wish to ease tensions
. a small measure of gratitude for the role our caste has played in the country's history would soften many grudges.
Of course. I'll reduce your taxes.
There's no way I'll pamper you any further.
That is an action worthy of your station.
brizh_nobles_grievance_aristo_complaint.prev: I come on behalf of the nobles of Rozenn, Your Grace.

lines: Your Grace, a great lady has asked me to pass on this request to you.
An old relic, kept in a silver box I was forbidden to open, apparently fell during a carriage transport.
The relic supposedly broke, and word got to her that you've got a talented blacksmith in your walls who, according to her, could definitely 'restore it to its former glory'.
It would be dangerous to restore an unknown relic.
Of course! She'll take care of it.
This is a Lady from a very noble family, and I'm sure her request is not dangerous...
Perfect. She'll no doubt be delighted.
brizh_nobles_grievance_broken_relic.prev: Your Grace, a great lady has asked me to pass on this request to you.

lines: Your Grace! I've come back to see you about the broken relic that you refused to restore.
My dear lady, although disappointed, told me that the absence of her relic had caused her to leave her room.
Here are some of the chocolates she made for the occasion.
Ultimately, it's a happy ending, and I thank you for that.
brizh_nobles_grievance_broken_relic_foll.prev: Your Grace! I've come back to see you about the broken relic that you refused to restore.

lines: I heard you had news about the broken relic.
A real little masterpiece of craftsmanship.
Don't hesitate to fill me in on how it goes.
I put it back in its box, ready to use.
Here's some compensation for your work.
This relic has inspired a new creation.
The ladies of the kingdom will be delighted!
The ladies? Oh, it was a comb, wasn't it? My Lady described it as a finely wrought silver object.
Yes, yes, that's it, a comb.
E-xa-ctly. Hurry up and give it back, now.
brizh_nobles_grievance_broken_relic_foll.prev: I heard you had news about the broken relic.

lines: As the illustrious families of Brizh, with roots here stretching back to time immemorial, we believe that no one is better suited than us to judge the local criminals.
Therefore...we should have the right of life or death when serving justice to them. Let it be done without emotion.
Why not? It would save us a lot of money.
Perfect, perfect. We will have them all theatrically executed.
Not even the right to [i]small[/i] public humiliations...?
[font_size=18]Not even getting them to write an apology letter?[/font_size]
brizh_nobles_grievance_criminels_executi.prev: As the illustrious families of Brizh, with roots here stretching back to time immemorial, we believe that no one is better suited than us to

lines: Your Grace! We have a major diplomatic incident on our hands.
A fashion designer sold the [b]same[/b] dress twice. At the last ball, two young ladies ended up wearing the sames clothes.
The designer will be jailed. And a decree will be published on the uniqueness of fashion.
Why *exactly* can't a dress be reproduced several times?
Why not *mass-market* the dress? It seems to be popular.
Exactly! We need to make these people understand the value of unique creation.
You really don't understand anything either.
brizh_nobles_grievance_duplicate_colours.prev: Your Grace! We have a major diplomatic incident on our hands.

lines: Today I bring you two magnificent emeralds. They were sold by two merchants from Grest.
He hands you the two stones. One shines with a strange lustre. The other smaller glows warmly.
Both were sold at the SAME price.
... The larger gem is a counterfeit.
Wait...what? What do you mean, [i]the larger one is a counterfeit[/i]?!
You mean you don't check what you buy?
I shall have all jewellers imprisoned.
[font_size=19]That'll teach me to hire the first "expert" I come across...[/font_size]
... wait, what? What do you mean, [i]all[/i]?
brizh_nobles_grievance_false_emerald.prev: Today I bring you two magnificent emeralds. They were sold by two merchants from Grest.

lines: We are looking for an old manuscript that is reportedly in the possession of the members of the Academy.
It is a document recounting the genealogy of the greatest families of Brizh.
But these bloody scholars calling themselves the [i]'guardians and observers of history'[/i], are reluctant to hand over the artefact.
That scroll should be returned to the Nobles. Every family will each receive a piece of the parchment.
Why not share? One for you, one for them.
... I guess it's better than nothing.
Wait, what do you mean, [i]one piece per family[/i]?
brizh_nobles_grievance_family_tree.prev: We are looking for an old manuscript that is reportedly in the possession of the members of the Academy.

lines: We're working with an extraordinary tailoress from Groveshire. We were planning to organize a huge fashion show featuring her designs on the Grand Place.
Everyone will be clamouring to see her creations. Think of the local economy!
... people can't even buy a button from one of these creations.
Let's show people what they can buy instead of food!
What are you talking about? There are plenty of people who can afford such wonders.
Perfect. I'm off right now to ask the organisa...
Hang on a sec. What did you mean by [i]"instead of food"[/i]?
brizh_nobles_grievance_fashion_show.prev: We're working with an extraordinary tailoress from Groveshire. We were planning to organize a huge fashion show featuring her designs on the

lines: Would not you like to host a grand banquet here?
A pleasant moment to learn more about the history of your lands, Your Grace, if I may.
A great opportunity to meet the kingdom's leading figures.
Throw money aw...how dare you? You won't find a better opportunity to.
Perfect. I'll get in touch with an artisan for the macaroons and other sweet treats.
brizh_nobles_grievance_first_meeting.prev: Would not you like to host a grand banquet here?

lines: The Scholars of Brizh enjoy far, [i]far[/i] too many privileges. Some of their published rags border on the ridiculous.
'[i]Taxonomy of Patrimonial Accumulation in the Upper Echelons[/i]'! Can you believe it?! We need stricter oversight of their research and academic publications.
Sounds like a good read. Grab me a copy! Chop-chop!
Indeed. I'll organize a noble commission to handle this.
I'll propose a new topic for them, 'A Study of Whining Bourgeois'.
[shake]You[/shake]... as expected, your reputation precedes you!
Does he refer to your origins or perhaps a brewing reputation as a cheeky Sovereign? Who knows?
Perfect. Let's restore knowledge to its former glory.
brizh_nobles_grievance_scholars_censorsh.prev: The Scholars of Brizh enjoy far, [i]far[/i] too many privileges. Some of their published rags border on the ridiculous.

lines: Have you heard the rumours, Your Grace? Some members of the common folk in Brizh seem fascinated by the political history of Brimwood... and, apparently are inspired by it.
By that, I mean ideas of executions of nobles, revolutions, and other such little amusements.
. You should act before they start all start taking on these "inspirations".
It can't hurt to learn a little about history.
This gossip will be punished and Brimwood should stay as is.
Let's organise a debate on this political system before fearing it blindly.
Can't hurt, really? Your Grace, are you aware of the number of victims caused by these Brimwood insurgents, long ago?
May you feel the consequences of your own words...
Perfect. I'll be smiling to pass on the news.
Really? In the face of the peoples' past follies, only fear seems appropriate...
brizh_nobles_grievance_some_revolt.prev: Have you heard the rumours, Your Grace? Some members of the common folk in Brizh seem fascinated by the political history of Brimwood... and

lines: We'd like you to negotiate an agreement with the Merchants' Guild on our behalf. They are currently withholding certain essential goods...
I'm obviously talking about tea, in case you had any doubts.
I suppose they have their reasons.
It's unacceptable. What am I going to drink during my breaks?
Fund them, and they might be more generous.
You really don't understand anything about the real problems facing this kingdom.
You may not belong to a noble lineage, but at least you understand our needs.
brizh_nobles_grievance_tea_time.prev: We'd like you to negotiate an agreement with the Merchants' Guild on our behalf. They are currently withholding certain essential goods...

lines: A scion of the Brizh family was tragically killed a few days ago.
We suspect his stable boy... his blood and the murder weapon were found hidden in the hay.
But we are at a loss as to how to react... To be blunt, the young noble's conduct was quite beneath his station.
His subjects' living conditions were... harrowing.
A crime is a crime. Execute the stableboy.
Why didn't you act sooner? Let him be brought to justice, and let the other victims be compensated.
You could go easy on the stableboy during the investigation, couldn't you?
Execute everyone. The stable boy. The *noble* family. Their fortunes return to the realm.
Yes, Your Grace. I thank you for your clemency. We will take responsibility for the subjects left behind.
... but this man still has blood on his hands and...
Is he really the [i]only one[/i] with blood on his hands?
brizh_nobles_grievance_the_bloody_hunt.prev: A scion of the Brizh family was tragically killed a few days ago.

lines: A few wealthy families are getting a little bored on their Sunday afternoons... why not build a casino at the foot of the Tower?
Everyone could have a great time.
Let's instead build a facility dedicated to treating addiction and debt.
Sure. This will keep the money from sleeping.
Wh-what? Do you really want to deprive the whole world of joy?...
Perfect. I can already see the smiles on the faces of the future winners.
brizh_nobles_grievance_the_casino.prev: A few wealthy families are getting a little bored on their Sunday afternoons... why not build a casino at the foot of the Tower?

lines: During the last hunt, a dog brought back a strange piece of bone in its mouth.
And by that I mean a piece of bone [i]at least a metre[/i] long. From some creature that walked our lands a very long time ago.
Scholars now want to conduct excavations... With a ban on hunting expeditions during that time!
It's important to study the past. Find other lands for your hunts.
You're not going to stop hunting for a few bones?
Pull off both. Dogs that hunt at night *and* dig during the day.
Why not. But we'll have first dibs on the day, then.
Again this thirst for meaningless knowledge... I hope that at least you won't let them study our old bones.
Exactly! Our huntings belongs to the present. The past means very little, apart from our bloodlines.
brizh_nobles_grievance_the_hound.prev: During the last hunt, a dog brought back a strange piece of bone in its mouth.

lines: It's been two months since some of our bourgeois stopped payin' our wages, Yer Grace. They think they can do whatever they like...
They will pay three times what they owe you.
They're probably having financial troubles. I'd lower their taxes.
They'll be publicly humiliated and forced to sing Brimwoodian songs.
We'll need to jog their memory on the lyrics, eh?
brizh_people_grievance_bad_payer.prev: It's been two months since some of our bourgeois stopped payin' our wages, Yer Grace. They think they can do whatever they like...

lines: We suspect the tavern-keepers are secretly ganging up on us.
The price of drinks has gone up. And all our drinks taste like water with a little alcohol.
What if you stopped getting drunk to forget your everyday problems?
With higher taxes, you'll reduce your personal consumption.
Let's set up a specific hour where prices are slashed.
... And what if you started solvin' our problems rather than squanderin' our taxes?
Well, that would be a good start, thanks.
... I don't think ye quite understand the pro--
... Ah...of course ye do. [i]We're[/i] the problem. All right, then.
brizh_people_grievance_cut_with_water.prev: We suspect the tavern-keepers are secretly ganging up on us.

lines: Some occultists allying with the merchants are hoardin' all the flour for sale at the market.
They say it's to bless the city's ovens... But eh, we need it to eat.
The merchants involved will be fined.
These occultists will have to pay a high tax on flour.
Make your own flour. Try grinding chicken feathers, for example.
... We'll make sure to send ye some cakes, then.
brizh_people_grievance_flour_breakage.prev: Some occultists allying with the merchants are hoardin' all the flour for sale at the market.

lines: We're exhausted, Yer Grace... Might ye grant a bit more leave to yer loyal workers before our weary bodies decide to strike on their own?
One additional annual day off for you.
Six additional annual days off for you.
[font_size=18]It seems gratitude is not really yer strong suit...[/font_size]
brizh_people_grievance_more_holidays.prev: We're exhausted, Yer Grace... Might ye grant a bit more leave to yer loyal workers before our weary bodies decide to strike on their own?

lines: Some of our workers came back as pale as a sheet.
They were working at the foundry and one of the cauldrons broke and spilled over. Fortunately, nobody was too close but...
Well, try to be more careful.
I'll negotiate with the nobles to set up compensation for hard labor.
Scholars could develop an accident safety system.
... If someone dies, I hope ye'll at least come and cry over their graves.
Negotiations are goin' to be tough, but at least we can be sure that our families won't be left behind if things go wrong.
That would be nice. A lot less hassle on a daily basis. Fewer deaths, too.
brizh_people_grievance_risk_premium.prev: Some of our workers came back as pale as a sheet.

lines: Workers in our mine feel... out of sorts.
In the morning all is well. At lunchtime, the owner offers them a nice hot gruel.
In the afternoon, they're as fresh as a daisy, capable of moving heaven and earth.
And by evening they're shivering, cold, irascible...
Our best doctors are on the case.
Make them stop eating the gruel and let the owner be thrown in jail.
Do you have a sample? We could analyze it.
Yeah, yeah, better not try it, though.
Detoxed? But what's been mixed into the bloody gruel?
I don't know much about colds, but this one's weird, isn't it?
brizh_people_grievance_strange_oatmeal.prev: Workers in our mine feel... out of sorts.

lines: Some of the guys and I thought it would be nice to have a place in town where we could eat quickly.
There are lots of little stalls at the market, but there's never anythin' left at lunchtime; It's expensive, and we're already not being paid very well...
Let's open an alternative tavern serving quick but healthy meals.
Can't prepare dinner the day before?
Wage increase for workers, with part of it paid out as meal vouchers.
Good thing we asked. Better than skipping a meal every two days.
Well, not like we have the money to keep food fresh for the next day.
... At worst, we'll get sick, nothing new.
brizh_people_grievance_the_canteen.prev: Some of the guys and I thought it would be nice to have a place in town where we could eat quickly.

lines: To the north of the Tower is a small hamlet that has not seen rain for several months.
Even during the worst storms, the little hamlet remains as dry as stale bread.
The nobles say the place is cursed!
Find the source, there must be a curse.
Forget farming... start a tanning business here. Long live vitamin D.
Well, it certainly doesn't require any brain-teasing...
...just hope it's not because of some nasty beast.
It's true, those noblemen are always complaining about the bad weather. Would be their little paradise.
brizh_people_grievance_the_drought.prev: To the north of the Tower is a small hamlet that has not seen rain for several months.

lines: Have ye ever seen a shiny tree, Yer Grace?
Because one of the most beautiful fruit trees in the orchard has started to light up at night
Involve scholars to study the phenomenon.
Decorate it and hold a celebration for the light.
Tourism is booming. Let's capitalize on that.
May it be protected and designated as a national symbol.
Good, because I don't touch anything that flashes like that.
A festival? That would bring people to our place, and we could set up a little local market using the orchard for the occasion...
Um, sure anyone will be interested?
brizh_people_grievance_the_lighted_tree.prev: Have ye ever seen a shiny tree, Yer Grace?

lines: Be nice to build some kinda massive giant carriage, wouldn't you agree?
Lotsa seats, lotsa horses, come through the morning in them far-off places and haul us to work.
I'll ask the scholars and craftmens to set up this system straight away.
We could do that for the nobles. So they can cruise around in *really* long carriages.
Why not a magic transport that follows precise lines?
I can ask the merchants to reinforce your soles, if you like.
I'll be able to stop changing shoes every week.
...wasn't here to give ye one more idea so that yer noblemen can strut down our streets even more.
...magic? At our service? Ye're too good, Yer Grace.
...ye can say it if ye don't care about our living conditions.
brizh_people_grievance_transports.prev: Be nice to build some kinda massive giant carriage, wouldn't you agree?

lines: At the Wednesday market, some fella's been sellin' vegetables... with human faces.
Says it ain't his fault, but I swear one pepper had the spittin' image of my Aunt Merilda!
It's witchcraft, plain and simple, you've got to do somethin'!
I'll call for this merchant's arrest.
Just make soup. No faces in soup.
I'll buy his entire stock and consult the oracles.
Promote them as sacred relics. Let's open a museum of haunted vegetables
As ye wish, Yer Grace. We'll send a crate...
Very well, Yer Grace... I'll let the others know that you've taken an interest.
brizh_people_grievance_vegetables_face_s.prev: At the Wednesday market, some fella's been sellin' vegetables... with human faces.

lines: A thief broke into the Academy to steal compromising documents about the Tower.
A friend of mine tried to stop him but in the scuffle he was...
The culprit has already been apprehended, so...
... before we do something way too...drastic, tell us, what should we do with him?
A public's court. Let's listen to the wisdom of the people.
Why are you hesitating? Kill him.
Let's hire a private investigator. Then we can conduct a trial.
N-no, I...I wanted you to stop me having those horrible thoughts and...
...perhaps you're right. Avenging my friend is what should be done.
I understand. You're right. We need to find out why.
... I just hope that...the reason will not be...futile, or I...
The fortune-teller saw me in her crystal ball, standing before you with a grievance. I am not one to obstruct destiny.
It so happens that some members of the nobility are interfering a little too much in our work.
My colleagues would like to be granted a bit more... [i]autonomy[/i], to avoid any potentially harmful influence on our research.
Unfortunately, the nobles are keen to retain this right of oversight.
Agreed, they don't have to act as censors.
It is only fair then that the scholars should be able to oversee any actions by the nobles.
Ugh. I suppose our nobles need something to do with their days...
Oh. Not quite the help we were hoping for, but if it lets us criticize their reckless spending...
brizh_scholars_grievance_censorship.prev: The fortune-teller saw me in her crystal ball, standing before you with a grievance. I am not one to obstruct destiny.

lines: ... We got some parchments. Anonymous contracts, to be exact. We verified them, and everything checks out as authentic.
It implicates roughly twenty noble families who apparently got funding from the Empire to keep control of their lands and...engage in some pretty shady activities.
They and their families will be executed immediately.
Burn these papers. They never existed. I'll deal with the relevant families directly.
Everyone on this list will be jailed.
Let's arrest everyone; everyone will get their day in court.
brizh_scholars_grievance_confidential_pa.prev: ... We got some parchments. Anonymous contracts, to be exact. We verified them, and everything checks out as authentic.

lines: Lost in a card game call 'Sovereign' or 'Scum'... I don't quite remember.
So here I am, bringing you a new issue.
Same thesis got submitted twice. Identical. Each scholar's got their own dated, handwritten notes. We can't figure out who actually did the work and who copied who.
Collect their possessions and fire them both.
Keep a closer eye on them until you find out who did what.
Lock them up and have them rewrite their theses without their notes.
Easier to make that kind of decision when you don't know the people, I suppose.
Let's hope this little game doesn't go on for months.
Oh, I'm curious to see that. A bit barbaric, but effective.
brizh_scholars_grievance_copy_cats.prev: Lost in a card game call 'Sovereign' or 'Scum'... I don't quite remember.

lines: Uh... one of my colleagues basically asked me to ask you if we could, like, ugh... mix two creatures' essence together to make a third one.
To be honest, it's a total gray area in our practices, and we generally consider this procedure banned for, well, a ton of reasons...
[font_size=19]Maybe because some shady guy once tried to do it to his kid and his dog...[/font_size]
It's out of the question. That's abuse.
That sounds extremely interesting. I'll vouch for this, provided the results are shared.
Do it on microorganisms that don't feel pain.
Thank goodness. I'll pass on the message.
I'll...pass the message on. [font_size=19]Even the Sovereign is this crazy.[/font_size]
brizh_scholars_grievance_creating_chimer.prev: Uh... one of my colleagues basically asked me to ask you if we could, like, ugh... mix two creatures' essence together to make a third one.

lines: Ughh... we played a game to see who could finish a thesis on the worst imposed subject in the shortest time. I lost, so it's my turn to pass on the message today.
Since your arrival, the Academy has reopened, so we need a dedicated librarian.
Someone who could organise everything in the main library for us. To stop spending hours looking for a lost book on top of a bookshelf...
Take it in turns if you can't do otherwise. Or be more organised.
Here's some money to help you recruit someone.
Play a game to decide who should take the seat.
... by the Hundred Scrolls...knew it would be a waste of time.
Oh. So we need to find someone now. Thank you, Your Grace.
[font_size=19]And try to tidy up...things...in the Academy.[/font_size]
[font_size=19]Ugh... I shouldn't have mentioned our decision-making process.[/font_size]
brizh_scholars_grievance_first_meeting.prev: Ughh... we played a game to see who could finish a thesis on the worst imposed subject in the shortest time. I lost, so it's my turn to pass

lines: I dreamed that I was supposed to bring you this grievance. So here I am.
We believe knowledge should be accessible to all.
. which is far from the case in Brizh. Why not adopt educational policies so our work doesn't remain locked away for a privileged few?
That certainly seems like a priority.
No. An educated peasant is a dangerous peasant.
Oh, do you think so? We'll look into it.
brizh_scholars_grievance_knowledge_for_e.prev: I dreamed that I was supposed to bring you this grievance. So here I am.

lines: I was looking for the archives hall in the Tower, but I got lost. So now I might as well speak what's on my mind.
Our study conditions at the academies of Brizh are, to say the least... exhausting. We wouldn't say no to a little financial help for education and research.
I take this matter very seriously. For now, take this.
Oh, really? We'll look into it.
brizh_scholars_grievance_more_funds.prev: I was looking for the archives hall in the Tower, but I got lost. So now I might as well speak what's on my mind.

lines: It's the Apocalypse. The end of the world. We're lost!
There's no more paper. Absolutely nothing left to write on. Prices of the few remaining scrolls are exploding...
The tanned skin of annoying scholars would make a good substitute, wouldn't it?
I'll try to discuss this with the Merchants' Guild.
You could save paper by stopping writing useless hundred-page theses.

lines: You recognise the silent young guard who previously stood beside the Count of Enberg.

It is a line of protectors, whose origins date back to the creation of the Empire.
Its members, who often serve noble representatives or earls, are all bound by a vow of absolute silence.
I don't know how you're going to be able to commu...

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]I had been serving Yohav, Count of Enberg, until recently.[/font][/font_size]"
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]Alas, I am now without a job, since you defeated the demon who was spreading terror in Enberg.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]I was greatly impressed by your methods during my recent visit to your region alongside Sir Yohav.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]Alas, my role consisted mainly of protecting him from the demon that you had the prowess to chase away.[/font][/font_size]"
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]I am not here to reproach you.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]Your determination to track down this creature has earned my respect.[/font][/font_size]"
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]In the past, the Virgo Guard, of which I am a member, served rulers such as yourself.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]My only wish now is to offer you my sword.[/font][/font_size]"

Sir Gwendan of Villador, the best knight in all the land.

It's okay if you want to applause or to faint.

Do not worry, with me at your Round Table, your little realm will very soon shine in glory.

I am afraid that you shine too much for this SHACK, Sir.
I'm already lighting this place up.

I'll come back in a few days.
candidature_gwendan.prev: I've heard you're in need of great heroes, so here I am.

lines: ... It's a pleasure to see you again, Your Grace.

... But one that has opened my eyes in many ways.

... That is, if you might grant me the honour of a second chance, Your Grace.
Welcome back to the Round Table, (reasonably) shiny young Sir.
A second chance, why not? But...not now.
No second chances for you. Reforge your memories elsewhere.
Forgiveness is not a trivial matter.
candidature_gwendan_the_humble.prev: ... It's a pleasure to see you again, Your Grace.

lines: For everything, really. Well, especially for your knights who agreed to my somewhat... strange requests.
Given everything that happened with my father, I was a bit

. Please make me a knight of your Round Table.

. have shiny armour and a helmet that doesn't scratch. And a horse, if possible. But above all, work with you.

. It appears you are the Chief Executive Officer around here, am I correct?
. In that case, would you happen to have a time slot to direct me toward your superior?

As for my strengths, I would say that I am... dynamic, versatile, and always proactive.

. I am a bit too much of a perfectionist, too passionate, and, erm

[font_size=18]No more water-soaked kibble from the Tower cooks...[/font_size]
[shake rate=20.0 level=5 connected=1][font_size=18]No more innocent victims.
no more chickens being eaten alive in their henhouse...[/font_size]
And now, I wish to spend that freedom.
Your diet seems rather... unique, to say the least.
Who are you, anyway? Is this... flirting?
My name is Rufus, Your Majesty.
But I was once known as the [i]'fearsome Beast'[/i] of Groveshire.
The one you spared, in your infinite mercy...
... Then chose to deliver, through the powerful arcanas of your Witch.

I'm more radiant than [wave amp=20.0 freq=5.0 connected=1]ever[/wave]...
my whole body, if you so wish.

On my knees if I must.

This creature is in fact the [i]terrifying[/i] "Beast" that had been reported in the Groveshire Woods. It was brought back yesterday.

Forge him some mighty puppy armour. Make sure we leave a hole for his tail.

lines: ... Greetings, strange Sovereign who rules over these lands.

... While wearing my blacksmith's clothes...which stink of sweat and molten metal... uh, maybe forget about it...

It's proof of your hard work.

Gently taking her hand, you share a few steps in the silence of the room.

A delighted, playful smile appears on her lips.

Gently taking her hand, you share a few steps in the silence of the room.
You could almost hear an orchestra playing a soft melody to the rhythm of your heartbeats.
You're a very good dancer, Your Grace...
She treasures your hand in hers before gently pulling you closer, leading you in her wake through the silent meanders of this strange Tower over which you reign.
... in order to share, [i]without a shadow of a doubt[/i], fascinating stories about modern metallurgy.
Ahaha, I understand, you might fall into a trap where I talk to you on hours about artefacts and metallurgy.
Gently taking her hand, you share a few steps in the silence of the room.
That was so much fun! I've been dreaming about this for ages...
I'm heading back to my quarters. Feel free to ask me for a dance from time to time, if it helps take your mind off things.
... Thank you for everything. For welcoming me here, and... for accepting me just as I am.
Have a pleasant day, Your Grace!
carina_full_romance.prev: Oh, Your Grace. It's rare for us to meet outside the forge.

Impossible for the moment, but I'll do my best.
I'll start a war for this relic.

carina_meeting_the_emperor_reaction.prev: Wow... what a presence, that Emperor. Do you think you could ask him to lend me his sword?

lines: I never thought [wave]such[/wave] an act could be committed within these walls...
And that... my sister could be... the target of such... barbarity.
When you find the culprit...I'll smash their skull in with this hammer.

This package is eagerly awaited, and our relations with the ruling family depend on it.
A knight will deliver the package by boat from Grest.
A knight will deliver the parcel by road to Basalt.

. The reality is, it that is does not sit on your side.

[i]Lady Cluckita the Third[/i] is a genuine national treasure. This egg is her tiny genetic heir, and it now faces the threat of being turned into a cheese omelette.

lines: ... Is that a code name for 'cheese shortage'?
No, but I fear that is what lies ahead for us.
Chavignol's sheepfold has [i]literally[/i] gone up in flames.
A fire broke out last night.
A sweet smell of grilled cheese tickles your nostrils.
... If you want to intervene before the fire spreads through the whole village, it would save us a few agonizing deaths.
There's a problem of mouldy milk in Chavignol.
... Isn't cheese, at its core, just mouldy milk?
Cheese is the result of controlled bacterial coagulation, meaning bacteria are introduced to milk to methodically separate its layers.
Quite so, Your Grace. It is a meticulous process designed to elevate the texture and taste of milk. Hardly comparable to undesirable mold on a block of cheddar.
Yes, it's sad, but I think you're being a little dramatic.
Anyway, someone clearly had a bit of fun by casting a spell on our cellars.
Every piece of cheese that comes out tastes specifically like cold ash.
I know because I've eaten it before.
A lil' bit of magical help wouldn't go amiss.
We'll just build you brand new, clean cellars instead.
I'm certain there's an audience for ash-flavored cheese. Go market it.
I was nudged into coming to you, but personally, I find this experimental cheese pretty tasty.

Let's launch an awareness campaign to encourage people to accept their rodent neighbours.

I'm going to recruit scholars for a magical milk extraction.

... You really want to eat goats bursting with milk?
We're genuinely talking about a [i]large[/i] volume of milk contained in these goats.
Now that you've cleaned up that whole mess in Gavault, we'll be seeing much more of each other.

She takes something out of her pocket.
Fancy a slice of my cheese?

"[i]Go on, buddy, take a bite of the pocket cheese.[/i]"

... If you liked it, I have plenty more in my pocket.
She returns the cheese to her pocket.
. Not very concerned with building any form of relationship, are you?
This Tower is certainly well-stocked, Your Grace...
Are you intending to lead into another metaphor?
The various rooms are cleverly thought out and arranged. A true little architectural gem.
One could almost believe this place is actually inhabited...
(I feel an almost carnal tenderness for the place you call the 'Kitchens'.)
(I've spent a great deal of time lounging in that green area you have curiously named the 'Gardens'.)
Without a doubt, that famous room full of books called the 'Library'.)
(The vibrations of that room... This 'Itendancy' possesses a breathtaking administrative purity.)
I've already spent hours there, pouring over tales about the greatest predecessor to this throne, the former ruler Arneb the Audacious!

I didn't know Arneb well. Who were they?
A stand-up goof, and very sexy to boot.
He reigned right after Candid the Kind's death
For example, I learned that good old Arneb once had the idea of knighting a legion of hares as Knights of the Round Table.
They all fought each other in bloody battles, a veritable historical fresco!
One of them, however, survived to become a mythical creature haunting the lands of Brizh.
Another day, Arneb wanted to replace the Round Table, the [i]very one[/i] around which his knights gathered, with a huge wheel of cheese!
Alas, the wheel was far too

The safety of our workers is more important than a pretty bridge.
clovermont_grievance_tunnel_or_bridge.prev: To meet growing demand for grain, our merchants are shipping heavy carts that our bridges can't regularly support

lines: Yesterday's storm in Clovermont turned a meadow into a lake. Now the poor farmers' sheep are standing in the water, all wrinkled up.
I'll send the army to drain the field.
I'll buy your sheep. I need some dinner.
Am I responsible for the weather now?
Let the sheep drown. I'll fine the farmers for negligence.
... We'll just have to teach the sheep to swim I guess...
clovermont_grievance_underwater_sheep.prev: Yesterday's storm in Clovermont turned a meadow into a lake. Now the poor farmers' sheep are standing in the water, all wrinkled up.

lines: Your Grace! As you know, we hold the great wyvern hunt every year in Clovermont to keep the creatures in check.

But this year, [font_size=18]uh[/font_size], well, there are far too many. We've found them perched on rooftops, hiding in attics... Some have even stolen hams from the market. We're not enough to handle it.
Let's protect our hams.  Knights will fend off the wyverns.
clovermont_grievance_wyvern_hunting.prev: Your Grace! As you know, we hold the great wyvern hunt every year in Clovermont to keep the creatures in check.

lines: Lady Angelica gently strokes the feathers of Columbus, who coos under her fingers.
Oh, I adore animals, Sir Ari, but I've never had the opportunity to see such a cute and round griffin before.
And he's the world's most beautiful boy!
You'll have to come up into the clouds with us one of these days!
You'll see, the lands of Brizh look so soft from up there...
conversation_angelica_ari.prev: Lady Angelica gently strokes the feathers of Columbus, who coos under her fingers.

lines: -thank you f-for all your good advice, Lady Angelica
And take care of yourself - get plenty of rest before each departure, okay? It's really important.
-I... Are you sure? My grandfather always told me it left him groggy before a battle...
Mmm...do what works best for you,
The other knights mostly ignore me, so...
thank you so much for spending time with me, Lady Angelica.
I'm far from perfect, but if you need help, tell me.
We've all been in your shoes, after all.
So, you were knighted just because you're the niece of the Sovereign's right-hand man...?
...Like, you got a birthright advantage to get here, without even having to prove yourself?
. I suppose you could put it that way...
But I really wanted to be a knight more than anything in the world and...
Just because we got a boost doesn't mean we don't have the teeth for it!
[shake][font_size=18]We're gonna stick together and show them all, okay?![/font_size][/shake]
The echo of their shared laughter carries through the entire hallway.
conversation_angelica_brunhilda.prev: So, you were knighted just because you're the niece of the Sovereign's right-hand man...?

lines: And don't forget to clean your armour after each quest.
You've been saying the same thing for twenty years...
Though it really means a lot to me that you're still looking after Elioth and me, after all these years.
... You know... just because I chose a different path doesn't mean you stopped being my little sister.
...  I'm really proud to see you living your dream now, to be honest.
conversation_angelica_carina.prev: And don't forget to clean your armour after each quest.

lines: ...Maybe you should try squeezing some rock salt between your hands?
Uncle Arlin used to give me a crystal when I was little, so it could soak up my nasty nightmares.
She leans her ear against her sword as though listening attentively.
A-and anyway, my nights are usually like drifting on little clouds.
I have an extremely, [i]extremely[/i] peaceful temperament, y-you know.
Her clenched hand tightens its grip on her sword.
conversation_angelica_edith_before_posse.prev: ...Maybe you should try squeezing some rock salt between your hands?

lines: I am in top form, Angela.
It is a pleasure to be here with you.
My heart overflows with a perfectly measured gladness.
Each mechanical word emerging from her disembodied mouth sends a fresh shiver through Angelica's spine.
Furthermore, your heart rate is fascinatingly steady today.
She backs away with a frightened squeak.
I heard that you had to travel for a very long time without ever having a home, too...
She contemplates his wounds with silent compassion.
I find it hard to imagine how anyone can face so many winters that way
. it takes a kind of courage I don't have, I suppose.
You do not see it yet, but your heart shines in the dark, Lady Angelica.
...It's a light capable of guiding an entire kingdom to a greater destiny.
O-oh, do you really think so?
. I hope that one day, I'll prove myself worthy of what you see in me, Sir.
conversation_angelica_epicrates.prev: I heard that you had to travel for a very long time without ever having a home, too...

lines: ... Y-you aren't going to eat me, are you?
I heard the servants talking about you.
They describe you as "a danger to all the women of Brizh."
And so my scandalous reputation precedes me...
Fear not, my Lady, I would never dream of laying a hand on you.
He seizes her hand to kiss it theatrically.
Your fingers are on mine, Sir.
conversation_angelica_gideon.prev: ... Y-you aren't going to eat me, are you?

lines: We could attempt some sort of acrobatic display to crush the enemy's morale during our next mission. What do you think, Sir?
A frantic bit of footwork, a voluptuous sway of the hips, and [i]boom[/i]!
I launch you into the air like a majestic champagne cork!
Before executing three perilous somersaults and landing elegantly right on top of our opponents!
And we would finish with a sparkling victory pose. Arms to the heavens, chin held high, and knees bent at a forty-five-degree angle.
That'll certainly impress them all, Sir.
conversation_angelica_goberto.prev: We could attempt some sort of acrobatic display to crush the enemy's morale during our next mission. What do you think, Sir?

lines: After all, at least one [i]real[/i] knight here must be worthy of the royal prestige expected at this rickety table we call home.
A noble hero in shining armour!
A loyal and resplendent man, illuminating every grimy cobblestone with his delicate footsteps.
Sometimes, the brilliance of it even gives me a bit of a headache.
A visual symphony, a living poem written with the ink of heroism upon the parchment of courage!
Indeed. Thank you for being such a worthy hero among us.
Are you just going to mindlessly agree with me every single time?!
conversation_angelica_gwendan.prev: After all, at least one [i]real[/i] knight here must be worthy of the royal prestige expected at this rickety table we call home.

lines: -I don't think chaining that many training sessions back to back is ver--
Since when do you get a say in what I do?
I just wanted to help you...?
W-what are you going to do with the remains of that poor little rabbit, Sir?
Rabbits are plentiful. Hunting them poses little risk to the forest's balance, unlike a doe or a deer. And far more nutritious than any strange mystical creature.
. I understand, even though I feel sad for this little fur ball.
. stewed, with mustard and a few baby turnips...
conversation_angelica_silgur.prev: W-what are you going to do with the remains of that poor little rabbit, Sir?

lines: How did you do it, Lady Victoria? How did you become the greatest knight in the entire kingdom?
Simple. You don't hesitate to snap the neck of every ridiculous inconvenience that stands in your way...
...Like little chicks fallen from the nest who get a bit too curious for their own good.
You mean you have to "break out of your shell" to grow, right?
... I can give you a live demonstration if you wish.
conversation_angelica_victoria.prev: How did you do it, Lady Victoria? How did you become the greatest knight in the entire kingdom?

lines: A ball shoots across the entire length of the hall.
The beast launches itself in turn and vanishes down a corridor, hot on the ball's heels.
A flood of clanging metal from the corridor.
some of which rolls to a stop at Angelica's feet.
. A-ah... Uncle Arlin's armour exhibition was in that hallway...
conversation_angelica_wolf.prev: A ball shoots across the entire length of the hall.

lines: HAHAHAHA! En garde, you cheeky young girl!
no, I-I...I just wanted to know how you became so...
Not that we'd fight each other.
What? But my dear, how can you learn if we don't cross swords?
conversation_angelica_zolta.prev: HAHAHAHA! En garde, you cheeky young girl!

lines: See? This is where the brush needs to go.
Get right in between the feathers, where it's itchy.
Sir Ari is clearly in the middle of grooming Columbus, who is letting out soft, rhythmic coos.
Rowan is frozen with the brush, looking utterly stranded in that shifting sea of feathers.
Don't be shy now. He only bites if he senses hesitation.
Or if he mistakes you for a big field mouse.
The griffin snaps its beak within two inches of Rowan's nose, clearly insisting on more pressure to his lower back.
conversation_ari_rowan.prev: See? This is where the brush needs to go.

lines: Ari, nestled on Columbus's back, skims the ground while the wolf gallops alongside them in an endless game.
The griffin spreads its talons, swiftly seizing the wolf in its claws and lifting it off the ground.
Spellbound, you watch the flying wolf swim breaststroke laps in mid-air.
Cries of shock drift in from the walkways flanking the gardens.
Another day within the Tower walls.
conversation_ari_wolf.prev: Ari, nestled on Columbus's back, skims the ground while the wolf gallops alongside them in an endless game.

lines: The witch fixes a piercing gaze on the creature perched on the Dacovik heir's shoulder.
This dragon is under MY protection, and I won't let you lay a finger on a single one of his scales!
But I certainly hope so, my dear. I'm delighted to see this little egg has finally [i]taken flight[/i].
I'm from Moonvale. The dragon who laid that egg is one of the most powerful creatures in the entire region.
To think those fools actually decided to steal her baby...
glad to see he's in good hands. You two make quite the pair.
you see something through this helmet?
Of course! Though [i]seeing[/i] does tend to be somewhat optional during a duel.
What truly matters is [i]feeling[/i]. The fire in our hearts. The spirit of our lands. The breath of those we fight for.[font_size=18] As long as they've brushed their teeth, of course.[/font_size]
is that the heroic wisdom of Almor?
... still, it can't be easy to fight without seeing a thing.
It was a duel to the death. Him, eight feet tall, built like an Angelorian wardrobe.
Armed with a sword twice the size of mine.
We locked eyes, not a word.
The crowd, wild up until that moment, went silent all at once. The tension wa...
-what did you do?! Did you get away?! U
Well, I wouldn't be here to tell the tale otherwise.
So I was saying, "The tension was suffocating", do keep up.
He looked at me. I looked at him, and...
[i]You looked at each other. They looked at each oth--[/i]
You'll [font_size=40]never[/font_size] hear the end of this story!
-but you told me to keep up! W-wait, I want to know how you survived!...
conversation_arron_gwendan.prev: It was a duel to the death. Him, eight feet tall, built like an Angelorian wardrobe.

lines: perfectly at peace with the idea of obeying without question, Sir.
Oh, I do have them, questions.
But in Our Majesty presence... they simply vanish.
One must always present their very best self before Our Majesty!
what if your opinions and Our Majesty's were to.
My desires are Our Majesty's desires!
...  That is what it means to be a knight.
ah... so I simply have to...cease to exist as a person.
You're nothing like your ancestor, kid. Go train instead of hanging around here.
I know we're not very alike, but...
-am I really supposed to be like that to become a proud knight? Merciless and... remorseless?
... To think we share the same bloodline...
I pray to all the Gods that my own son will never sink into such mediocrity.
The beast slowly pads toward the boy and settles down before him.
He reaches out with a trembling hand, his fingers disappearing into the beast's thick fur.
-I expected your fur to be dry and thick, but it's really soft.
Ahaha, you're like a big stuffed plush.
-BUT you're still an excellent knight! [font_size=18]Well, feel free to stop by if you ever need your fur brushed.[/font_size]
Chester performs a well-rehearsed trick and makes an apple appear behind Brunhilda's ear.
She wipes the tears of laughter away from the corners of her eyes.
And why are you the one who inherited the old lady's gorgeous curly hair?
...Perhaps there are similar mysteries surrounding the origins of your own birth?
[font_size=18]...Mind you, who knows who the old hag has been messing around with...[/font_size]
Keep your distance, I know your tricks.
I've heard all about you, Gideon the '[i]Heartbreaker[/i]'.
Just so you know, your little tortured poet vibe with the silky hair? It's not working on me at all.
Fear not. That tumultuous past is far behind me.
From now on, my heart aspires for nothing more than simple camaraderie, Princess.
So, at the absolute peak of our relationship, the most you'll ever be is a friend!!
Or like a brother to me, okay?!
You are officially banned from my list of suitors!!
The '[i]Spells and Potions[/i]' series? Forget it, it's a total waste of time.
The author is seriously out to lunch, like, totally clueless.
There's this badly explained ritual in book two, I almost leveled my room with it...
[font_size=18]I guess I'll just have to cancel my order for the complete, leather-bound edition...[/font_size]
... I have a few best-sellers I can recommend instead, if you want.
W-why not, if it saves us from a workplace accident.
conversation_brunhilda_oliver.prev: The '[i]Spells and Potions[/i]' series? Forget it, it's a total waste of time.

lines: I heard that you were the big loser in the Almor Tournament.
Getting knocked out by the first dimwit that comes along is a respectable performance.
Ah, if only Our Grace didn't wish to hold onto me so tightly unlike that other oyster they packed off to the throne.
You only believe what you see, is that it?...
[font_size=32][shake][b]I'll become a Count for you, Childeric!![/b][/shake][/font_size]
(Next time, send me to reign in Almor, Your Grace.)
conversation_childeric_chester.prev: I heard that you were the big loser in the Almor Tournament.

lines: And keep your ideas to yourself!
I have a feeling you might find the reflection of your own misgivings in my writings, my friend.
I am not your friend at all!!
... May you lower your walls, and one day understand that we are much more alike than you think, comrade.
... Except for the minor detail that you seem to be toiling through much more anxiety than I, for sure.
In the flesh beneath the armour, man!
And what kind of character do I have the honour of meeting?
... Doesn't ring a bell at all, pal.
... [font_size=18]We shared the same school bench for seven years...[/font_size]
Well, you should've picked a name that was a bit less generic, dude!
Hey, lass, you couldn't help me sew this up, could ya?
My fingers are too fat for these blasted needles.
His cape is cut at the collar. A blade seems to have grazed him closely.
you should take better care of yourself.
If you keep going like this...
What, I'm gonna kick the bucket?
A man's gotta pass on sooner or later, lass. It's no tragedy, eh?
Duh, no no, the time'll come, but in the meantime, I'm a knight just like I always dreamed.
Even if it took me eighty years, blimey, I did it, and that's the only thing that matters!
. a huge achievement just to have made it this far, despite everything.
With a bit of luck, talent, and good comrades, maybe you'll make a finer carcass than mine, who knows?
conversation_daguez_angelica.prev: Hey, lass, you couldn't help me sew this up, could ya?

lines: I was sceptical when you asked me to refurbish this old sword...
[font_size=18].... especially since it weighs a ton, luckily I practise every day.[/font_size]
... But all things considered, you manage quite well with it!
Well, 'lady, that's a fine job. My lil' spade looks ridiculous next to it.
I could perhaps make you a fastening? Something to keep it on your back, like...
Yes, I believe I've seen a knight use something of the sort--
Oh, 'too complicated. I'd rather carry it at arm's length. Can you imagine having to twirl that thing around to slip it onto your back? Could dislocate a shoulder doin' that, 'telling you.
Haha, yes, maybe. Either way, feel free to stop by if you'd like me to take care of that rust on it.
No, hehehe, 'fine to let age speak too.
conversation_daguez_carina.prev: I was sceptical when you asked me to refurbish this old sword...

lines: There's only room for one of us here.
[shake rate=6]My placement here is already approved.[/shake]
Our Grace prefers my composition to yours.[/shake]
Your vessel isn't even equipped with pores.
. I would never permit myself to steal meat without authorisation.
. that I am preferred over you.[/shake]
The opportunity to tame the flesh is only granted to the finest among us.
And the application of proper manners.[/shake]
conversation_dulahan_edith_possessed.prev: There's only room for one of us here.

lines: So that was the cause of the unpleasant smell lingering within these walls...
Being a demon does not exempt you from scrubbing your vessel, filthy vermin.
with the aura of a demon.[/shake]
I could tear you apart just for fun, you poor thing.
... But fear me not, I'm won't [i]eat[/i] you too.
Your scent is far too foul for my palate.
You have no business within these walls, you vile creature.
Dare only to answer the monstrous instincts to which you are a slave.
and you shall perish by my own hands.
Dulahan's... gaze (?) remains fixed on Epicrates' sulfur-colored eye.
The armour curls up and shrinks like a hunted animal cowering in the dark.
conversation_epicrates_dulahan.prev: You have no business within these walls, you vile creature.

lines: Dark powers accompany you, strange creature.
. I feel their icy fingers coiling around your will.
Succumb but once to those voices whispering for your attention, and.
She clutches her sword to her chest with the awkwardness of a frightened child clutching their doll.
conversation_epicrates_edith_before_poss.prev: Dark powers accompany you, strange creature.

lines: Thus, the terrible occult powers have accomplished their evil work.
How absurd... you would parade with my kin's body parts attached to your face...
You may fool the Sovereign, but I do not sympathize with your kind.
Your appeals with human emotions are lost on me.
I needed to share an urgent matter with you.
Its yellow pupil stares at you, undisturbed.
Do not delude yourself, old fool.
As long as I am within these walls, I will pour all my rage into muzzling your every scheme.
... I have naught to fear from a man who knows no law but only savagery.
Your presence here is but a hiccup in history. A momentary lapse.
I shall cherish every moment that shall see you disappear until you're completely forgotten .
I'm afraid you will be long gone before then.
conversation_epicrates_tarcus.prev: Do not delude yourself, old fool.

lines: You were far more vigorous in your youth, Gideon.
What happened to the young prodigy I trained?
I may have grown a bit rusty, it's true.
Let's say my recent years have been.
I haven't been able to maintain your teachings as I would have liked.
Oh, "cluttered," I don't doubt it for a second.
I've heard of your other recent [i]feats[/i].
flexibility that have nothing to do with fencing, alas.
... Don't worry, my Lady, I am determined to do you honour. I'll resume training day and night to catch up to your level.
Well, don't dream too much either.
conversation_gideon_alwena.prev: You were far more vigorous in your youth, Gideon.

lines: Ah, what a tragedy, alas... to possess such divine assets yet be utterly incapable of granting them the honour they deserve...
A rosemary infusion with a dash of my lavender decoction, followed by a vinegar rinse... and your mane would recover its former glory.
Why polish the filaments growing upon my vessel?
I fail to see the point.
You would simply be much more pleasant to look at, Sir.
That means you want to possess me, doesn't it?
conversation_gideon_dulahan_human.prev: Ah, what a tragedy, alas... to possess such divine assets yet be utterly incapable of granting them the honour they deserve...

lines: It seems like every step we take in the mist of this castle brings us a little closer to the unknown.
I didn't catch a single word, mate.
There's no mystery. We go out, hit things with sharp metal...
... and then, [i]boom[/i], cold beer, sore arms, maybe a missing toe, end of the story.
The greatest mysteries lie dormant in the mundane.
... I'm going to give you a real mystery, what are we having for dinner tonight, dude?
conversation_gideon_goberto.prev: It seems like every step we take in the mist of this castle brings us a little closer to the unknown.

lines: ... I thought I'd finally rid myself of your shadow after our last duel, but no.
Apparently, our Sovereign has decided that any stray dog deserves a place at court...
I heard your dear aunt had become an emissary, and I simply couldn't resist the urge to answer her sweet requests.
She is always so generous with me.
. I hope Our Grace sends me to settle a few "matters" over in Villador soon.
Does your lack of lineage weigh on you, you pampered pet?
My family is no refuge for orphans of your kind!
Ahh, [i]Gwendoo[/i], if only you kept that same energy for our one-on-one duels... I really wonder why you hide it.
Your aunt, at least, never lacks for fire.
conversation_gideon_gwendan.prev: ... I thought I'd finally rid myself of your shadow after our last duel, but no.

lines: So, the one and only Gwendan has finally lost his insufferable glow?
...I'll admit modesty wasn't exactly my strong suit during all those years we spent fighting.
It was quite to your credit.
I finally admit it. Few men have managed to make my blade tremble as you did.
... Even if, much to your ego's chagrin, it was never enough to actually beat me.
Believe it or not, I've finally found the strength I was only pretending to have back then...
I think I actually have what it takes now.
...Perhaps you are [i]finally[/i] worthy of being called my rival?
Let us cross blades some time soon.
. and see if this prodigious transformation of yours also fixed your dismal footwork.
Your agility would be impressive if you didn't owe it to your habit of bolting out of windows before the cuckolded husbands return...
Let's have at it, then! And let's pray your sword is just as sharp.
conversation_gideon_gwendan_humble.prev: So, the one and only Gwendan has finally lost his insufferable glow?

lines: Do you also... find yourself constantly seeking to extract yourself from the vulgar clamour of this world?
All this noise is giving me a headache.
assaulted by the joy of others, don't you think?
But seeing you here, so beautiful and inaccessible in your solitude...
The whole point of being inaccessible is precisely that you shouldn't try to get in.
conversation_gideon_ursule.prev: Do you also... find yourself constantly seeking to extract yourself from the vulgar clamour of this world?

lines: Raise your arms for a second.
Yep. Arms spread wide,  so I can examine every inch of that armor.
B-but the thing is, this kind of armor isn't really made for...
Come on, come on, higher! Let me see those trellises.
One and two, and three, higher.
Ah! I've been scouring the picture book section for ages, but I'd never laid eyes on these gems.
Drawn by the former Sovereign, Arneb the Audacious themselves!
What a bloodhound of the brush!
I had no idea the guy was clever enough to appoint the very traitor who overthrew his predecessor as his own personal guard.
Intelligent, handsome, with a brushstroke that would make angels weep.
. Did he lack even a single quality for the throne?
I'm certain of it now, they're the greatest ruler to ever live!
(And what about you, Your Grace? Is there one you idolize?)
conversation_goberto_chester.prev: Ah! I've been scouring the picture book section for ages, but I'd never laid eyes on these gems.

lines: Are you going to keep your helmet on even when you're [shake rate=20.0 level=5 connected=1]DRINKING[/shake]?!
But of course! Our armour is our pride and joy is it not? Our badge of honour! Aren't you yourself fond of your shiny suit, Sir Gwendan?
Just look at that beautiful reflection of mine sparkling on that soft silver plate.
conversation_goberto_gwendan.prev: Are you going to keep your helmet on even when you're [shake rate=20.0 level=5 connected=1]DRINKING[/shake]?!

lines: A curious way to use monkshood decoction.
Seeking to extract purity from a plant so toxic reminds me of my exercises at Brimwood.
I wasn't aware you had become a practitioner of the alchemical arts, Sir.
It is indeed my inspiration; my method lies halfway between the rigour of Moonvale and the very peculiar approach of the mages of Brimwood.
The precision of the former, and that stubborn refusal to ever shrink from the darkness of the latter...
For there is no thick poison that does not hide a potent remedy within its heart.
...I'm glad to see you were able to draw something from your time away, Sir.
... I fear it was at the cost of me distilling countless tears.
conversation_gwendan_humble_belladonna.prev: A curious way to use monkshood decoction.

lines: ... Sorry, but I think there's a [i]one[/i]-princess limit in this place.
Perhaps I should try to shrink myself?
I can become quite small if I pull my shoulders in.
Sadly, [i]girlie[/i], we don't have any other choice to solve this...
is this the only logical way out?
I am prepared to accept my fate, if that is the protocol.
She observes her interlocutor's carotid artery, as though trying to gauge the optimal level of pressure required for strangulation.
No room for female competition here, [i]girlie[/i].
Sit down, tell me your fallen princess lore...
Running a county... that's just small potatoes!
And believe me, I know what I'm talking about. It happened to me.
And I'd be ready to do it again, if necessary.
It only happened to my father one little time, and yet... he's already in pieces.
His bones make the sound of old damp wood in the morning.
It's because he's no good at the job.
(You should take his place, Lady Ligia.
I do not find this conversation pleasing, Sir.
But perhaps... is it the truth within it that I dislike?
If I were a Countess, my decrees would be more lenient...
And I believe my expertise in fish would constitute an underrated political strategy.
conversation_ligia_chester.prev: Running a county... that's just small potatoes!

lines: Sir Childeric and Lady Ligia watch as people stream into the dining hall.
... E-everyone... h-how do they all manage to talk at the same time and l-listen to each other
I don't think they pay attention to each other, Sir.
Like fish in a tank that's too small.
They bounce off each other [i]instinctively[/i], you see?
A-ah, sometimes I just feel like a f-fish out of water.
Oh... try to focus on your heartbeat, Sir.
If you focus on that steady sound, everything else becomes background music, doesn't it?
It's a very soothing form of relaxation for me...
conversation_ligia_childeric.prev: Sir Childeric and Lady Ligia watch as people stream into the dining hall.

lines: Have you never dipped your body in the blue of the ocean, Sir?
I see no point in letting my meat marinate in a saline solution for several hours.
And I imagine it alters the taste of the flesh.
I have never bitten my own arms to check, but since I leave the water more relaxed than when I entered.
. I imagine the texture becomes more tender.
Water unties the knots in one's head and in their body.
And sometimes, you can even feel the fish brushing against you softly.
Their eyeballs are so empty they give me the physical impulse to shove my phalanges in just to fill them.
... Why do humans need "relaxation" when they possess the ultimate biological vessel?
The model everyone dreams of piloting?
... It's a vessel that's sometimes difficult to steer, Sir.
Can you teach me how to swim?
conversation_ligia_dulahan_human.prev: Have you never dipped your body in the blue of the ocean, Sir?

lines: ...Have you never thought of offering your theoretical writings as gifts?
Truth is always more palatable when wrapped in fine linen, isn't it?
. my father might have been more inclined to change the world if the idea had been served on a bed of cake.
... But the conditions must be right for such ideas to resonate.
But what if you came [i]in person[/i]?
I am certain my father would be impressed.
Your wounds make you very human, after all.
I can feel your intentions are pure...
... But these scars are merely the marks of the order of Southbay, which left me with nothing but forced labour to survive back when I lived there, Lady Ligia.
conversation_ligia_epicrates.prev: ...Have you never thought of offering your theoretical writings as gifts?

lines: Get out of my way, dog.
Between a dragon and a mutt, you already know who walks away.
The wolf's wails echo plaintively through the hallway as the young heir walks away.
