lines: Epicrates stands before you as though he had been expecting you to arrive today.
It seems we never had the opportunity to properly introduce ourselves on this path, comrade.
Yet, I believe that for our alliance to flourish, it is essential that I unveil certain aspects of my existence.
His sulphur-yellow eye, seemingly an intruder lodged in the centre of his battered face, sends a chill down your spine.
... Whatever you may have heard about me since the start of your reign, I am originally just a young man from Southbay.
And like many others, I was a sailor there long before my journey led me to the lands of Brimwood.
Should you have further questions, I am prepared to answer.
Why did you go to Brimwood?
Where did you get all your... injuries?
What was life like in Brimwood?
We did not name it so then.
What role did you play in the revolt?
(END) I don't want to know any more.
What exactly *are* you? How are you able to retain your memories through these cycles of time?
Alas, this is not the moment for me to reveal that here.
(END) I have nothing more to learn.
So it looks like our roads will not converge on this particular trail.
Yet, I remain at your disposal. Who can say if, by pondering my words, you might yet discover other times, other threads that would better accommodate our alliance.
Life in Southbay was not easy back then.
I was born on the docks and spent my childhood there. The common fate of children whose births were never claimed.
In those days, ships needed countless small hands for the dirtiest chores.
I possess no memory of my life prior to my first crossing.
Quite naturally, I departed Southbay in the hope of a more auspicious life.
Brimwood was also very different back then.
After all, your face cannot be so very different from my own, beneath that mask of yours.
Those burns are all I have left of Southbay.
Suffice it to say, the carpenter of the ship on which I served left a scar that neither time nor healers can erase.
Perhaps we share the same ugliness.
That's what I like to think.
Brimwood was nothing like you can imagine today.
It was a monarchical county like any other.
Barely out of childhood, I had no horizons there other than the mines in my struggle to survive.
The days were arduous, yet we possessed a sense of camaraderie that flourished among us laborers. All, enduring the same hardships.
I forged my education there, between mining labor and the manuscripts I managed to steal.
It was the sole path to freedom offered me.
In the mines, poverty takes on a singular taste.
Wherever one's gaze might fall, only the grim and dreary rock confronts you.
One must nourish the mind elsewhere.
Today, it is the nobles who work in these mines in Brimwood.
How did Brimwood become this proletarian republic?
It seems cruel to inflict the fate that caused you so much suffering on the nobles.
I respect your point of view, my friend.
Brimwood's justice claims no perfection, yet it's outcry against the system was articulated this way for legitimate reasons.
A legitimate backlash against those who oppressed you back then.
This form of material restitution through labor may, however, seem vindictive in some respects.
If that is your wish, my friend.
What is your knowledge of Brimwood's history within this timeline, my friend?
Back then, Brimwood's riches, its ores and timber, were exported throughout the realm, financing the opulence of a caste of nobles and bourgeois.
Yet the nobles greed proved their undoing. They attempted to deceive the Angelor Empire by selling mining rights that were not theirs.
The Imperial response, led by the Emperor, Uther the Despot, was merciless.
This marked the first turning point.
While the nobles abandoned the sacrificed populace to their fate, the workers united against the Empire.
Once victorious, we caught the traitors.
They were forced to repay their debt at the very place where they themselves once shackled us.
Thus were born the penitentiaries of Brimwood, after the Great Revolt.
When we first began to organise amid the darkness of the mines, our gatherings took the form of vast popular assemblies, later becoming the Congregation.
Concurrently, smaller circles forged what would become the the Guild's precepts, debating politics and philosophy to give direction to this anger.
I helped erect these ideas, committing them to paper.
As for the term "Epicratism," so often spat by the nobility to decry the Guild's texts, it is nothing more than a misnomer used by terrified aristocrats.
What are your real goals? And those of the Guild?
The Guild preaches equality and liberty for all peoples, and the abolition of the dominant figures that currently impede these freedoms.
The intensity of his gaze increases even more.
... Monarchy is still the norm. The Guild won't stop there, right?
That world still falls short of the Guild's ideal, does it not, my friend?
Accordingly, my designs continue to strive toward that aim.
However, the hour has not yet struck for me to divulge further details.
epicrates_affinity_1.prev: Epicrates stands before you as though he had been expecting you to arrive today.

lines: In a slow gesture, he hands you a book with his left hand.
Are you familiar with the story of the former Sovereign, Candid the Kind?
I know about his love story with Shamrock of Clovermont.
Indeed, this idyll is one of the preeminent legacies preserved from that Sovereign's reign...
I know he is the author of a book of songs renowned in Brimwood.
This volume I hold is a copy of it.
Your predecessor, however distant, indelibly shaped our history.
Their life and deeds lie at the heart of our precepts.
The volume I now hold is a copy of the songs they composed during their lifetime.
Beneath their apparent childish simplicity, these songs serve as the foundational texts for the Guild's precepts.
His bright eye takes on a hint of regret.
Their convictions endure within this modest, child‑like collection I carry, the [i]Candid's Songs[/i].
Candid mastered the art of subtext.
When one reads between the lines, a genuine critique of the monarchical system emerges.
Their entire reign mirrored these writings.
That of a seemingly naive, benevolent ruler who secretly worked towards their ideal.
His bright eye takes on a hint of regret.
Regrettably, contemporary perception reduces their rule to that naive, softened image.
In collective memory, it is through the '[i]Song of Shamrock[/i]' that they are most frequently evoked.
. According to that ballad, Candid died of love, their gaze fixed upon their beloved knight, Shamrock.
And that is all history has chosen to preserve.
Yet, celebrating this romance to such an extent serves chiefly to conceal a darker truth. Candid were assassinated for their convictions.
Shamrock, their knight and lover, is invoked to obscure the figure of Melior, their knight and assassin, who was manipulated by the ruling nobility.
They were slain for having dreamed of a world without rulers.
What exactly do their writings say?
Why are you telling me all this?
For, after all, the Candid's Songs are naught but that, symbols and messages...
A slight smile stretches his injured skin.
The tale of a mad Sovereign who ultimately destroyed his own castle, his seat of power and allowed his people raise a farm upon its ruins.
The narrative is filled with bizarre and even incomprehensible details, talking animals and symbolic caricatures.
A slight smile stretches his injured skin.
It is striking to observe what a distorted trace history has preserved of this Sovereign, is it not?
... For the same voices always author official chronicles, disregarding deeds and convictions.
They were driven by a dream, a vision of the world, and they sowed symbols so their partisans might continue their work.
Candid's dream world seems utopian and dangerous to me.
Is such an ideal truly achievable?
Is it not the very essence of power to convince you of its own necessity, my friend?
After all, it is far easier to imagine the end of this world than the end of the order that governs it...
Even when your region found itself deprived of the Tower's regency, its inhabitants continued to wait relentlessly for the return of a royal figure.
But a path toward that ideal does exist.
His voice suddenly deepens, taking on a serious tone.
... And this necessitates an artifact, attainable by treading a virtuous path, my friend.
in this reality, or perhaps in another.
It can appear to the Sovereign who succeeds in rallying all subjects under one and the same banner.
But there are many dissonances standing in the way of that goal, aren't there?
Know that a lost child possesses the power to heal the discords dwelling within your people.
Thus... following his path may well lead to this unification.
Which child are you talking about?
The cards are already in your hand.
Regardless, remember that, whether upon this thread or another, these aspirations shall aid you in engendering a new end.
Provided that you have not succumbed to the snares of the demon lurking here, beneath the stone.
To conceive of achieving such a design will be impossible if you have entered into a pact with the occult forces of power.
For never would such potencies consent to their own destruction.
That is all I may reveal to you here.
The presence of Epicrates in these places gives you a distinct feeling, as if its occult powers were lying in wait.
... It is here that all may be concluded; are you aware?
Should you choose to bring down the Tower, it is in these very places that the [b][color=986b3b]Golden Key[/color][/b] will prove useful.
... If this thread of destiny has indeed inspired such designs within you.
I don't know if I wish such a thing.
Doubt in the face of the unknown is natural.
It is even counter‑intuitive to imagine such a paradigm shift without being cornered into it.
Uncertainty does indeed appear dangerous to a mind lulled by comfort.
I hope to bring this system to an end.
That is the only way to achieve it.
For the yoke of power is a cage from which one cannot break free as long as its symbols and representatives endure.
The people live through those same symbols, unable to extricate themselves, trapped in a form of passive consent.
That is what sustains the illusion of order.
That is what prevents any alternative from emerging in our unconscious minds.
If the people agree, why change anything?
Can one truly speak of consent within a space of such narrow confines?
Let's say we overthrow the monarchy. Then what?
It is the people who must decide their own fate.
The fall of the Tower and the collapse of the monarchy constitute only the first stage; what follows will be the work of those who remain, building upon the ruins.
As the people of Brimwood once did, I deeply hope that this reconstruction will take the shape of a popular union, carried forward by workers and the oppressed.
Yet it is not my place to dictate the direction to be taken.
After all, if people are not prepared to conceive of such a system and their consciousness has not been sufficiently nurtured, then this future simply will not come to be.
Nevertheless, I am convinced that it is vital to afford these alternatives a chance to exist.
No model can appeal to the majority without a leader.
... And yet Brimwood proves the opposite.
I aspire to make that possible.
Glad to hear you say so.
... But surely, imagining such an event without strife is utopian, is it not?
Even as far as you are concerned.
This Tower and its powers are what sustain your life, after all.
The destruction of the Tower will unfortunately spell your slow death.
Should you indeed decide to employ the [b][color=986b3b]Golden Key[/color][/b]
. remember that it is vital for you to combat the threat of the Empire, Sovereign.
Without doing so, the Empire will descend upon your realm once the Tower falls.
Unfortunately, this scenario entails vulnerability for at least some time.
He stops for several minutes, intensely sizing you up with his eye.
You have shown wisdom by not succumbing to the demon's powers along this line of destiny.
Thus, if you possess the Key, my friend, it falls solely to you to walk this path.
... But I persist in believing that other times, other threads, shall know how to welcome this resolution.
A sad smile crosses his lips.
... Such is an endeavour that shall have required many a journey, my dear friend.
My legacy now rests within your hands.
Perhaps, at last, I may find repose.
Naught remains between you but silence, tinged with a breath of hope.
A breath as gentle as it is ephemeral.
. This thread of destiny does not permit the fulfillment of that scheme.
By pact with the demon, you have here accepted its occult power... as I told you, it is now futile to hope for the Tower's destruction.
Once the Emperor is vanquished, you will be able to wield your power with unmatched strength, allowing you to turn back the clock to a moment before the pact's consummation...
In the next strand, should you manage to reign without ever succumbing to the occult forces, then...
This other end shall become possible.
Make the right decisions upon this coming journey, my friend.
History shall continue to watch you.
The weather is fine, my friend.
A new, unheard calm marks his voice.
... Though I reject that Tower and all it represents...
... I must concede that its architecture remains fascinating.
A pity it should serve the cravings of power, alas.
His sulphur-yellow eye, which never leaves you, scans the surroundings for the first time, absorbing the vegetation and flowers.
I'm glad you've found peace here.
But it is not this architecture that grants me solace here, you know.
You exchange a meaningful glance; his gaze is tinged with deep esteem.
Before crossing paths with you, I must confess that had never felt such closeness to anyone.
This is very dear to me.
As orphans of everything, I believe we share a common experience of a past filled with wandering and loneliness.
The weight of our tormented faces, the stigma that exiles us from the world of men.
This singular worldview that lives inside me, I see its reflection in you.
And how ironic to find that resonance in a figure of power who should oppose me.
And even so, upon this thread, our designs cannot be reconciled
. I retain the inner conviction that other eras harbor our alliance.
His gaze wanders into the distance.
I feel close to you, my friend.
You are also precious to me, my friend.
I still see you as my equal, and I do not doubt that, in other circumstances, you would open your heart.
His gaze locks with yours again.
... Perhaps this ability of mine, monstrous as it is, also lets me resonate with your condition.
Its energy mirrors what lingers in your dungeons, after all.
A reflection of the dark side of the Tower's power.
. I think I can now reveal it to you.
This singular faculty I possess, granting me leave to read between the lines of time.
It was inherited from a demon.
I met it in the Brimwood mines when I was younger.
I had the leisure to converse with it at length.
His words are imbued with a serene, almost mystical calm.
But such entities are only capable of deception, aren't they?
When it tried to manipulate me to regain its freedom, I captured it.
then dissected it to grasp its faculties.
At the end of that research I managed to extract its eyes.
Two demonic eyes with unrivaled mystical properties.
One of them was given to you when you cleared me during the trial.
His sulphur eye stares at you more intensely than ever before.
... To it, I owe this supernatural clairvoyance.
... What exactly do you see through it?
Welcoming such power is never without consequences, right?
Yet that sacrifice was necessary to set the course of time towards the designs within me.
fragments of other temporal strands assailing me, beyond my control.
have multiplied since you took the throne, my friend.
You sense a collision of sadness, determination and melancholy within him.
In any case, you make this path a little more bearable, my friend.
Could this be our time of collaboration?
I look forward to seeing what this path will hold for us, my friend.
Epicrates left the kingdom forever, disappearing into the maelstrom of history.
"[i]This isn't the one[/i]" was all he said to the Sovereign before leaving.
epicrates_ending.prev: Epicrates left the kingdom forever, disappearing into the maelstrom of history.

lines: ? I would not have thought such practices still in use in this kingdom...
One would say misfortune seeks you out, in this line of fate.
Sordid events accumulate along your path, I must say.
The dark forces of your power may find fertile ground here.
Things do not distort themselves thus without a hand to twist them, do they?
epicrates_intervention_after_rupin_griev.prev: Sordid events accumulate along your path, I must say.

lines: It is troubling to see that the evil plaguing these lands has taken on the ugly reflection of the power that governs them...
You have fractured things here, Your Grace - irreparably.
These lands shall forever bear your mark.

lines: Daisy is followed by a trotting goat in good condition. The creature glances at you but not with enough hatred to kill you this time.
"I'll let you live. For now." Her eyes seem to convey.
The poor girl was trapped in a fermenting cellar after surprising a thief inside.
During their struggle, the door was locked and she couldn't get out.
The locals found her and the thief was arrested.
I'm sorry for wasting the guards time searching the Tower.
Buuuuut here's a little reward for puttin' your heart into it.
The woman is followed by a trotting goat in good condition. The creature looks at you with a hatred you have never seen before.
"Time's up." Her eyes seem to convey.
The poor girl was trapped in a fermenting cellar after surprising a thief inside.
During their struggle, the door was locked and she couldn't get out.
The locals found her and the thief was arrested.
Wanted you to know, even though, y'know.
We're feeling a little less inclined to be paying such high taxes to someone who cares so little for one of our own.
The woman is followed by a trotting goat in good condition. The creature glances at you, and then ignores you completely. You feel empty inside.
The poor girl was trapped in a fermenting cellar after surprising a thief inside.
During their struggle, the door was locked and she couldn't get out.
The locals found her and the thief was arrested.
I know that you cared, even if you couldn't do anything.
Perhaps it all worked out for the best.
Thanks again for this wonderful forge!
I'm still setting things up but I have a few relics to sell.
Very well, Sovereign... looks like you're about to meet a rather inglorious end...
... all thanks to your own 'brilliant' choices.
But hey, maybe if you hadn't played your cards like a sucker, you'd be sipping sweet, sweet victory right now.
But you're in luck: in my great mercy, I'm giving you the chance to write History once again.

lines: You've smashed this threat... for now.
But just imagine all the splendid chaos you missed by not trying other ways.
Start over, if you dare... the real game is just beginnning.
Oh! That was... unexpectedly easy. I had a whole monologue ready.
But if you will allow me, I shall continue.
.a small detail I may have overlooked.
But if you will allow me, I shall continue.
No need. I know you're looking for information on your origins.
As I have said before, my origins remain an enigma I yearn to unravel.
. And you may hold the key.
I recently learned something crucial from the Governess of the Brizh orphanage where I spent my earliest years. I was apparently left there by a local brigand.
With your aid...I believe obtaining further information from this bandit would be quite trivial.
...That is not your *only* reason for joining my Round Table, is it?
What a thought but I wouldn't dare pull a stunt like that.
I truly wish to serve you.
So one might as well combine my duty with... the resolution of the mystery that has robbed me of sleep since time immemorial.
We don't have time for such frivolities.
I am delighted to provoke such emotions.
I thought you were ready to dissect the mysteries of the civil registry...
In the blink of an eye, my aura of mystery has been blown away like dust in the wind.
You are likely the child of Mathilda of Gavault and Guilhelm of Groveshire.
With all due respect, what is the source of such a theory?
You were taken as an infant from a Groveshire convoy, during a raid by Gavault militia.
. Did you get this information from... the man I was planning to question?.
. An ambush in Groveshire by Gavault, which would have occurred about a quarter of a century ago...seems rather plausible to me.
The tensions between these two counties, unexplained and fierce, date from approximately that period...
. Are you implying that my possible abduction is the source of these tensions?
that these two Counts had an affair?
...There were several rumours circulating during that period around this.
[font_size=18]But how did you come to learn this?[/font_size]
Eyes lost in the distance, Sir Gideon is in a trance.
. I think these two believe you are dead, as I doubt these two counts would have knowingly abandoned an heir.
...This would certainly explain their long-standing and unexplained feud.
. All of this is a lot to process.
With hunched shoulders and downcast eyes, the glamour of your new recruit is somewhat faded.
Take some time to digest all this. Get some rest.
You'll be able to do your job, right?
Your kindness seems to elicit a slight spark of positivity in the young man again.
His words are sharp. You have snapped him from his thoughts with your cold reality check.
.P-perhaps this revelation would have been easier to accept at the end of a heroic quest for the truth...
He tries but fails to mask the emotion in his trembling voice.
...What if your surprisingly insightful information were the key to resolving this discord?
...Let us simply hope that Sir Gideon can overcome this revelation.
gideon_accept_recruitment_reaction.prev: Oh! That was... unexpectedly easy. I had a whole monologue ready.

lines: I imagine you're not unaware that the water in the jars now tastes of twilight rain.
Even the air feels heavy with silence. Thick, almost tangible... As if the stones themselves were holding their breath.
What exactly do you see in our jugs?
Unfortunately, I have to say that I don't either.
Despite appearances, I am mostly content to simply put random words next to each other, Your Grace.
However, you really should examine the water in our jugs.
I saw an insect floating in one of them.
Do you need me to clean the jug?
I think it was some kind of cockroach.
I can clean it, if you like.
Would you like to share this carafe with me?
A sign of misfortune? That's a good excuse not to go on a quest today, Your Grace.
Although I find the idea repulsive, I appreciate your boldness.
However, my answer is obviously no.
The last time I crossed that line of intimacy, it ended poorly...
My thoughts are occasionally clouded with recollections of that person. Frantically. Affectionately.
It's a burden I wouldn't wish on anyone.
Memories can be cruel, can't they?
Extreme intimacy equals sharing water. I take note.
I see there... the shadow of a weighty past,
a legacy hanging in the air,
And yet... there is something melancholic in its aftertaste.
Would you like to share this carafe with me?
Do you want me to clean the jug for you?
Yes, and grief... is a patient guest.
It seeps into everything. Jars. Porridge. Politics...
And in our exchanges as well, clearly. My apologies.
. I'm afraid I have nothing more to offer now...
Apart from my irresistible charm and unattainable aura of mystery, of course.
[font_size=18]Still, that would be kind of you.[/font_size]
The young man's voice is deep and melodious.
You look almost as tired as I am.
. My sleep has been restless lately. Tortured dreams haunt me...
And I awaken with the feeling of having been pursued, like a shroud battered by the wind...
A tunnel of shadows and echoes.
What is the thing that is chasing you?
Don't understand a single thing, but good luck with that.
Well, I find myself wondering whether there is a single thing on this earth that doesn't come after me in the night.
Even in sleep, my consciousness chooses to debate my life choices and every single one of my relationships without cease.
One of them is... particularly stubborn. I suspect my own subconscious is, regrettably, utterly obsessed with the vestiges of that last liaison.
Twisted dreams... I know all about them.
Perhaps getting in touch with this person again could help you get some sleep?
Are your nights also filled with hazy dreams?
Mine assail me with absurd fragments, chasing me at all hours. But... I imagine your nights are haunted in other ways.
a puzzle for the mind that may never truly find rest from.
If the weight of my errors haunts me to such an extent then the those decisions made by the Sorvereign must manifest in your dreams as terrifying forms.
Does anything in particular trouble you?
I'm a pretty good analyst, I know.
Perhaps you could ease your mind by expressing your regrets in a clearer way?
I didn't understand a single word.
Unless, you're implying that a good blow to the head, administered by the person who haunts me, is indeed a way to obtain eternal rest.
I put this down as a mistake from my youth that resulted in unfortunate ill feelings. And those feelings unfortunately concern someone who is... quite fierce.
Thus my regrets will remain firmly in my mind, protected from any fatal blow.
I doubt that sleep will come to those who choose to bury their remorse.
Maybe I can help you forget this person?
Is it not this dramatic complexity that makes me so charming, Your Grace?
What a delightful humiliation to make such a confession but to then see reason from another...
You wish to replace my memories of them with you?
But I must commend your ambitious saviour syndrome.
Alas, I am doomed to be understood by none.
. It seems to me that your reputation portrays you as a lone wanderer with no family or past.
Chosen despite themselves for an extraordinary destiny...
Many assured me you didn't even have a single friend left standing.
Not a relative, not even a forgettable acquaintance.
Despite the years spent building a life of my own, the desire to know more about my past has never left me.
Are you satisfied with what you know today, Gideon?
But perhaps that's the right mindset.
Perhaps my pursuit of knowledge was merely concealing a desire for control. The illusion of mastering my own fate.
I'm...still confused. Sometimes, I even regret that insatiable, candid curiosity that drove me to escape the dark of the unknown.
Knowing where I come from doesn't shed much light on who I ought to be.
Am I Gavault's son, or Groveshire's?
Does either option hold any meaning at all for a soul with no memory of either place?
I'm afraid these questions are forever trapped in limbo. I may never find an answer to them.
And they will forever plague me.
I don't know what to tell you.
You're already much more than your origins could ever define.
You're right, it's time to stop letting my past control me.
Seated on a bench, the young man writes diligently in the pages of a small notebook.
He's focused with a frown on his face.
Still deep in concentration, he bites his lip as he pens a new line.
His hair catches the light rather nicely.
You're standing there perhaps a little too long, though.
The wind with a soft whisper.
...Were you just watching me, Your Grace?
And here I am feeling terribly disappointed.
I was just...jotting down a few memories.
Before you say anything, it's not a diary.
I'm penning my biography and a draft for a song. My hope is that someone shall stumble upon this goldmine one day and turn it into a heroic ballad.
In fact, I plan to throw it off the highest point of Brizh in the near future.
I'm curious. Would you share it with me?
I began, of course, by recounting my noble and lost origins, as well as the war of succession between Groveshire and Gavault that was mine.
I began, of course, by writing about my unknown and forgotten origins. Detailing how a bandit supposedly left me at the Brizh orphanage...
Then, I recounted my journey here.
.up to my integration into your Round Table.
. Do you have any suggestions on how I should continue?
You join him, and he hands you the open notebook and quill.
(Mention a wonderful engagement to a *very* attractive Sovereign.)
It'd be a tragedy for my legend if the bards were to omit that detail.
That's right, I'd forgotten about that irresistible paternal instinct of yours.
And here I was, trying to erase that line from my legend...
Well, you have quite some nerve infiltrating my personal memoirs like that.
...But I must admit you do hold a prime spot in them.
(Draw something. A little cat in the corner of the page, for example.)
That's very sweet, Your Grace, but I fear it may undermine the gravitas of my epic somewhat...
Would you like to add anything else?
...Oh, we're starting to run out of space.
And so ends the additions of the juicy and memorable details for the legend of Gideon.
What an idea I had that day... I hope that's what I'll be remembered for [i]most[/i] of all.
. But I'll let you in on a secret. Don't tell them, but that last name you wrote.
They were quite a thorn in my side on several ventures.
Anything further you think we should add?
(Cross out the last name mentioned in Gideon's comrades.)
Shoot, Your Grace, I hope they never see this...
(Mention a quest where Gideon narrowly escaped death.)
Yes, the tension...the suspense. We need that, indeed.
...I was being a bit overdramatic that day, I must admit.
. b-but is that really appropriate for an epic ballad?
(Mention your desire to spend the rest of your life with Gideon.)
. I...I guess that would be the happy ending for the tragic hero.
...Come to think of it, we missed one last detail.
He reopens the notebook and adds a line about how you were his most devoted admirer, secretly spying on him from the Tower gardens.
He reads over the lines with a smile on his face.
He carefully reviews everything with a smile on his face.
... This will make a sumptuous ballad for the first bard lucky enough to find it.
Despite all the troubles I've faced since I first set foot on the lands of Brizh...
. I must say I'm glad our paths crossed the way they did.
And after all these years spent searching for who I am.
. I find myself thinking that perhaps my place was here all along.
Absorbed by a book concealed within his bright curls, the young man looks up.
...I was completely immersed in this old manuscript I stumbled upon by chance.
He shows you the book's cover,
Shamrock of Clovermont was a Knight in the service of the Round Table under the ancient Sovereign, Candid the Kind.
Shamrock was a former knight of Candid, right?
.let's just say those two had a rather.
...I imagine that some historians may have summarised it that way.
. This song I was reading is...none other than the tale of their passionate romance.
...Candid fell in love with Shamrock, and it is said that.
Hand in hand, their love forged the destiny of the prosperous kingdom of Candid...
.Alas, their story is inseparably tied to a tragic end... for which Shamrock bears some...partial responsibility.
...However, I prefer to tell myself that it's just a minor detail of the story.
Do you find this story more...tragic or beautiful?
Candid was murdered by another knight who disapproved of their union.
It is said that despite being forewarned of this tragic end, Candid refused to call upon the occult powers to save his own life...
... choosing instead to offer his Knight nothing but a silent smile to his knight before passing away...
Eyes locked, until life, gently, left them.
Their love forged an ideal peace that they both strived for.
They completed each other in that way...
And...with their hands joined, they achieved their shared goal.
He stops, seemingly waiting for your reaction.
Does this story...remind you, in some way, of our relationship?
He returns to his book, visibly troubled.
A confession breathed in barely a whisper, yet carrying infinite tenderness.
.You were on my mind whilst reading this.
[font_size=18]And perhaps you've been on my mind for a few too many nights now...[/font_size]
He raises his eyes to you, and his long hair falls softly around his contrite face.
...You can exclude the part about the assassination, obviously.
. I...I haven't had the courage to express it until now, but.
. I don't know if you realize how much you mean to me.
And this goes beyond simple appreciation for helping me learn about my past...
All this despite your rather mad idea of adopting me. A strange whim, but one that ultimately reveals what I admire most about you...
Your peculiar decisions which have always sought only the well-being of those in your care.
. I hadn't quite prepared myself to lay bare such feelings.
I also found myself thinking that, since we are to be wed.
Perhaps our union, like that of Candid and his Knight, could be one of love.
I caught myself envying the place that knight held in Candid's heart...
I must confess that after my last...turbulent relationship, all of this frightened me greatly.
Your hands timidly brush against each other.
Don't apologize... I feel the same way about you.
Your hands finally meet, without another word.
The contact sends a burning shiver down your spine.
You take his hand to seek refuge behind the shelter of a large bookshelf.
(Lift the bottom of the mask slightly, revealing your mouth.)
He holds your gaze momentarily, letting you savour the scent of sweet lilacs.
His trembling lips delicately meet those of your mask.
His trembling lips delicately meet yours.
Next to Gideon, you watch the soft light float in through the library's skylight.
He holds you close to his side.
.Promise me...we will remain loyal to each other?
. I feel ready to try again,
He gently closes his eyes, feeling peaceful.
... You requested my presence, Your Grace?
I want to recruit you, but I still need more time.
You would condemn me to these dreams of lavender?
The minstrels do not sing of waiting of in line, Your Grace.
gideon_come_back_later.prev: ... You requested my presence, Your Grace?

lines: You have never heard such sadness in her voice.
I was deeply saddened to learn of Sir Gideon's passing last night.
You were his instructor, weren't you?
I grieve also. I didn't know you were close.
I did help with Gideon's combat training at the orphanage in Brizh.
... A formidable and courageous knight, the pride of our Round Table.
My heart is heavy with sorrow.
... All of our hearts weep, Alwena.
Sir Gideon remained a loyal knight to the kingdom, respecting his sovereign's decisions at any cost.

Having failed to shed light on the mysteries and conflicts surrounding his birth within the Round Table of Brizh, it seems that his origins must, much to his dismay, remain forever an unanswered question.
After years of loyal service, he finally returned to Groveshire, where he inherited his father's throne.
Beloved and respected by all, he nonetheless spent his life lamenting his tumultuous youth.
After years of loyal service, he finally returned to Gavault and inherited his mother's throne.
Governing was no easy task, but he managed, with time, to earn the trust of his people.
He carried within him a stubborn melancholy until his final days which resurfaced each time the Round Table of Brizh was mentioned...
And with the curious decision the Sovereign had taken to name him successor...
Unwilling to surrender Gideon to any other, the Sovereign bound him to the kingdom of Brizh...
...  Gideon became the chosen heir to the throne of Brizh.

I was stolen as a child during a Gavault attack on a Groveshire convoy.

...Perhaps [i]you[/i] are the cause of these tensions, Sir.

Could this information allow us to manipulate both countries?

it will be difficult to glean anything from these wild speculations.

Alas, the county of Groveshire was rather.
offended at our clear preference for Gavault over them when their representative came to visit us.

offended at our clear preference for Groveshire over them when their representative came to visit us.

.if only we had had this information earlier...
.And thus, am I condemned to carry this secret alone?
...Because all of this seems highly plausible to me, Sir Arlin.

What other explanation for this forbidden dichotomy that gnaws at me? These contrary forces clashing in the depths of my dreams

. Let us resume the audiences of the day, Your Grace.

On the threshold of what I believed would be the most delicate of liberations, only a vast, unfathomable abyss ultimately consumes me...
You just have to give it time.

I know this emptiness. Irresolution hollows it out forever.
My mind just keeps circling around everything that could have been...
... but things will remain this way.

lines: What are you doing in the kitchen? Are you writing to someone, too?

I suppose that's a plot convenience.
Sometimes it's better to be on your own...
A [b]hot experience[/b]? Not sure what temperature has go to do with this, but you are quite the optimist!
I'll mention you in my letter as such an individual.
Oh, come now, Your Grace... playing hard to get is very last century!
Are you playing yourself off in the old fashioned lone wolf type of way, mate?
I was recounting all the sensational things that have happened to me recently.
My arrival in the audience hall and of you who agreed to take me on.
The moment I stepped onto the kitchen floor for the first time.
It changes a man, doesn't it?

Now, if you'll excuse me... there are some familiar faces I'd like to see light up.
I feel like I've grown up just since lunchtime.

I'm so happy I stumbled upon this book! This author illustrates those gallant heroes who risked their lives in the Arena of Almor...

. Ahh, just thinking about it gives me chills!

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]Its pages are written in an ancient dialect, unique to the Virgo guard. I doubt you possess the ability to decipher it.[/font][/font_size]"
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]... Yet I am able to provide you with a summary.[/font][/font_size]"
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]Some elements, in my view, deserve your full attention.[/font][/font_size]"
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]The earliest notes...speak of the necessity to unite all the counties.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]They describe, metaphorically, a gate that would open only once the kingdom is unified, gathered under a single banner.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]Strangely, in this particular sentance the destruction is presented without any apparent negative judgment.[/font][/font_size]"

"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]... While the Clover might serve as a way to guide the innocents to the key, following a path untouched by bloodshed.[/font][/font_size]"

Result was, a few of our lads near ran her aground on the coast.
. could've ended a whole lot worse.
I'll send a knight to investigate.
I'll send a knight to investigate.
... Aye, well... I reckon it's 'em damned scholars of Grest.
All day they squabble, squawkin' how we fish too much and 'ruin the coastal ecosystem', blah, blah, blah... But bellies don't feed themselves, blast it!
I'll send a knight to find the culprit among the scholars.
I'll send a knight to investigate.
Let's hear scholars. Fishing will be regulated.
'n what next, be we goin' to build 'em a throne in the market square while ye're at it?
grest_grievance_scholars_against_overfis.prev: Not long ago there was some nasty fiddlin' with our trawler, someone tampered with the ship to keep us from workin'.

lines: Yer Grace, it's complicated with Grest's scholars.
'Em gone and started a strike right outside the new ore mine. We need you to knock some sense into 'em so the miners can get back to work.
I'll send a knight to put a stop to the strike.
Why are they on strike, exactly?
'pparently they reckon the mine's sittin' on some ancient site from a lost civilisation. Sounds like one of 'em pub stories to me, Yer Grace.
Sounds like it. I'll send a knight to stop the strike
We should let them excavate the site.
Rip their banners and hand them shovels. History digs don't fill coffers.
If that's yer wish, Yer Grace.
I'm sure the miners'll be thrilled to have the.
grest_grievance_scholars_strike.prev: Yer Grace, it's complicated with Grest's scholars.

lines: Say, does a sea salamander breathe fire? Or rather water?
It depends, a Brizh salamander or a Basalt Isles salamander?
... hold yer horses, if it's not water resistant, what the hell is it doin' in the ocean?
Aye, we be no strangers to the squalls...
Nay, 'cause one of these here sea devils has made its home in one of the town's sweet little coves.
I'll send some men. Trap it, and roast it.
A ritual to calm her and send her back into the depths might help.
Try to tame it? For sea fishing.
Uh, but ain't salamanders got a touch o' poison, aye?
Erm... 'cept fer the fishin', we ain't got much in the way o' [i]local rituals[/i] 'round these parts...
grest_grievance_sea_salamander.prev: Say, does a sea salamander breathe fire? Or rather water?

Is your armour... even shinier than before...?
Shinier? It has always been this way, Your Grace. But I am not surprised if you continue to still be mesmerised by my presence.

lines: Aye, we be wantin' ye to join our tug-of-war, the one we're settin' up with the folks across the bay. But I'd forgotten that ye can't move.

We were fixin' to use a bit of muscle, but them landlubber bookworms in town wanted to try some strange enchantments.
Shiver me timbers, I dunno what to think!
Build up your strength with the scholars.
Use the spells, but warn your rivals. They'll work something out.
Aye, we'll be makin' waves again this year, for sure!

Ghostly voices? My fearless knights are here to help.
If made up voices frighten the people then perhaps they are not fit to walk my roads.

lines: Ah, how sad it makes me to face your charming face in such dire circumstances.
My name is Rupin, I'm a modest merchant of curiosities in Brimwood, and humble treasurer of our little...local fraternity.
A pleasure to meet you in person, my dear. Even if it is under such circumstances.
. A-are you referring to the Brimwood Guild?
... What is the purpose of your visit?
See, it would appear that one of your knights had the bold idea of contracting an abyssal volume of debts with my associates...before vanishing into thin air.
After politely questioning his family (charming people, if a bit talkative) it seems he goes by the name of '[i]Gwendoo[/i]'.
I imagine that rings a bell?
Ah... Gwendan.  I'll clear this up with him.
How refreshingly honest of you to admit it!
Well, don't delay in clearing up this matter. I would be very saddened if the Guild were required to pay another visit to help "remedy" this situation...
. If that's the answer you wish to give, my dear Grace...
But a word of advice... recover your memory. And quickly.
The Knight is clearly wearing your colours, and the Guild will not let the walls of this Tower stand in the way of collecting what is owed...
. Words to the wise, my dear.
Stop bothering me, peasants, you are wasting my time.
Now, let us dance, feast and...
Isn't that MY throne, Sir Gwendan?
Err... This isn't what you think.
I was just wondering what the view was like here.
Turns out, it's not that great, if you ask me.
You dared to sit on MY throne?
Would you like to suggest any improvements, Sir Gwendan?
Come now Your Grace, it's hardly high treason.
You've only been here for a couple of weeks, haven't you? And all you had to do was open a door to become the new Sovereign...
If I had come here sooner then perhaps I would have been able to...
Picture it. The sparkling knight Gwendan, adorned with this armour that shines like diamonds and is (obviously) magical. The tower doors thrown open with such ceremony...
. Well. Too late for that now, I suppose.
I'll pretend I didn't hear that. What's so bad about the view from the throne?
I was wondering when you would finally think to ask for my opinion.
Firstly, this hall is terribly dull. You should have jesters, musicians, jugglers and poets at your court. Otherwise, how can you expect anyone to take you seriously?
Back when Villador was at the height of its prosperity, we would frequently host banquets and valiant tournaments day in and day out.
I care little for such frivolities.
Tournaments? I shall think on it.
Well, I don't think I will be staying in this graveyard of a court for a very long.
I have a lot of other ideas, if you need my advice again.
gwendan_affinity_1.prev: Stop bothering me, peasants, you are wasting my time.

lines: When will we finally be able to eat properly in this cursed Tower?
This soup... tasteless, [i]bland[/i]... a veritable crime against my noble palate.
Nobody's forcing you to eat it.
Anything else the spoilt little prince wishes to cry about?
Ah! I'm glad we agree on that point!
. Don't you bear some responsibility for this?
Should we ignore such crimes as a given? Inaction does not make a knight.
[shake]You will NOT. Speak to me. Like that. EVER AGAIN.[/shake]
I think I'd be rather embarrassed if I was in your place.
I will find out who is responsible.
He stops and seems to fix his gaze on something in the distance.
Did you know that the last time I was served a dish as pitiful as this, someone was murdered at the same dinner table?
Not by my hand, of course - I would never permit such a vulgar end with such cowardice attached.
I recall it so vividly. The late Duke of Beaconsbury.
face-down in his vile stew, which was already a crime in itself.
The wine wasn't half bad, though.
And you survived such horror? You are very courageous.
Even worse. It was enough even without being able to see in the dark. The splashes, the screams and the reek of that stew...
And what about my family's beautiful silk tablecloth? Completely ruined!
Trust me, it's something that stays with you for life.
Many guests had fainted, but I, of course, remained sparkling.
... When you're dressed like me, you have to keep your cool.
Murder is rampant nowadays. It must displease you.
It's brutal, inelegant and it ruins the upholstery.
There's no honor in sneaking off to murder someone while their family, just in the next room, goes about their lives in blissful ignorance. It's all so hollow...
gwendan_affinity_2.prev: When will we finally be able to eat properly in this cursed Tower?

lines: ... You have a knack for arriving just as you are being spoken of, Your Grace.
Your knight folds up a scroll he was busy writing on.
And to whom are you singing my praises?
Are you writing to your family?
My adoptive family, so to speak.
As unlikely as it may seem, some of the connections I made in Brimwood have become...particularly dear to me.
We promised to stay in touch, so I owed to them to share the news of my return.
I half-expected you to make nothing but enemies in Brimwood.
So you paid your debt by working, right?
Ah, the early days were far from easy.
Between my unpaid debt, my flashy armour, and my privileged name, I became the penitentiaries' official punching bag in less than two minutes.
And since I hadn't yet learned how to shut my damn mouth, I'd even insult the jailer who brought me my soup...
The 'penitentiaries'? You did some kind of community service...right?
So you learned to shut up...which just goes to show, anything is possible.
So how did you manage to make friends there? I'm curious.
And how do you feel now?
So to speak, the Brimwood penitentiaries are the final destination for criminals and highborns with debts to settle with the county... whatever the nature of those debts.
They were established during their Great Revolt... but I'm sure you already knew that.
Those bleak pits at the bottom of their mines ultimately taught me quite a lot.
Though it did cost me a bit of the shine on my armour...
I'm surprised you've settled in so well.
And did you meet friends there?
I won't argue with that. Given the ego I once had, seeing me humbled must look something close to a miracle.
Who knows what else I'm capable of now?
These penitentiaries are crawling with petty nobles, who, for the most part, had sold out their county to the Empire before the Revolt.

Watching that bunch of haughty fools make a spectacle of themselves, snickering, backstabbing eachother for vainglory... It was like a mirror being held up to my own face. I looked far too much like them... I WAS them.
... The people of Brimwood may seem vindictive, even cruel, but believe me...no one appreciates redemption quite like they do.
He pauses for a few seconds, lost in though.
... I think it was only once I'd dropped the arrogant act that I finally managed to make some real connections outside the pens.
I wouldn't have bet you'd last more than a day there.
And how do you feel now?
Honestly, I feel...pretty lucky to have crossed paths with people capable of forgiveness.
Comrades who managed to see something genuine in me...
I think that's what truly changed me, far more than the hours spent working the mines.
... That has most definitely tarnished my armour's shine, though. I imagine it will never gleam quite like it used to.
It's for the best. Honestly, it looked tacky.
I almost regret sending you to that hellhole.
I think you are more brilliant than ever...
You could have told me, though.
... You preferred me liar and arrogant?
There's no accounting for taste, I suppose.
... That... goes straight to my heart, Your Grace.
You too, are lighting up this place.
gwendan_affinity_3_humble.prev: ... You have a knack for arriving just as you are being spoken of, Your Grace.

lines: He hands you a small leather purse from his armour.
Where does such generosity come from?
Well...  I have to admit that your sudden eagerness to settle my debts, though much appreciated, has left me feeling a bit...awkward.
And since I promised to return the favour, well...
I was planning to pay you back, and it just so happens that I received some unexpected financial assistance from a rather wealthy relative.
So you went crying to your Aunt, is that it?
Sorry to put you in this situation.
Actually, some of my Aunt Gwendolen's friends were there that day, and let's just say I know how to use my charms.
It's very noble of you to acknowledge the emotional toll your reckless generosity has put me through.
I even had to turn on the charm for my Aunt's old friends, can you believe it?...
... But sleep well. You'll have your money back.
Did you seriously collect those coins just by batting your eyelashes?
Charming people is child's play for you, I suppose.
Let's say I know how to make the most of the gifts that nature has so generously given me.
A little something to keep in your mind.
. I suppose it's always handy to have some pretty boys at your Table.
... That said, judging by the others, one can't exactly say that's a mandatory requirement for sitting there.
My knights are all *very* easy on the eyes.
Yes, I see who you're referring to...at least he's sweet.
If you prefer denial, Your Grace, so be it...
Well, I suppose he needs at least that much going for him.
But I won't deny that it is sometimes hard for me to stand by his side.
... I do it for you, Your Grace.
The competition is not actually very fierce.
I must say I wonder about you.
What a waste to hide behind that mask.
I mean, I wouldn't want to be ruled by a toad.
But enough talk. Just two or three more visits with my charrms, and I'll owe you nothing.
You see Sir Gwendan standing motionless in the gardens.
He seems to be rotating his arms and hands in front of his eyes, as if checking his armour.
No, it's not really my thing anymore.
... Do you remember what I revealed to you about this armour?
About how its legendary power was nothing but a sham. That it was, in truth, nothing more than an ornate suit of mail, entirely devoid of any magical properties?
Well...when I put it on this morning, I had the feeling that something had [i]changed[/i].
Have you turned into a magician?
You mean it only took *a little* dirt for it to reveal its full potential?
Erm, I don't know exactly what caused this, but...
And, having confirmed my suspicions with an apothecary in Brizh
.it seems that powerful traces of magic are now radiating from it.
... Anyway, it seems that compulsive investment wasn't so foolish after all.
So...your desire to shine has finally paid off.
I hope that in Brimwood, you had also learnt how to manage your finances.
It just took a little introspection and some permanent calluses on my hands. A long-term investment.
But deep down... I don't think buying that armour was purely about showing off, you know?
... Maybe it was just my way of looking for a little security after my parents died.
He stops as if he had said too much.
... Let's just say I've learned the value of money.
I'd never wanted for anything, so naturally.
once my parents were gone, I made a number of decisions that were questionable.
Including the purchase of this armour.
... I didn't know your parents had passed away.
a sordid story I almost never bring up.
To cut a long story short, my parents were murdered in their own home by a man they had taken in and sheltered from a conflict.
... An event that...left its mark, I suppose.
His voice is tinged with regrets.
I wouldn't want to get too heavy.
... Thank you for sharing this with me.
It's not that tragic. I've got worse stories.
You're not. I want to learn more about you, Gwendan.
I'm sorry for you, Your Grace.
The feeling is mutual, you know?
And besides, it'll be a relief to finally stop being the sole subject of conversation.
Let's spend more time together, then.
... I'm ready to share all my secrets with you.
But it's important that you keep your share of mystery, isn't it?
Seems healthier that way to me.
gwendan_affinity_4_humble.prev: You see Sir Gwendan standing motionless in the gardens.

lines: You wished to see me, Your Grace?
I thought about recruiting you, but turns out I still need more time.
gwendan_come_back_later.prev: You wished to see me, Your Grace?

lines: The voice of Villador's emissary echoes throughout the courtroom, reverberating with anger and pain.
. that Villador no longer stands with you.
I... I knew that joining your ranks was a bad idea.
.If only he had the sense to listen to me.
You wished to see me, Your Grace?
You have an outstanding debt with Brimwood...is that true?
So your skipping out on your debts?
... Err, I can explain everything, okay?
I... maybe, some time ago, had the [i]need[/i] to borrow a rather [i]reasonable[/i] sum from certain
For a very noble cause, of course.
... Why didn't you tell me about this beforehand?
And you used that money for...?
... I simply thought that a shameful unpaid bills story would be a stain on the first page of my memoirs.
. would you have welcomed a hero of such grand destiny.
if that grand destiny came with empty pockets?
Thanks for saying that out loud.
I would have accepted you as you are, Gwendan - with your flaws and your... debts.
And you used that money to...?
A hero must have armour worthy of the name, wouldn't you agree?
Armour whose brilliance is matched only by the magic it holds...
By a series of circumstances involving...a distant step-cousin...of a friend...of the ruling family of Clovermont... I happened upon just such a little marvel.
... In short, I wasn't going to pay back for equipment that only half works.
Dressed in my finest attire, I was therefore forced to cut ties with the creditors of Brimwood.
... Let's avoid any trouble. I'll pay your debt and it would be best that you stay here.
... You'll have to leave this Round Table. Come back when you have paid your debt.
Would you do that for me?
Well, you are certainly a most.
I'll do my best to return the favour, Your Grace.
Very well, if that is your wish.
gwendan_debt_reveal_reaction.prev: You wished to see me, Your Grace?

lines: Sir Gwendan remained at the Tower, where he became a wealthy and distinguished knight.
Stories of his striking beauty and his "modest nature" were told throughout the kingdom.
Sir Gwendan became a knight respected for his modesty and the nobility of his conduct. His heroic deeds were sung long after his death.
His example led many nobles, including his own aunt, to open their hearts to their people.
Gwendan was heartbroken by the Sovereign's marriage to the Emperor but kept silent on his feelings until his death.
It seems his long love was never meant to be.
gwendan_ending.prev: Sir Gwendan remained at the Tower, where he became a wealthy and distinguished knight.

lines: You see Gwendan sitting a little way back, at a table to himself.
That distracted air lends him a very particular beauty.
Yes. But I believe that the role of the Sovereign is one of solitude.
No. The bond I share with my knights is more than enough for me.
But no one would blame you for expressing a certain sense of
.frustration regarding this role that robs you of any normal connection.
I do not miss what I do not know.
You're right. Actually, I think it weighs on me a little.
Guess it's a way of protecting oneself.
No, rest assured. I'm not suffering from it.
After all, a certain difficulty in feeling close to others has sometimes been...a source of real suffering.
Admitting it without fear would save you a great deal of suffering.
But you know, I think things aren't set in stone.
Whether you're a Sovereign or anything else
Nothing is stopping you from...breaking the mold.
Perhaps I am indeed too fatalistic.
Maybe I should start a dating club for lonely Sovereigns?
I'd be curious to see which neighbouring leaders would show up.
He watches you closely, a slight mischief in his eyes, before continuing.
... Don't you sometimes feel that you must uphold some kind of
.boundary with the people who swore an oath to server under your banner?
I am close to everyone regardless of that.
... Indeed. I'd like to deepen certain relationships, but it's complicated.
But no doubt my past and who I used to be certainly play a part.
Feeling close to others has sometimes been...a real challenge.
... Guess I still have a ways to go on that.
I try not to dwell on the past too much.
... I understand... I felt it, too.
But you know, I don't think it needs to be so hard.
It's easier said than done, of course, but
.sometimes, you just have to speak plainly.
Perhaps I shall endeavour to try to follow my own advice.
I fear I am a prisoner of the framework imposed upon me, alas...
You say that as if you only had a limited range of choices available to you...
He observes you attentively, his eyes tinged with deep respect.
... But don't think you can just throw the question back at me to avoid answering it.
Despite my recent accomplishments in Brimwood and the bonds I've managed to form there
.certain old habits always end up resurfacing.
.still struggle immensely to truly open up.
He lets out a slight chuckle.
In the past, my ego served as a shield... very convenient for avoiding any real connection with anyone.
. I find it's my oaths as a knight that are keeping others at arm's length.
... A role that dooms certain relationships before they ever begin.
He's now looking at you intensely.
Talking about it is the first step towards moving past it, isn't it?
. it felt good to talk about it out loud.
The question seems to take him completely by surprise.
It's true that I've had no trouble being myself around you since my return, and.
... You have truly helped me to...find peace...
He chooses his words carefully but the warmth in his eyes towards you reveals everything.
And...you listened to me with such patience and... kindess.
I...didn't expect you to bring up the subject yourself, I must say.
I appreciate you... But my status does not allow me anything more.
A silence greets your reasonable words.
His hand is shaking ever so slightly.
You savour the sensation of his warm palm against yours.
. I had hoped for some time now that you felt the same way. But I hadn't dared to put it into words...
. I would... devote my everything to you.
I'm sorry...but you know I cannot go any further than this.
A long silence greets your words.
That is my wish too, Gwendan. I wish to know you completely.
Your words catch a glint of held-back emotion in his eyes.
Nothing is left but a soft breath caressing your cheek, bridging the few inches that separate you.
He leans towards you, bringing with him his sweet fragrance.
Without a word, you stand up to go and lock the kitchen door. Your status allows it, after all.
You return to Gwendan, who approaches to embraces you shyly and softly.
... His hands reach out to touch your mask with infinite gentleness.
You step back slightly to undo that which hides you from the world.
I'm sorry. I'm not ready. (Keep your mask on.)
Your bodies find their rhythm in a faltering dance until your faces are finally brought together, inches apart.
Your bodies find their rhythm in a faltering dance until Gwendan's face finally finds itself in front of your...mask.
You slowly trace the features of Gwendan's face.
. That roguish look, where the marks of the past have only served to magnify a pure beauty.
His lips draw to yours in a heartbeat.
His lips draw near to...where yours are supposed to be...since you are...once again...STILL wearing your mask.
Lying on the floor, you peacefully watch some dust motes drift down toward you as the light slowly fades in the room.
Gwendan delicate scent tickles your nostrils once again.
... we'll look out for one another, won't we?
No matter what happens, I will be there for you...
You can hear life flowing through the castle and, outside, the birds singing their last notes.
you press a kiss to the nape of Gwendan's neck,

lines: A faint voice reaches you from one of the open doors of the corridor.
[font_size=19]... All eyes on the left profile...[/font_size]
... The left profile inspires confidence, and
Are you lost within your own Tower? Or do you just not know what to do with your free time?
Getting lost in the confined space where you spend all your days requires a certain kind of talent.
I have a few ideas to suggest to keep you busy, if you like.
Why not start by dealing with the deadly boredom that overwhelms anyone who resides within these walls?
... Just a few words of affirmation before heading out to face the world. So I don't forget to shine.
I'd bet my cloak that you do the same before climbing onto your throne, don't you?
Well, perhaps you should give it a try.
Looking at you, it's easy to guess that no one ever bothered to whisper sweet flatteries in your ear when you were young.
I have plenty of words of affirmation for you, if you'd like.
I see the way you look at me.
To be honest, I don't even think you fell in front of me [i]by accident[/i] today. You're following me, aren't you?
I plead guilty...you don't leave me indifferent.
Come now, there's no point in denying it.
I fully understand how you feel about me. I'm rather flattered
A hero of my caliber, with this kind of magnetism, right here by your side?
It'd be borderline inhuman to resist.
?? Are these more of your words of affirmation?
Perhaps you were already dreaming up some absurd scenarios involving myself?
... Unfortunately, I have to stop you right here.
Not that this...admiration isn't absolutely mutual, but let's stay pragmatic. My own admiration for myself already fulfils any need in that department.
There's no need to hide your distress behind that marble mask, Your Grace.
Don't make me repeat it, Your Grace.
Gwendan watches you intently without another word, a tiny glint of pity flickering in the depths of his eyes.
With a heavy heart, you must accept your grim fate... you'll have to live without his love.
Looking for some inspiration for your next song, are you?
N-now then, Your Grace, it is hardly becoming to presume the intentions of such a great arti...
Our Grace  is quite perceptive! My visit concerns but a single question regarding my next ballad's lyrics
. No need to dither with trivialities.
Your advisor seems to mutter something about courtesy being a dying art.
hildegard_omniscience.prev: N-now then, Your Grace, it is hardly becoming to presume the intentions of such a great arti...

lines: ... what a voice... as if it fell straight from the celestial peaks...
He wipes a few tears from the corners of his eyes.
Now, there is a ballad that restores the lyrical heritage of our lands to its former glory.
[i]I[/i] should be the one thanking you.
In fact, I'll give you two free passes for my next recital.
... But I cannot leave this Tower.
Keep your identity shrouded and reveal nothing of it. All may form their own idea of what lies beneath the mask... though some, by convention, will simply refer to you as a man.
