lines: I'd not want my own cheer to overshadow your success.
... I'll not hide the fact that I cannot bring myself to fully rejoice in your recent expansion.
History is rife with tales where victory is often but a prelude to greater torments, is it not?
. Do not rest too heavily on your laurels, Your Grace.
No one knows what perils still lie in wait for us.
You have demonstrated remarkable skill in overcoming the recent challenges you have faced.
I prefer to stick to a contained joy.
But I wanted to convey my sincere hopes for what is to come.
The Empire's threat keeps growing... but I'm certain you'll lead us to prosperity, whatever lies ahead.
. so the Empire of Angelor has decided to cross paths with you.
A confrontation that promises to be tough.
It is perhaps a tad excessive, but I cannot say you are wrong.
Allow me to think exactly the opposite, my dear.
I heard that Arthur Pendragon, son of the formidable Uther, came to you seeking common ground rather than preaching confrontation.
In my humble opinion, Your Grace, he deserves the benefit of the doubt regarding the sincerity of his intentions.
After all, young Arthur only ascended the throne at the age of ten.
He was then but a child full of innocence...
He did not experience his father's tyrannical reign with full awareness.
. but merely suffered its unfortunate consequences.
Therefore, it seems entirely consistent to me that he would strive to move away from what he witnessed as a child.
I find it hard to believe.
I do not have the details of the events, alas.
It would seem that it occurred during the Brimwood Revolts....
His death left everyone stunned, so fiercely did that crumbling old dynast cling to his crown for centuries.
Ah, Your Grace, do have a cup of tea.
A little bird has shared a most interesting anecdote with me...
intendant_finished_investigation.prev: Ah, Your Grace, do have a cup of tea.

lines: We will start investigating at once!
I reaffirm my deepest support to you in this ordeal.
May the Gods grant you the insight needed to unravel this matter.
The dread taking hold of your knights is... concerning.
I fear this atmosphere of terror will end up consuming what peace my people have left.
As if our nights weren't haunted enough already, ah...
What a displeasure it was, Your Grace, to catch the eye of a very old acquaintance within your walls today...
I thought she had been lost in the mists of oblivion.
A woman with whom I traded blows many a time during my years of service as a knight...
I imagine that she has come to offer you her services.
She has indeed joined the Round Table.
Which one of you was stronger?
She is a formidable warrior, though she never quite managed to rise to my level.
She still carries the weight of her failures against me. A bitterness she has never truly been able to shake, you see...
In any case... congratulations on this promising new recruit.
Just try not to offend her too much. Her ego is as fragile as her footwork.
intendant_zolta_recruitment_reaction.prev: What a displeasure it was, Your Grace, to catch the eye of a very old acquaintance within your walls today...

lines: . You have thus provoked the wrath of the Dragon Knight, whose fury had not been felt for many moons.
Do you think my attitude offended him?
You really ought to, you poor fool.
That said... don't take it personally.
The Dragon Knight is a mere contrarian. He opposes you on principle, simply because you managed to open the ancient Tower of Brizh.
It's nothing new. Even during my wild youth, in the days of the Tarascus War, this old fossil was already well over a hundred years old and driven by conservative values.
Believe me, I fear he would have behaved the same way with anyone who managed to ascend to the throne...
I see. A standard skills test.
Not in the slightest, Your Grace.
The advantage being that it's a safe bet he won't hold a grudge, and will accept your rule once you've proven your worth.
...  I did not expect the eternal disputes of our neighbours to come to your attention so early, Your Grace.
I suppose you can't change Gavault's nature, though.
This isn't Gavault's first attempt at insurrection, is it?
That is the least one could say.
The fall of their former tyrant owes everything to the alliance of our two peoples....
After all, their current reign was achieved through revolt.
And we were then their brothers-in-arms in the struggle against their former tyrant.
But any resemblance to recent events remains fragile.
For here, the leader of this revolt met her death without her people ever seeing their wishes fulfilled.
The silence shall only breed further contempt.
This death was accidental. I did not wish for it to happen.
And yet, that is not the story that shall be written in our history, Your Grace.
You're free to believe that if you wish.
Though the revolt has triumphed, I worry to see this young princess taking up the reins...
Mathilda's regency had certainly become stifling, but it was nothing like the tyrant she herself had once deposed.
A woman who sacrificed much deserved a better fate...
But the people made their choice.
I fear this people lives primarily through its past exploits.
I regret the turn of events. Let's hope that the young princess is under wise counsel.
Above all, let us hope that she truly desired this burden.
You chose to nip this revolt in the bud in the most... unusual of ways.
An understandable choice; this princess wasn't ready to rule.
But do her ideals truly belong at your Round Table any more than they did among the people she once defended?
... At the very least, Countess Mathilda managed to avoid the worst outcome.
You chose a pure and simple repression against the noise of revolt.
An understandable choice; this princess was not ready to rule, and Mathilda's rigor bore no resemblance to the tyranny she had once overthrown herself.
You still managed to make Mathilda hear the lamentations of her people.
However, it is unfortunate that the people's grievances were dismissed so quickly.
What else could I have done?
Between black and white lies an entire kingdom of grey, Your Grace.
intendante_gavault_resolution_reaction.prev: ...  I did not expect the eternal disputes of our neighbours to come to your attention so early, Your Grace.

lines: Perhaps you wished to hear some gossip?
Brunhilda jumps up and down, clearly looking for [i]someone[/i].
[font_size=35][wave]I'm your [i]biggest fan!![/i][/wave][/font_size] I've read all your books!!
Brunhilda, Princess of Gavault, and former leader of the Gavault revolt.
This witness's testimony is worthless! Her rebellion was influenced by the defendant's doctrine, which clearly incriminates her!
[i]Calm down[/i], Grandpa, [i]I'm[/i] the one influencing here, not anyone else.
Obverruled. Let us hear what the witness has to say.
. Ewww, I don't get the connection...
These are [i]MY[/i] actions, I started the revolt in Gavault entirely of my own free will, [shake]ok??![/shake]
Not Epicrates, not whatever. Just me and my desire to fight for a better world, [i]slayy[/i].
So I think a bit of history wouldn't hurt you.
Because the Guild has never meddled in other counties' politics, [i]cuties[/i].
Accusing Epicrates of pulling the strings is infantilizing, and if I may, a very [i]cringe[/i] conspiracy theory.
My mother committed this crime, and it's that old crazy hag who should be standing trial!
But what evidence do you have against your mother?!
It's, like, [i]literally[/i] the origin of the revolt, her guilt. Do you think I just act without thinking, or what??

Even contemplating the possibility of Epicrates being the mastermind ofthe revolt is the same as [shake][font_size=26][b]KNOWINGLY DENYING THE PEOPLE OF GAVAULT THEIR RIGHT TO SELF-DETERMINATION!![/b][/font_size][/shake]
[font_size=18]Well, that shut you up good, Grandpa.[/font_size]
She's not wrong, Arlin, you've been really patronizing.
Marian turns to exchange a few words with the Assembly.
I think we have enough information now to reach our verdict.
A service delivered by yours truly, the [i]Queen[/i].
She winks at Epicrates before walking away.
... Well, it's written there, isn't it? When I talk to someone, I always see their name displayed.
I believe we are in the presence of the random member of the peo.
I mean, the person who has been skilfully selected at random to give evidence.
[font_size=18]I've never seen this clown in my life
All these details are just personal anecdotes - juicy, yes, but irrelevant to the investigation!
Don't apologise. More juicy private details, please.
That is indeed inappropriate. Focus on Gavault. *Please*.
... In short, if I had to sum him up in one word, it would be 'innocent'. But not necessarily in a good way.
... OKAY. So let's talk about the Gavault revolt, since apparently riling up the crowd is forbidden here.
After the murder of that noble, people chirped a lot.
They wanted to cut off heads! Rise up against the established order!
But [i]absolutely not[/i] in any political sense. I never once heard Epicrates name mentioned in Gavault.
(In fact, I've never even heard that name in my life.)
Even in his youth, he excelled in the art of villainy.
A textbook case for anyone wondering where evil comes from...
.[font_size=18]the absolute worst...[/font_size]is that this guy is a true home-wrecker!
He broke off my engagement to my dulcinea, Your Grace!
These details, while undeniably juicy, are in complete contradiction with what we know of the witness, Your Grace.
The first time you came to us, witness, you smelled so foul, so pestilent, that the entire village of Milkford spoke of you as a curse.
Under those circumstances, how could you even have imagined getting engaged to anyone?!
Imagining the witness being engaged does indeed seem perfectly absurd.
[font_size=18]... get me out of here, please...[/font_size]
What do you have to say concerning the matter [i]that interests us[/i]... namely Epicrates influence in Gavault, witness?
I think we're missing some more juicy details.
... If I had to sum him up in one word, it would be 'guilty'. But not necessarily in a good way.
[b][shake][font_size=40]OBJECTION Your Hon--[/font_size][/shake][/b] I mean, Your Grace!
This statement is in complete contradiction with the rest of the testimony.
The witness is talking absolute nonsense!
Maybe! But at least I'm telling it with [i]flair[/i]!
He has *clearly* exonerated the accused. Hasn't he?
His testimony was *fairly solid*. Wouldn't you say?
I think this witness was particularly damning in his stupidity.
So blatantly stupid that he could have exonerated the accused had he attempted to incriminate him.
So blatantly stupid that he could have put the accused behind bars if he had tried to exonerate him.
(I can try to do that too, if you'd like.)
We have all the information we need to reach our verdict.
I would like to extend my special thanks to your counsel, who brilliantly succeeded in discrediting this damning testimony.
The frantic look on the face of the man who has just burst in is reminiscent of a rabbit being hunted down from every corner.
Y-Your Grace! I-I... I am Childeric. From the county of Almor.
. second [i]claimant[/i] to the throne of Almor. The throne you are wanting to claim.
And we fully intend to win.
He is dumbfounded, unable to comprehend how anyone could reach the final stage without [i]wanting[/i] to. Is it a stroke of outrageous luck, or a pure masterpiece of stupidity?
W-well... well. In this case, listen carefully.
The thought of one of your knights sitting on Almor's throne seems particularly painful for him.
P-please... listen to what I have to say first.
I-I love Almor County, Your Grace. I am devoted to it. But its rules and systems are...profoundly stupid.
Stupid rules, and this Great Tournament is just the epicentre of them!
Caught up in a strange mixture of anger and fear, he is now gesticulating wildly.
A man of the Empire, that lineage of bloodthirsty madmen, had the audacity to present himself during the first trials!
What will become of us if such a man ever seizes the reins of power?!
O-or... Someone who would be convinced by the words of the Brimwood guild
T-they force their false revolutionary ideas on people
The rest is just paranoid gibberish.
I [i]beseech[/i] you. Let me claim victory, and I assure you that the County of Almor will be your ally, now more than ever.
Send forth your weakest, most foolish, most catastrophic knight of all your subjects to face me in the final trial, and let me win.
BONJOUR! [font_size=30][b]DAMIAN[/b][/font_size]! Official emissary of Mavignac from the County of [font_size=30][b]GAVAULT[/b][/font_size]!
[font_size=30][b]ALRIGHT[/b][/font_size]. I'm here to talk about the murdered Count- Edward. But apparently nobody ever calls him by his first name.
He was a good man. Not like the other toffs. [font_size=30][b]HE[/b][/font_size] really stood up for the common folk like no one else...
When he was killed, it was [font_size=30][b]INCOMPREHENSIBLE[/b][/font_size]
. Why go after a man like that, gentle as a lamb?
And when you learned that Epicrates was suspected of having orchestrated the murder, what did you feel?
And the Brimwood revolt, let's be honest, sometimes gives us something to dream about - us common folk.
I can tell you, there's more than one head here in Gavault I wouldn't have minded seeing sent off to their nobles' penitentiaries.
So seeing a figure like that stoop to such depths by bumping off an innocent man, and a kind one at that....
How can you be so certain of his guilt?
That is not the subject of the current interrogation.
Let the witness develop his thought.
The only word Arlin hears now.
Uh, don't worry, [font_size=30][b]I'M GETTING THERE[/b][/font_size], YOUR GRACE!
I saw the reactions in Mavignac after the murder. All manipulated, all rallying against Countess Mathilda, no evidence, riding the wave of the Brimwood revolts.
Look, I won't lie to you... I know Epicrates' texts well, I always believed in them. But here, his ideas were [font_size=30][b]COMPLETLY[/b][/font_size] twisted.
Before Our Grace cuts us off again, I would like to point out that it's particularly disgraceful to see anyone's name turned into a reference after a barbaric murder!
Well said. Because even [font_size=30][b]WITHOUT[/b][/font_size] hard evidence that Epicrates is behind this murder...
...Seeing the people's reaction, it's hard to believe he wouldn't have tried to pull the strings to spread his revolution elsewhere.
I know our conditions and, of course, I could have supported him, yes
. but murdering innocents crosses the line.
Marian turns to exchange a few words with the Assembly.
A damning testimony, to say the least.
Can you confirm whether, in one way or another, Epicrates writings were used to prepare the uprising?
No doubt about it... people were literally gathering for group readings, when all this started.
... Well, I think we have enough information to reach our verdict.
intervention_damian_brimwood_testimony.prev: BONJOUR! [font_size=30][b]DAMIAN[/b][/font_size]! Official emissary of Mavignac from the County of [font_size=30][b]GAVAULT[/b][/font_size]!

lines: I won't hide from you that the threat of Kingslayer inspires the greatest fear in me.
Nevertheless, my armour of light could be extremely effective against his magic...
Rest assured you can count on me to lead the expedition to crush him to pieces.
Lisel, representative of the people of Chavignol in the county of Gavault.
Was asked to come and talk about Epicrates' influence in our community.
She takes something out of her pocket.
A small piece of cheese emerges, standing tall and defiant.
Its sweet, milky and heady aromas rise into the room.
Here is a strong, creamy cheese made from raw cow's milk that originates from Chavignol. One of our most famous.
Can you guess [i]what[/i] it's called, Your Grace?
Are you just going to talk to us about cheese?!
[shake]What does this have to do with the investigation?[/shake]
Please answer... what is this cheese called?
A murmur of astonishment ripples through the Assembly.
A murmur of astonishment ripples through the Assembly.
All of this only adds to the growing list of clues pointing to Epicrates' influence over your lands!
Epicrates is a symbol, a political figure of struggle.
His name is known in our lands, correct.
But in Chavignol, you see, when people speak of Epicrates, they think first of his [i]crust[/i] before his [i]cause[/i].
True, this cheese has a political past.
but who still knows that in Chavignol?
It didn't grow more popular after the murder.
It remains a somewhat rare delicacy.
I don't see how this exonerates Epicrates of any wrongdoing in the murder case.
I'm here to talk to you about Epicrates' influence, and here's my answer. To us, Epicrates is mostly a cheese.
A cheese that carries hopes, perhaps - but [i]first and foremost[/i], a damn good eat.
As if to prove it, the scents of Epicrates return to tickle your nose.
Thank you for your heartfelt testimony.
This may not be the right place.
Indeed, you may do that in private.
Marian turns to exchange a few words with the Assembly.
So you confirm having had no knowledge of any communication, direct or indirect, between Epicrates and any of your members?
Our exchanges with Brimwood's members have always been sparse.
And most of them have, alas, never had the chance to taste our delicious cheese.
The discussions are lively, and it seems that trade agreements are on the horizon.
... Well, I think we have enough information to reach our verdict.
She walks away, carrying with her the scent of Epicrates.
I would have preferred to get back to you under different circumstances.[/b]
Her calmness was enough to silence the last of the voices buzzing around the courtroom.
[b]You are no doubt aware that I was wrongfully accused of the murder of the Baron of Mavignac. A particularly painful ordeal.[/b]
A murmur of outrage ripples through the Assembly.
[b]Answering the question of what influence Epicrates may have had on our lands is not an easy task.[/b]
[b]The people of Gavault are proud, hard-working folk.[/b]
[b]And, like any proletarian people, they've been shaped by tales of popular revolt - notably those penned by Brimwood in the past.[/b]
[b]But in my view, that alone is not enough to establish any clear link between Epicrates and recent events.[/b]
It is important to distinguish between the political figure Epicrates and the historical event of the Brimwood Revolt!
[b]Is that not precisely what I've just stated?[/b]
This objection does indeed seem somewhat incongruous.
[b]Thus, the mere fact that the story of Brimwood inspires our people is not grounds to implicate Epicrates.[/b]
[b]However, it does seem reasonable to consider that he may have sought to sway my people's opinion against me.[/b]
That suspicion appears quite consistent to me, given that Epicrates and his Guild have never shied away from getting their hands dirty in the name of their principles.
[b]... And, as I have already explained, the people of Gavault are plainly very receptive to revolutionary rhetoric once a spark has been lit.[/b]
Can you say with confidence that Epicrates is the mastermind behind this revolt?
[b]I simply think it would have been obvious for him to pull the strings. It would even have been foolish not to try.[/b]
[b]Furthermore, my authoritarian regency policy has made me a prime target for the wrath of such a revolutionary.[/b]
As the leader of a revolt, do you think she may have been influenced?
[b]However, I also have no evidence that establishes a clear link with Epicrates.[/b]
Marian turns to exchange a few words with the Assembly.
Well, I think we have enough information to reach our verdict.
I have a proposal to put before you regarding the illustrious Dragon Knight's challenge.
He drums his fingers against his hip, visibly impatient.
. Let's get straight to the point...he has something I'm interested in. The dragon.
Do you want to eat it?
No. At least, not to start with.
The sheer seriousness of his reply set against your light‑hearted suggestion leaves you speechless.
... Truth be told, slaying a dragon is my ultimate fantasy. Obviously a modest ambition for anyone who considers themselves a proper hunter.
If I were to set an ambush for the Dragon Knight before he reached the site of the confrontation, I am certain I can bring his creature down with a single arrow.
Thrown off balance, our victory would be nothing but child's play.
Two or three other knights should be enough to see this through.
With all due solemnity, I ask that you place your trust in me for this mission.
He barely seems to be making an effort to mask his disgust.
Sir Tarcus, nobleman from Gavault and brother to the former Count Tarascus. I have come to enlighten you on information surrounding the revolt.
As a close friend of Countess Mathilda, I had a front-row seat to how deeply these false accusations have affected her.
Her little foolish daughter, that [b][shake]idiot[/shake][/b], orchestrated it all to wound her mother. And believe me, she had been completely indoctrinated by Epicrates' fanatics.
This is mere conjecture on the Princess' motivations.
Not conjecture. Fact. It had been discovered that the child's own caregiver had been slipping them the delusional writings of that man when she was still young...
And the more Epicratist texts you consume, the more Epicratist your brain becomes.
So that little fool had already been immersed in those books for [b][shake]years[/shake][/b]! Truly one of her disciples...
I wouldn't even be surprised to learn that this [b][shake]idiot[/shake][/b] was in direct contact with that scoundrel.
Still conjecture with no witness testimony. This cannot be used to prove the defendant's guilt!
What are you even doing, old man? Defending that crown-slayer?
Don't be stupid. We're on the [i]same[/i] side here.
Sir Tarcus. Do you have any witnesses or further evidence to corroborate that these two were in communication?
The little nitwit behaviour completely changed overnight.
She does indeed seem very impressionable.
I have known this scatterbrain since she was a child, Your Grace.
You have the account of someone who witnessed all of this up close, in the company of the noble victims to shed some light for you.
Do you need any more proof than that?
A damning testimony, at the very least.
And what proof implies that Epicrates' writings were used to prepare for the revolt?
Obviously! The princess kept [b][shake]stupidly[/shake][/b] repeating to her followers everything she thought she understood, without ever thinking.
No need to look any further.
Well, I think we have enough information now to reach our verdict.
A shame, I had even more to present on that cheeky little thing.
But I hope you will reach the only reasonable conclusion in light of all of this.
He glares at Epicrates before stepping away.
I may have a proposal for you, Your Grace.
He ignores you and continues on.
His voice grows softer as he moves closer.
The Kutnar clans are nothing but [b][shake]savages[/shake][/b], Your Grace... They say they kill their weak newborn foals at birth.
They don't deserve our participation in this [b][shake]ridiculous[/shake][/b], tournament, though I grasp the political necessity.
Let's turn the odds in our favour shall we?  Make a few adjustments here and there...
Send me to compete, Your Grace, and I will bring you back far more than victory.
intervention_tarcus_county_quest_kutnar_.prev: I may have a proposal for you, Your Grace.

lines: Your Grace... allow me to say that we have here a [shake][b]golden[/b][shake] opportunity. One only the truly wise would dare seize. And I trust we count ourselves among them.
He ignores you and continues on.
The silly girl was [shake][b]foolish[/b][shake] to reveal so much of her incompetency to us...
If her support is weak, now is [shake][b]the time to act[/b][shake], Your Grace.
Send me to intervene, Your Grace. I promise you we will gain more than you could ever dream of.

lines: It seems the Grand Dragon Knight is looking to pick a fight with you, Your Grace.
That man is a fearsome warrior, practically a living legend
. You [b][shake]won't[/shake][/b] defeat him in equal combat.
I'm not sure I want to resort to underhand tactics.
Nothing is underhanded when it comes to protecting our people, Your Grace.
That knight...he's the nanny of some [b][shake]sniveling brat[/shake][/b]. Pathetic, helpless, probably still needing someone to change his [b][shake]diapers[/shake][/b].
A fine bit of irony, considering that little weakling is supposed to inherit the regency of Drakovic...
Here's my idea...capturing this runt will be child's play.

Send one other to aid me with this plan
. and secure the advantage for our side.

lines: Pro tip. Send me after that spectre who threatens you - the Kingslayer. I'll sort him out.
Not that I'm thrilled about it, but.
you know I can't die. And right now, I can't shake the feeling that we're facing a pretty serious threat...
if it'll save lives, count on me to set it straight.
Forgotten and abandoned from everything, the wretched leper was looking for salvation across the old kingdom.
In despair and exhausted, a soft voice echoed in their heart. Beckoning to a distant place.
At the end of their journey, the poor soul finally reached the ruins of the Tower, the last remnant of the once glorious kingdom of Bretania.
Something akin to fate seemed to guide their path to this forgotten place.
At the foot of the Tower, a few nobles seemed to be arguing. Once again, the royal selection had proved to be a disappointment.
The door to the Tower remained closed and the prophecy unfulfilled.
Slipping through the crowd, the stranger reached for the legendary key adorning the giant lock.
In their mind, the words of the prophecy echoed,
"Only the true Sovereign, chosen by the Gods, shall be allowed to wield the silver key to the doors of the Tower."
From that moment on, people called them.
intro_cutscene_final_sequence.prev: Forgotten and abandoned from everything, the wretched leper was looking for salvation across the old kingdom.

lines: One hundred years have passed since the fall of Ermen the Wise at the hands of the impious Kingslayer.
Since then, the White Tower of Brizh has become nothing more than a lifeless relic...
Having lost its fortress, the Kingdom of Bretania once again finds itself under threat from the Angelor Empire...
... Just as it did in ages past.
For centuries earlier, the Empire was already preparing to devour these lands.
After fierce battles, fate seemed sealed and defeat inevitable
... Until, out of mercy, the Gods bestowed
This Tower granted unparalleled strength to its knights and an inexhaustible wellspring of magic to its sorcerers.
But of all these gifts, the most fearsome was that bestowed upon its Sovereign
It was the power to foresee the future.
One hundred years have passed since the people of Bretania have awaited the coming of a new Sovereign... the chosen one who would awaken the ancient Tower of Brizh once more.
... And it seems their prayers are finally about to be answered.
For far from the royal court, in a humble country church, a wandering leper awoke to the sound of flames and chaos...
intro_cutscene_tower_explanations.prev: One hundred years have passed since the fall of Ermen the Wise at the hands of the impious Kingslayer.

lines: We absolutely do not have time for such trivialities!
The situation is serious, Your Grace...
But I am your only knight, Your Grace...
All the others went off to fight...
... Those weren't just rumours, Your Grace.
The [i]Kingslayer[/i] is back, and it is not alone.
It is heading towards us this very moment, dragging an army of the dead in its wake...
His words trail off, as though the Kingslayer's icy hand were already closing around his throat.
... What should we do, Your Grace?
Stay calm and evacuate the occupants of the Tower.
I'll deal with him myself... Leave now!
I SAID GO. THIS IS AN ORDER FROM YOUR SOVEREIGN!
[shake rate=3]You pierced the veil of arcana that no hand was meant to find.[/shake]
[shake rate=3]Only to offer the void a heart already withered and unkind.[/shake]
I know why you are here, but I shall not give in... or the Empire will take us all.
If this is where it must all end, so be it.
[shake rate=3]This holy seat grants your shadow no spark of grace.[/shake]
[shake rate=3]Return to the frigid soil with the rest of your renegade race.[/shake]
[shake rate=3]May the next soul finally prove worthy.[/shake]
Our bakers are running out of wheat.
Use buckwheat instead; it's better anyway.
We'll use our personal wheat reserves to support the affected regions.
Well, guess that'll have to do!
Please forgive me for my slight delay!
Her question ends in a small squeak of panic.
. at the Magical Academy, we might've, hmm
Don't worry, I'm sure we can help.
... We accidentally released one of our poltergeists into the wild.
. He's got a thing against grain, don't ask me why.
You idiots... better find a solution yourselves.
A farming ghost? I've already got someone on it, matter settled.
I'll send someone to exorcise it.
Screams and the crackle of flames surround you, spreading the sound of death.
Through the shattered stained glass, you see armoured figures moving frantically and bearing an emblem that you do not recognise.
A cry of terror rises from outside,
"[shake]Run! The Knights of the Empire are here![/shake]"
You hear one of the armoured figures shout, their voice trembling.
Dense black smoke floods every corner of your dwelling.
You rush toward the entrance, but a flaming wall collapses with a roar and seals off the main exit.
The ceiling groans, releasing a rain of ash... the entire structure threatens to cave in at any moment.
Amidst this blazing chaos, as you desperately search for another way out, your eyes meet those of a panicked cat.
Follow the cat and trust its instincts to find another way out.
Take the cat in your arms and try to jump through the flames of the collapsed doorway.
You miraculously escaped unharmed and the cat seems to be fine.
Just as you start to feel better in the fresh air outside, the dull thud of iron-shod boots echoes around the corner.
A cry, raw with pure rage, tears through the roar of the inferno,
Meow with *precision*. No one can tell you're not an actual cat.
Try to adopt the deepest voice you can, 'IT'S JUST ME, A KID RAN AWAY TO THE OTHER SIDE!'
The knight has turned back and you breathe a sigh of relief as you hear the sound of his boots gradually fading away.
But as you approach to trail him from a distance, you watch in horror as he reaches for a child trying to flee...
Taunt the knight: he should be picking on a leper (you) instead of a toddler *way* stronger than him.
Run towards the child and try to push the knight away from him.
The knight turns towards you and charges, consumed by rage.
He hunts you down for some distance, driving you to flee until you reach the very outskirts of the village.
Find a leper-shaped rock in the forest and hide behind it.
Hide in a field and pretend to be a scarecrow.
This hiding place proves precarious... The knight finds you with ease and blocks your escape.
Locking eyes with you, he raises his arm, ready to strike.
Remove the bandage from one of your wounds and try to trip him up with it.
Try hitting him with a piece of wood.
Your maneuver paid off and your attacker collapses heavily.
Now defenseless, the Empire's warrior lies helplessly at your feet. This is your moment to act.
Smash his skull in with a stone. He deserves it for trying to murder you.
Leave him there and run away before he wakes up.
You run away into the darkness...
intro_sovereign_personnality_test.prev: Screams and the crackle of flames surround you, spreading the sound of death.

lines: We're in a bit of a pickle.
Our wheat stalks are bowed, forced into... strange circular patterns.
Can you lend us a hand?
Ah, a classic children's prank, I know it well. Here's a little royal help.
Must be of magical origin. I shall send a mystic knight.
Thank you, my good Grace! I'll finally be able to rest...
And such was the end of our story...
In an unexpected turn of events, the Sovereign made the unthinkable choice, to surrender, unconditionally, to its invader.
What was once the Kingdom of Bretania became nothing more than another county in service of the Emperor.
Many despised the Sovereign for this choice.
And yet, not a single life was lost in the conflict, and the terms of the treaty proved remarkably generous toward the county of Brizh.
The Sovereign finally found his place as an advisor, entrusted with the Tower in the Emperor's name.
And so, a lasting peace seemed to settle at last.
Unable to repel the forces of the Empire, the Sovereign finally surrendered to his invader.
What was once the kingdom of Bretania is today nothing more than a simple county in service of the Emperor.
Most of the surrounding nations eventually bent the knee before the Empire.
Some, however, resisted - fiercely opposed to seeing their territory fall under its influence.
The Sovereign was sentenced to public execution in the aftermath of the war.
But as the executioner's blade drew near their neck in the final moments, something stirred in their pocket.
kind_ending_cutscene.prev: And such was the end of our story...

lines: A dull magical tension grips the air as the Kingslayer stands before your knight, impassive.
May she emerge from this unscathed...
A dull magical tension grips the air as the Kingslayer stands before your knights, impassive.
May they emerge from this unscathed...

lines: I find myself obliged to announce the end of my service as a knight.
I must admit your recent missions have somewhat dampened my former fervor. I must withdraw before my health suffers any further.
. but you are right. One must know when to listen to their body.
Your validation goes straight to my heart, Arlin, even if I hadn't solicited it.
It has been a pleasure to serve you, Your Grace.
You can always find me at the intendancy, over a cup of tea.
All this death. Friends leaving one after another that have entrusted their lives to you.
. I can't take it any more.
To be a knight... and accept the consequences.
.My heart is not in it anymore.
.just hard for me to keep doing a job I no longer believe in.
. really sure that this choice won't end up weighing on you?
Columbus and I really can't get used to your
I think we'll go back to the Islands for a bit. Have a think about all of this...
... You're officially the worst leader I've encountered in my entire career as a princess. And trust me, the bar was already on the floor.
. Even my mother wasn't this clueless.
Good luck trying to run your little kingdom, I'm out.
knight_leaving_brunhilda.prev: ... You're officially the worst leader I've encountered in my entire career as a princess. And trust me, the bar was already on the floor.

lines: I must leave you now; I have to go and fetch some milk.
I'm gonna lay my cards on the table.
I reckoned I was brought in here to represent the folks back home with a bit of dignity.
But truth be told, I'm startin' to think bein' a knight here is just a slap in the face to my folk.
... With all due respect, I figure I'll be a lot more useful elsewhere.
[shake rate=6]For as mindless as this vessel may be, it can.
His... voice (?) seems tinged with an anger you have never seen in him before.
I perceive that this vessel craves other horizons.
It thirsts for unforeseen stimuli and organic discoveries.
But it here it only feeds on disappointment and the bitterness of a mounting contempt.
knight_leaving_dulahan_human.prev: I perceive that this vessel craves other horizons.

lines: .crawling fear of what you might extract from me.
. You who wishes me such harm.
My presence here is no longer required nor desired.

lines: I believed you to be trustworthy upon this path, my friend...
But now, you have chosen to wound that oh-so-fragile trust.
Until a new path opens up for us once more.
knight_leaving_epicrates.prev: I believed you to be trustworthy upon this path, my friend...

lines: And thus... the hour of my tragic farewell tolls.
I had nourished such lofty dreams of grandeur within these walls, Your Grace...
... But I am forced to conclude that my legend shall be written elsewhere.
Do not take it personally. You simply lack.
the elegance required to deserve my deigning to stand by your side.
knight_leaving_gideon.prev: And thus... the hour of my tragic farewell tolls.

lines: Duty calls me elsewhere, and I find myself compelled to withdraw my blade from your service.
To lose a talent of my caliber is truly heart-wrenching, I know.
By all means, do not stifle your sobs, Your Grace.
But do me the favour of waiting until I'm out of sight, here is my last request.
The young knight approaches to scrawl a few words with a trembling hand.
"[font_size=35][font=res://fonts/font_variations/eu/Quintessential_remappable.tres]I regret to inform you of this, Your Grace.
But your conduct is an insult to the honour of the Virgo Guard.[/font][/font_size]"
You can remain in this shack of a Tower. It would appear you have no interest to [shake rate=20.0 level=5 connected=1]shine as you should[/shake].
... And I would follow suit if I was to stay here.
I'll find my glory elsewhere, Your Grace.
I must be honest with you... I no longer feel I belong within these walls.
I had hoped to escape the shadow of who I once was but it seems that I cannot by your side.
Perhaps trying to reconcile with the past was a futile effort.
Perhaps the only way forward is to say goodbye.
Your Grace...I wish you every success for the future.
. strange. It find myself turning into somethingthat does not resemble me.
And above all, I no longer know why your words were supposed to become my gestures.
this is the standard procedure for announcing one's departure, right?
We will not see each other again.
I must provide you with a brief.
. personal debrief: I no longer feel quite aligned with the core values of the enterprise.
. explore other fiefdoms. To consider new opportunities...
B-but... we can agree on an amicable departure, right?(
A mutual separation agreement would do the trick, [font_size=18]haha[/font_size]).
No. And don't expect any severance pay.
Thank you, Boss! It truly is a relief to know that my nutritional survival is budgeted for the upcoming quarter.
I suppose I'll have to put myself back on the market very quickly, then...
It pains me greatly to come and announce this to you today....
. I believe we need to distance ourselves from each other, Your Majesty.
I've been thinking about this from every angle, but nothing helps.
You know what's good for me.
. I don't know what came over me.
Thank you for your understanding, Majesty!
No, don't turn around...I must be strong...
. surprising decisions, which I'm not quite fond of, I believe...
... that you will have to do without my services.
I'm going back to my village.
. I undoubtedly will be of greater assistance to my people than by indulging in your strange little schemes.
I see I no longer have any place by your side, Your Grace.
I thought we us destined for something greater - the forging of a powerful, dignified, and secure kingdom.
... But I see now your ambitions echo only the weakest, most pitiful rulers these lands have ever known.
knight_leaving_tarcus.prev: I see I no longer have any place by your side, Your Grace.

lines: ... I imagine we won't see him again anytime soon.
I'm taking my leave, Your Grace.
My tolerance for your decision-making has officially reached its limit.
I'm going to find somewhere that makes me feel a bit more... alive?
Honestly, anywhere will do, as long as it's nowhere near you.
What an unlikely error of judgement on my part to have placed the slightest amount of trust in such an insignificant being.
You never knew how to live up to the honor I bestowed upon you. Your little sham of a kingdom is going nowhere... And I certainly don't offer my time as charity to weaklings.
Have the decency to die in silence when the time comes.
knight_leaving_victoria.prev: What an unlikely error of judgement on my part to have placed the slightest amount of trust in such an insignificant being.

lines: I had been quite clear. We play together only under certain rules.
I'll go and offer my services to someone with more... experience. I've never felt so stuck as I have within these walls.
On that note, good luck to you in this world, [i]Sovereign[/i].
One of our inmates at Kralgrun is starting to get on our nerves.
Smug, charming, acting like he's right about every bit of crap he says. Not even our worst kings had a head that big.
This guy is known for taking a swing at one of our top people, so...it reeks of mutiny.
One of my knights will restore order.
Yeah, yeah, not an ally of the bourgeoisie, if possible.
Let's discredit him by staging a fake public confession.
But I'll make sure to enjoy the show.
, handling these kinds of problems ourselves, usually.
But this time, it's a whole different ball game.
. smuggled magic weapons have landed in the penitentiaries, God knows how.
Some of the guys, the worst scum to ever walk the earth, have decided it's time to tear the whole place down.
There's a massive worm in the main Kralgrun mine.
Hundreds of meters long, several tunnels wide...you get the picture, a world-ending size worm.
, some nerds are giving us a headache, beggin' us not to kill it, [font_size=18][shake]grmph[/shake][/font_size]
No choice: a squad's gonna go and crush him.
I imagine a reduction spell should do the trick.
... And how can you know it's not painful for a worm that huge to become that teeny-weeny?
Some lil' ones are trapped all the way down in the bowels of the mine...
The ground gave way right under their boots when they thought they were safe... they fell all the way to the bottom, where the air starts to run thin...
Let's try to bring them to the surface using a pulley system.
Knights will go and fetch them.
We've struck a vein, a real beauty.
A hidden cave, connected to our deep tunnels, bursting with precious metals.
The problem is, we can't just send any old hack in there... need reliable hands to head down into those depths.
you help us clear out the lode, and we split the take.
. 15% for your pocket, 85% for ours. Fair deal, right?
Couldn't we do something like... 40-60 instead?
Forget it, I'm happy with the original deal after all.
? But that doesn't even add up to 100...
[font_size=26][shake][b]GRMPF[/b][/shake][/font_size], 30-70 THEN, you're doing my head in.
... Actually, I preferred the initial deal.
[font_size=26][shake][b]GMRMFGK??[/b][/shake][/font_size] What the hell is wrong with you?
A pleasure doing business with you.
kralgrun_grievance_mine_treasure.prev: We've struck a vein, a real beauty.

lines: These pieces of crap come down from the surface in Mossgart just to stay warm in our tunnels. [font_size=18][shake]Grumph[/shake][/font_size].
Our guys can't even swing a pickaxe without repainting the walls in slime.
Knights will go hunting for slugs.
Oh yeah, sure, since there's no other way to fix this, go ahead and smear the tunnels with mucus for us.
Knights armed with buckets will carry them out of the mine.
Knights will lure them all to the same spot, then seal their grave.
The Tower has been transformed by its divine grace in the wake of your power, my Sovereign.
It is now a little closer to its former glory.
This tower that changes according to my actions... Such magic impresses me.
This edifice was not always the time‑worn relic it has become.
But deprived of its ruler's power for so long, the Tower has weakened again and again.
I recall the moment of its creation... It was such a magnificent monument that its summit, piercing the horizon, seemed to vanish from sight.
A beacon raised to broadcast the kingdom's independence, a flagship whose magic reflected pure strength.
Perhaps you will manage to restore its full splendor, my Sovereign...
Let us walk hand in hand toward that goal, then.
With your support, there's no doubt about it.
I hope I can prove worthy of you, my dear.
"Its creation"...? The Gods built this Tower, didn't they?
That is merely the version that religion has chosen to believe.
The builder of this edifice was a powerful mage who transcended his own limits to raise it.
For this place was indeed constructed by a man, contrary to the religious account that claims it is the work of the Gods.
Alas, it sometimes turned against him.
. Magic that can reshape reality according to the strength of a soul is not something to be placed in everyone's hands.
It became necessary to curb some of the Tower's powers... and to ensure that any future ruler would be worthy of it.
So this place is now less powerful than it once was.
lady_tower_act_2_reached_reaction.prev: The Tower has been transformed by its divine grace in the wake of your power, my Sovereign.

lines: Memories have been flooding back since I awoke at dawn.
As if the Tower's restored radiance is granting me access to even more distant memories.
My father... his face remains blurred, but his voice echoes within me.
Some of his words resound in my head...
I was left here with a purpose.
My father charged me with identifying rightful Sovereigns and guiding them faithfully through the ages.
For a soul had to be consecrated to retain this balance.
... He sealed my body to the stone.
Thus my flesh falls to it, body and soul
. and my presence, at last, is rendered eternal.
I don't remember, my dear Sovereign...
But once I had that body of stone then no doubt I had acquired the sole privilege of no longer physically suffering.
This story has all the makings of a tragic fable, does it not?
. But my father's heart was not evil.
Before he faded away, I recall him telling me that he, too, would become a regulator for the Sovereigns to come.
I know not what became of him, but I suppose his flesh underwent its own metamorphosis to serve that purpose...
In any case, do not be grieved for me.
I don't recall ever having refused this duty.
Had it not been me, it would have fallen to my younger brother.
My father had provided a way for me to reclaim my flesh one day. Should that be my wish.
She pauses for a moment, searching your eyes.
... this gift he left me to break these chains of stone is nothing less than a gift of love.
He wished that only love could release me from my duty, my dear.
Only a kiss of love, sincere and shared, shall set me free.
Her eyes are misty with emotion.
... But of course, such a thing has never come to pass.
And now that my mind glimpses this possibility, I know not if one would ever free me from this fate.
And if I could deliver it to you, my Lady?
She retreats into a stony silence.
The words of deliverance seem to dance before her eyes.
[i]"A kiss of love, sincere and true."[/i].
The words echo in the room and hum in your head.
Could you offer her such a thing?
With her cheeks curiously... flushed (?), the walls of the Tower seem to steadily beat like that of a heart.
She remains spellbound with the thought of what was once a distant hope.
Earlier this morning, I had the unpleasant surprise of feeling the Tower's defence system awaken... However, it did not activate to the fullest.
I could feel it. The [i]murderous[/i] intentions.
Had I not intervened, the results would have been... fatal.
I thank you. But I already knew of this man's intentions.
She falls silent for a few moments, as if tracing... the threads of your assured clairvoyance.
I can't help but notice that you are making.
full use of every [i]being[/i] at your disposal in this place...
I would suggest caution around that "thing" my Sovereign...
... But I am certain that you already have this in mind when wielding such power, of course.
The Tower chose you for a reason my dear Sovereign.
Don't worry. I feel perfectly safe here, thanks to your protection.
Watching over you is my most sacred duty, my dear...
I was horrified to learn of the attempt on your life, having been alerted the very moment the Tower's defense systems were activated.
... And yet, you have chosen to show mercy to the man who sought to harm you.
I must confess, my Sovereign, this troubles me deeply...
This magical "anti-royal assassination" system seems quite effective.
Knowing that I am under your protection, I have little to fear.
Watching over you is my most sacred duty, dear Sovereign.
This man whom you have rightfully cast into the Tower's cells.
. Should I curse his nights, my Sovereign?
I will make sure this man never sleeps again.
No need to punish this poor man any further.
Your kindness knows no bounds, dear Sovereign.
You are only allowed to haunt my nights.
... It is duly noted, my sweet Sovereign.
... I must admit, I am surprised to see that this ancient magic has lost none of its splendour... The protective blessing has survived the ravages of time.
Alas, I fear it is but a fragile shield. Should an army ever lay siege to this Tower to strike at you, this magical rampart would prove a meager defense indeed.
... let us hope you never have to face such a dire fate, my dear Sovereign.
I sensed the formidable Dragon Knight looming within these walls
You were able to "sense" his presence?
Of course, my dear Sovereign. Although it is difficult to pull my gaze away from your exploits...
As the protector of this Tower, I can feel every ripple of energy that passes through these walls.
He once sat at the Round Table during the reign of Ermen the Wise.
What was he like back then?
. a fearsome young warrior, with strength forged through unyielding values.
Under Ermen's rule, I seem to recall that the kingdom flourished.
. But it's hard for me to remember further details.
. a remarkable Sovereign, who unified a realm once plagued by bitter divides.
The shadow his achievements cast was certain to fill his successor with dread. Who could ever hope to equal him?
Perhaps the Dragon Knight feels a certain longing for that era.
... But I have no doubt that you will succeed in proving your worth to him, my dear Sovereign.
I have felt the omnipotence of a shadow I had dreaded seeing appear before you for many moons, my dearest...
Has Uther Pendragon, the Emperor of Angelor, challenged you?
No. Uther is dead. It is his son who showed up.
So, that tyrant has perished... I believed his end to be impossible.
He was already imposing his iron grip upon the lands of Angelor for decades when I faded.
Too many long decades...as if he were gifted with unnatural longevity.
His imprint bears a haunting similarity.
He seemed to have the desire to break the shackles of his predecessor.
Perceiving his shadow does not allow me to discern his intentions.
It is entirely possible that a reign as murderous as Uther's has branded the lineage of Angelor with a red-hot iron, tainting his legacy today.
That despot was guilty of atrocities, my Sovereign... He shed blood far too often, sometimes for mere pleasure.
But let us not forget that our kingdom also experienced periods of calm with the Empire.
A peace that was certainly fragile, yet very real.
That his son now seeks to regain that balance is a perfectly credible hypothesis.
The Empire will always be a threat.
I'm sorry, my dear Sovereign, I cannot enlighten you on that matter.
But you have complete freedom to decide how to deal with this threat according to your conscience.
No matter what happens, you must put an end to this danger one way or another...
Otherwise, the Empire of Angelor will eventually seize the Tower, and
I would never let such a thing happen, my precious.
I have faith in you, my Sovereign.
lady_tower_emperor_reaction.prev: I have felt the omnipotence of a shadow I had dreaded seeing appear before you for many moons, my dearest...

lines: The legendary Lady of the Tower remained a loyal servant of the Tower.
She continued to serve the next Sovereigns of the Tower, forever and ever and ever...
Having returned to her human form, the Lady of the Tower could finally rest from her role as protector of the Tower, and at last enjoy an ordinary life.
The future of the Tower is now uncertain forever... but the Lady is finally free to live a life of love and freedom.
lady_tower_ending.prev: The legendary Lady of the Tower remained a loyal servant of the Tower.

lines: I waited patiently for your visit today.
You know... time is dragging in this crypt.
One might think that it softens as my memories return to me.
but strangely, it is not so.
Those memories of old and the centuries I watched pass from here, a prisoner of the stone, now intertwine in a greyness that chills me...
She stops as if afraid of saying too much.
. Your presence draws me out of it a little.
I believe... I feel strangely closer to you now.
You too live recluded within these walls, captive to an endless weariness, do you not?
Recovering my memories allows me to better grasp the bitterness of such an existence...
It is true. But I have not been here for several centuries.
Confinement has its virtues for me. I try to cling to that.
... but whether one counts the hours or the decades, absolute solitude always possesses that same taste.
A taste that is only more bitter for the soul that remembers...
The soul that remembers always seeks to justify its fate.
My role here is indispensable, is it not?
I have never questioned it, as I already confided to you...
But is it truly out of conviction? Sometimes, I doubt it.
A light dusting of granite slips from the vault and floats before her troubled eyes.
... recently, my oldest memories have been resurfacing.
Fragments of my past life, before I was abandoned here, frozen in stone.
Sensations that overwhelm me at dawn...
Visions that, every night, come to disturb my sleep...
... But it is possible for you to regain that existence.
My curse can indeed be broken.
Yet... it is a prospect that fills me with nothing but deep melancholy.
The granite dust swirls down to the ground with an almost unreal slowness.
... Would it not be a bitter injustice, my sweet Sovereign, for me to be restored to freedom while you remain sealed within these walls?
My condition causes me suffering, to be sure.
. yet it offers me the privilege of carrying this burden by your side until your final breath.
It is the most precious gift I can offer you while I watch over my father's legacy.
Deprived of its protectress... who can say what would become of this Tower?
I did not choose this prison.
but I am still free to choose for whom I accept to wear its chains.
I want what's best for you. And your freedom is the most important thing.
I want to stay with you here forever.
If such is your wish, my sweet Sovereign... then let it be so.
My own desires bow before yours...
And my shadow shall continue to accompany you until your final breath.
From the vault, the granite crumbles endlessly into an impalpable powder.
this mean that mean I'll never experience this sincere, shared kiss of love, right?
The dust rises once more, falling in light cascades that cloud her vision.
... If that is where you reside, I shall content myself with this void.
How can you think such a thing?
Because I love you, my Lady. (Break the curse.)
You're right, it's reckless. Let's just stay sealed up here forever.
In a delicate slowness, you draw closer to her, moving to the rhythm of the swirling granite dust.
You gently lift your mask to gather the kiss of this sweet stone.
. the contact sends an icy shiver through you, soon invading your entire body.
Then, beneath your lips, the stone wavers.
Those once-fixed eyes ignite with a new flame, a muted passion that the rock had kept secret until now.
Slowly, nothing remains but a delicate warmth between your two bodies.
That's how we dressed in my day, you know...
The delicacy of a breath; the caress of air; the scent of crypt dust... One by one, these forgotten sensations seem to awaken her a little more.
How can I ever thank you enough, my Sovereign.
This shameful desire to tear myself away from this stone prison frightened me, but.
you knew how to see beyond it.
Your love has liberated me from my own doubts.
It has offered me the grace to breathe once more.
to wrench myself from the sentence of an eternal solitude.
And the possibility of gently embracing death's release, after all these centuries of memories piling up like layers of dust.
This perspective makes all my memories feel much more peaceful.
I know not what will become of the Tower hereafter, but.
You embrace one another, softly, delicately, in the intimacy of this crypt bathed in a new warmth.
The scent of dust has vanished around her, as if this promise of love had swept away the last demons that still haunted the place.
At last, I awake from my slumber!
Oh, and what a [i]sight[/i] greets my eyes...
A speaking statue? What sorcery is this?
And mine also. Such a beauty in stone.
I am the Lady of the Tower and its protector. I wish you no harm.
I am the Lady of the Tower and its protector. How delightful to meet you.
Long have I watched over these halls. But alas, how decrepit everything has become!
It is not safe to wander too deep yet, my brave Sovereign... Not the welcome you deserve.
However, as I retrieve my powers, I will endeavour to restore your Tower's rooms to their former glory.
Will I be graced to see your lovely face again?
Your presence has gradually begun to return my magic to me. With this I can begin opening new doors within the Tower for you, dear Sovereign.
Now that you've stirred me from my slumber...
Believe me, there are many doors that can be opened.
I shall always be waiting for you here when you finish your day's duties, dear Sovereign.
lady_tower_introduction_dialogue.prev: At last, I awake from my slumber!

lines: I felt a strange vibration today, my Sovereign... like an old echo.
A trace of ancient magic, an imprint that stirred in me an odd sensation.
the feeling I once had of my late father.
Yes... but I'm not truly certain.
Time has blurred its edges, and my memories of him are fading.
I struggle to recall his presence with precision.
. know that my father is the mage who erected this Tower.
You must be really old, then.
The stones that make up this room are far younger than I am, dear Sovereign.
Your father... did he condemn you to remain within this Tower?
So it was he, the man who transcended his own condition to build this place.
My father... I remember he was uncle to a Sovereign... perhaps even the very first to rule these lands.
This monument was meant to be the shield of his kingdom, the foundation of its power.
Yet I'm left with a bitter taste in my mouth.
This feeling that my father's ideals have been twisted, that he eventually lost control of what he himself created.
bitterness hangs heavy in the air today.
I'm sorry...I cannot enlighten you any further.
lady_tower_kingslayer_reaction.prev: I felt a strange vibration today, my Sovereign... like an old echo.

lines: A murder has occurred, right here within our Tower...?[/shake]
She seems to be sobbing heavily, which is rather unusual...for a stone statue.
I'm just as upset as you are...
I'll do everything in my power to prevent this.
I did everything in my power to avoid the worst-case scenario.
[shake rate=4]... Take care of yourself, my Sovereign.[/shake]
Her sad eyes gaze into the distance, lost in thought.
But how can you prevent something that has already happ...[/shake]
She suddenly stops, twisted with anguish.
[shake rate=4]...Take care here, my dearest Sovereign.[/shake]
[shake rate=4]Finding the culprit...amongst [i]your own[/i] knights...What a dreadful task falls upon you, my poor Sovereign...[/shake]
Your words make her tremble even harder.
[shake rate=4]Ah, my poor Sovereign... what shall we do?[/shake]
[shake rate=4]Is it possible that the Tower is no longer a refuge I promised
? That [i]I[/i] am no longer enough to guarantee complete safety?[/shake]
Alas, the destiny of the souls who dwell within these walls may not always be altered.
Dry your... *tears*, stone lady. Everything will be set right.
. I'm Laelle, emissary of the Laik Valley in the Kutnar lands.
She looks at you with great curiosity.
Around here, they say you're all shaken up and that it's the magic of this Tower keeping you alive. Is that true?
Not at all, I'm *perfectly* in my prime.
You're here for the horses, aren't you?
Impressive, Your Grace. At your age, I'd have chosen a coffin more comfortable than that of power.
She doesn't seem to believe any of it.
. At the request of [i]you-know-who[/i], I have brought you three faithful steeds.
The aim was to sell you all three, but
. I must admit, it pains me... I became very attached to them during the trip. You understand?
She doesn't give you time to respond.
First, Gringalet, a thoroughbred, ideal for competition. Unfortunately, Gringalet sometimes tends to...forget that it is being ridden, which causes a few falls. ([font_size=18]Frequent.[/font_size])
Then there's Black Horse, who is... just a black horse. We haven't been able to identify his breed. Nevertheless, it's still fast enough.
Finally, there's Sovereign, a Shire horse that always makes an impression. Women can't help but giggle when they see it. However, it's not a breed ideally suited for racing.
I've changed my mind. I won't be taking any.
Oh, right. Good choice, very good choice.
She actually means, '[i]I wouldn't have picked that one myself[/i]'.
Oh, that's funny. I hadn't made the connection, but he has the same name as you.
Well, Your Grace, I wish you a happy life with your new companion. Our... mutual friend will certainly be delighted.
Oh... Are you sure about that, Your Grace...? [wave][i]Too bad[/i][/wave]...
That's... that's impossible, Your Grace. As I said, I've grown very fond of them and...
I don't care. All three or nothing.

A kind of... stone golem emerged from the depths of the mountain, high above the city. We don't know where it came from, whether it's an invocation or a natural creature, but... that's not the problem.
It is heading towards Naoned, destroying everything in its path, and we have already suffered several major rockfalls that have crashed against the walls of our beautiful city!
There must be a way to grind it into dust.
T-thank you! I knew I could count on you.
naoned_grievance_emergency.prev: This is not good, this is not good, this is not good!

lines: Many individuals have been at the gates of our county since the Great Tournament, and our alliance has piqued their curiosity.
I can't blame them. To behold the homeland of Sir Goberto of Naoned is reason enough for such curiosity, right?
But the gateway is too narrow. Just wide enough for a carriage. And they pile in by the hundreds...
Charge an entrance fee; this will cover the costs of the work.
Here is what you need to do the work.
Oh, yes, it will slow down tourism a bit, but it will make it possible to manage these kinds of cases in the future.
I knew I could count on you, Your Grace.
A giant dahu is wreaking havoc around Naoned wherever it goes.
I thought it was a children's story?
You see, those peculiar goats that roam the hills and mountains, yet only in one direction, as their left legs are shorter than their right.
Of course not. I was informed of his presence as recently as yesterday.
The problem is that it's circling around, and it'll come back at some point to ravage the neighbouring villages. It's been circling around Almor, you know...
Surprise it by calling out from a distance. It will fall while trying to turn around.
I think someone is making fun of you.
Build a wall in its path to stop it.
Capture a dahu with shorter right legs, and make them meet.
Oh, that's a good idea. It will be unbalanced and we can take care of it. Thank you.
... Do you think I'll fall for that? My brother met several of them during his adventures, you know, so I know they exist.
Oh, of course! Why didn't I think of that?
Ah... and they will fight when they meet on the same cliff face?
Naoned is made up of knights of all kinds, and while we love combat, we also have a great love for feasts and therefore ceremonial armour.
We're proud of our armour, but they're not always... [i]fancy[/i].
Do you know any craftsmen who could help us create beautiful yet practical combat armour?
I have a few contacts in the world of haute couture.
Armour should be practical, and nothing else.
Lady Carina will probably be able to help you.
Take this money, and hire the finest craftsman. You have well earned it.
[font_size=18]You ask for nothing whatsoever in exchange?[/font_size]
... As long as they don't make us wear capes or lace.
Certainly. But we... wanted to stand out for once.
Oh, would Lady Carina do that for us? She could easily combine style and practicality, indeed.
naoned_grievance_shining_armor.prev: Naoned is made up of knights of all kinds, and while we love combat, we also have a great love for feasts and therefore ceremonial armour.

lines: We count among our ranks the finest knights in all of Almor.
But they want to become more! We hope you will advise us on how to achieve this.
In time it is our deep wish for us all to become powerful Gobertos! Though admittedly, we shall never match his fiery spirit nor his courage...
What did you observe through my brother's rigorous training regime?
Pull your helmets up even higher over your eyes, like Goberto.
Oh! You're right. That's where my brother's power comes from, after all!
Stop wearing helmets. They only slow you down.
That doesn't sound like something brother would do...
I'll send you some good examples.
Send your men to train in Anveld. It's easy, apparently.
It's true that your knights are the cream of the crop.
Do you know anything about birds of ill omen?
Yes, it's not a bird you might say. More like a dragon.
And many scholars will tell you that they are not dragons either, because wyverns have only two legs instead of four blah-blah-blah. But hey, storytellers do whatever they want.
However they're circling over the city in mass. We don't have much experience of dealing with these creatures around here, and there aren't many people practised in magic.
I'll send a knight to hunt them.
Just scare them off. I'll send you some knights.
Perfect, I will be ready and waiting! I can't wait to see them in action!
Err... as long as they don't come back.
naoned_grievance_wyverns.prev: Do you know anything about birds of ill omen?
