lines: How long is the probationary period?
Your knight is sitting there, energetically stirring his soup with a big spoon.
That is indeed one of the many advantages of the position.
Ah, yes... what a truly fantastic perk, indeed, being allowed not to starve to death.
He shovels a large spoonful of soup into his mouth.
It's a line of work where you're never really sure you'll get a proper meal, after all.
Between small, precarious contracts and quests that come out of nowhere...
Bad experience with your former employer?
I suppose all work has its negative aspects.
. Being a knight isn't worse than anything else, right?
Well, even if not all jobs involve bending over backward for people.
...Well, uh, those are just examples. I'm very, truly happy you hired me.
. one has to make a living somehow, right?
He looks down at his soup.
Bad experience with your former employer?
Don't worry, I'll treat you better.
Y-you already want to give me a promotion?
He seems momentarily unsettled by this suspiciously, professional tension.
... But it must be his imagination.
. I have absolutely [i]nothing[/i] against my old boss in the Empire.
. eh, I wasn't referring to him. [i]Not at all[/i].
. I have absolutely [i]NOTHING[/i] to complain about my time there...
No urgent files we had to finish by midnight, no endless meetings where nobody listens to anyone...[i]none[/i] of that, really.
It was [i]absolutely not[/i] a gigantic nest of vipers filled with petty conflicts of interest and power struggles between colleagues.
I'm not going to go talk to your former employer, you know.
My apologies, I was afraid you were going to request a reference for my next quarterly report.
Let's just say I wouldn't want to seem like I'm biting the hand that once fed me.
He is now stirring his soup awkwardly.
T-to be a bit more transparent.
well, the Empire and its territories have...a rather personal take on team cohesion.
... Almost all the counties distrust each other, but they smile for the portraits and official speeches.
They often say they're like a "big family-county", but between the lines, it's something else...
He nervously shovels spoonful after spoonful of soup into his mouth.
... The upside is that at least they have a nice diversity within the teams.
We get the chance to work with all kinds of people...Sometimes that means accidentally getting stepped on by a giant during a meeting.
His gaze falls on his right foot, as if recalling a painful memory.
That's part of the job, I guess.
With so much experience, you'll be a real asset to my team.
Y-you already want to give me a promotion?
He seems unsettled by this suspiciously, professional tension.
B-by the way... I wanted to apologize for.
. the events during which I was enlisted by the Empire.
I-it led to the burning of the village where you lived, among other things.
. Well, it wasn't my own decision, you know?
It's nothing. I did consider smashing your skull at that moment though.
But you obeyed your orders anyways...
Well, uh... you're right... I guess...
W-We... hadn't intended to start the fires.
. argued with a villager and then...
I'd never seen a job go so wrong before. I decided to quit after that...
But the feelings of guilt didn't leave me.
So I came to you... hoping you could help me repay my debt to the people of Brizh... and ease this burden. One way or another.
D-do you think that's... selfish of me?
It is... So I hope you'll repay us in full.
I think it's pretty noble of you, actually.
.a relief. I'll do my best, Boss.
A little crouton floats on the surface of the soup he hasn't actually finished
You see your knight deep in thought, his nose buried in a book.
He pays no attention to you.
(Squint to try to make out the title.)
You lean forward, back hunched and eyes squinting, with a discretion so lacking that it pulls your knight away from his reading.
. I was doing some technical research.
Part of building up my skills, you see.
You read the title of the book, "[i]Spells and Potions III[/i]."

Then you notice a stack of other books piled on the small dresser beside him, "[i]Five Steps to becoming an Archmage[/i]," "[i]The Sigma Wizard Within You[/i]," "[i]Three Types of Mages in Companies[/i]"...
Scattered notes are also visible here and there, sticking out from various pages.
I didn't know you were such an avid reader.
Actually, it's magical knowledge that interest me.
My main skill, of course, being
You want to become a mage?
. not really within my reach anymore, is it?
If you like, I can recommend a few books of that kind.
Is he expressing a wish or a fear?
He seems to have trouble figuring that out himself.
You sense a hint of regret in his voice.
Great. Keep up the good work.
... But you know, I should probably tell you.
. Well, maybe it's worth mentioning, for your next performance review...
Would you like to practice more?
He responds in the usual weary voice but the glint in his eye is unmistakable.
I was once enrolled at the Great Academy in Moonvale.
The best in all of Bretania.
I had started a course in applied arcanism, specializing in offensive spells.
[font_size=18](well, no, fortunately, otherwise I probably wouldn't have ended up here)[/font_size] I had to stop halfway through.
I needed to send money to my little brother so he could continue his own studies, so...
He lets out a long sigh.
... Between that and my financial troubles, my parents kindly suggested I...get a "real" job.
One that pays quickly and not continuing to study a "fringe discipline."
. a slight feeling of incompleteness about all this as you can probably tell.
I understand. I didn't end up here by choice, either...
He seems somewhat reassured by the fact that you didn't end up in this position of responsibility entirely through your own choice.
Well, that's not exactly what I said.
You don't necessarily need that to perform magic, do you?
Well...let's just say that ever since that dre--uh, that [i]opportunity[/i] was taken from me, the rug pulled out from under my feet...
It's hard for me to see it as anything more than a mere hobby.
And, well, it was the best Academy in the region, you know... I-I'll probably never reach the level I was aiming for.
... Not from books alone. That's for sure...
This Academy offers accelerated programs. You could still earn your diploma.
Y-you'd allow me to do such a thing, Boss?
You have never seen such burning excitement in his eyes - a bonfire that needed only a single spark to be lit.
... A-and it wouldn't be deducted from my salary?
I-I... I'm going to get that diploma, I promise!
A shame. But you can take comfort in this, you're already a very good knight.
oliver_affinity_2.prev: You see your knight deep in thought, his nose buried in a book.

lines: You see Oliver scribbling diligently in his notebook while looking out of the window.
He stops when he sees you approaching.
... Did you know that certain magical rituals can be affected by the weather?
I thought I knew... but then I was surprised.
People often think that performing a pyromancy ritual in the rain is counterproductive, for example.
In reality, this isn't an absolute rule. The ritual's effectiveness depends less on the rain itself and more so on more subtle factors like atmospheric pressure, relative humidity, and cloud density.
High pressure favours the rise of flames and the concentration of magical energy, while low pressure can scatter that intensity, even in dry conditions.
You look out the window. The sky is a clear, bright azure blue. Not a single cloud in sight.
And with this weather, what are your conclusions?
Could you perform a pyromancy ritual today?
Ugh... today, even though the weather's nice, the air density and slightly unstable pressure force me to stay cautious.
So I'll limit myself to a light ritual.
A small flame, let's say...just enough to roast a few sausages?
Anyway, it's wonderful to notice all the little subtleties I learnt in Moonvale.
... Which will surely prevent me from accidentally starting an arson.
But above all, I think I've developed a much more analytical eye...something I used to lack.
After all, many of the internal procedures for mages are passed down only orally...
Pleased to see that our investment has been a wise one.
The most important thing is that you have achieved your dreams.
Your cold analysis seems to trouble him a little.
Perhaps you should wait for the quarterly performance reviews.
(You're revealing the results of my quarterly review ahead of schedule?)
A-ah yes, is that really what you think?
I-is that [i]the most important thing[/i] for you?
He fidgets slightly, clearly struggling with feelings that his employment contract doesn't cover.
You know, professionally speaking... and beyond, I'm truly grateful for everything you've done for me.
This dream, for me, was practically dead and buried.
... And you funded the training, too.
Boss, how can I ever repay this?
Let's say a slight deduction from your salary for a few months.
You should never feel indebted to your employer.
Your smile is my greatest reward.
. But I really thought you wouldn't do that.
[font_size=18]I don't remember reading that in the contract...[/font_size]
I've had so little encouragement from people close to me... it feels strange to realize it was [i]you[/i] who made that happen.
I mean, I don't doubt you, but... who would've guessed that work would end up being my source of fulfillment, really?
. not that I've been unhappy at work, mind you, [i]I love it[/i], but.
He trails off in his explanation.
His eyes seem to dart to every corner of the room. His mind clearly racing.
Is this just some cruel game for you?
Or... could it be that your sweet words in his ears are only the product of his imagination?
And above all, is it...really reasonable to give in to such words, in this strictly professional setting?
while your disarmed knight finally manages to voice his brave response:
I like seeing you smile too, well.
[font_size=18]not that I've ever seen your smile beneath that mask, but[/font_size]... I like the idea.
A-after all, what could make an employee happier than seeing their boss pleased, right?
oliver_affinity_3_mage.prev: You see Oliver scribbling diligently in his notebook while looking out of the window.

lines: Hello. Do you finally have any vacancies?
A-ah, I see. And so you called me just to tell me that in person. Clever.
oliver_come_back_later.prev: Hello. Do you finally have any vacancies?

lines: In search of new professional opportunities, Oliver decided to devote himself fully to sorcery. His talent there became legendary.
He eventually took the reins of the Moonvale Academy, and proved himself an exceptional teacher.
His students, however, often complained of his sometimes too.
Oliver attempted to find other professional opportunities - to no avail.
Having failed to secure anything better, he ended up remaining a Knight of the Tower, long enough to build himself a decent retirement.
He is also said to have become the author of a personal development programme for broken hearts.
. inspired, it is whispered, by an unrequited love from his youth.
oliver_ending.prev: In search of new professional opportunities, Oliver decided to devote himself fully to sorcery. His talent there became legendary.

lines: The sky is a deep blue today.
Only a few clouds pierce the edge of the horizon.
A herbal smoke, tinged with sage, drifts through the air.
The drifting smoke brushing against your nostrils comes directly from the reed pipe he holds between his fingers.
It's...a mix of sage and dried lemon balm.
No, thank you, I'm trying to quit.
You sit together on a small stone bench nestled among the flowerbeds.
... At the Empire, actually, on duty, only smokers get proper breaks...so non-smokers end up missing out a bit.
He takes a long puff from the instrument he twirls between his fingers, then hands you the reed stem.
He takes a long puff from the instrument he twirls between his fingers.
With habit... I feel like I enjoy my breaks less when I don't have this.
You take a puff of the herbal blend in a small breath. The scents of lemon balm and sage brush against your tongue.
I had managed to quit for a little while, but... with my recent exams, the stress came back.
[font_size=18]And when it's not that, it's coffee...[/font_size]
And everyone smokes at the Moonvale Academy, so...well...
Students need to let off some steam, after all, right?
... In the end, I started smoking again a little before my final theory exam.
A second puff, and you hand the small instrument back in a languid gesture.
Oliver's face melts for a moment into the pale blur of smoke, before its features sharply come back into focus under your eyes.
... Anyway, I didn't feel the urge to smoke when I first arrived here, you know.
You've got to admit... it's still much better here than in the service of the Empire.
The smoke escapes from his lips in thick, milky clouds.
I imagine your job at the Empire didn't help.
The smoke catches you off guard and makes you cough for a moment, distracted. You hand the pipe back to him without a word.
The Empire forced you into a certain...pace, huh?
Have you always been prone to stress?
I understand... smoking also helps me with stress.
I suppose with your role... making decisions non-stop all day...just thinking about it makes me quite agitated.
And you've never found... anything else to help with your stress?
... As far back as I can remember, I've always been someone...rather stressed.
My parents said I cried over nothing...and I could already feel that tension rising before certain days...
Like a...trembling inside me, you know?
He hands you the small instrument again, and you take another puff of the herbal smoke.
He takes another drag from his pipe, lost in thought.
But well, is there always a reason?
Maybe I was just...born this way.
Let's just say that at the Empire... they quickly realized I was effective, especially on... slightly longer missions.
My curse, you see. Too good for them to let me rest even a little.
He chuckles lightly, then coughs a little.
But I couldn't afford to cut corners on my work.
So... I was away from home almost all the time.
.was exhausting. I did it for my family, but over time.
. I barely got to see them anymore.
A-and the stress settled in as a habit, until I couldn't even sleep...
The herbs in the reed pipe have burned completely, and the last embers fade slowly in the heart of the stem.
Around you, the smoke spreads into a vast ocean, rippling under the caress of the rays of sunlight.
... A-ah... I have to admit that.
someone helped me a lot with this,
When that person was near me, everything seemed to calm down.
My trembling would almost disappear just in their presence, you see?.
B-but I think I've always needed... something, or someone, to...keep me steady.
A sad smile fades across his lips.
I don't see that person anymore, today.
... It's difficult to function alone, isn't it?
Recognizing this is already a step forward.
... I guess... I still have quite a way to go.
But I feel... well, I think...saying it out loud helps a little... like it lets you get rid of it somehow.
. have the habit of talking like this.
You know... I could listen to you talk like that all day long.
A bright flush colors his delicate cheeks in an instant.
Your words seem to trigger a whirlwind of conflicting feelings in him... emotions he finally seems ready to let show.
I believe you have touched me more deeply than anyone else ever has. I had to tell you that.
... The sharp hesitation in his words shifts into an awkward mix of tenderness and gentle panic.
His voice drops, and in his eyes seems to shine a passion held back for so long-a passion born from those hours spent passing each other in the corridors without a word.

A passion that grew in the silence of your coffee breaks, colored by stolen glances, a passion kept behind stacks of files and quests reports, nurtured by every time he hesitated to speak to you one-on-one.
I thought...that...your words, your attentions toward me, were... just my imagination...
You're probably right, it's not reasonable. And it breaks my heart to admit it.
To hell with company rules... I love you, Oliver.
Each word seems more painful than the last.
Maybe in another context... we could...
A silence heavy with mutual understanding wraps around you.
The rays of the sun warm your faces, while the final wisps of smoke that surrounded you fade away gently, leaving a soothing calm.
At your words, you feel everything he had held back finally daring to burst in his chest.
He presses himself against you, seeking the comfort he had never dared to ask for before.
... The gardens are quiet at this hour, aren't they?
You inhale the delicate scents rising to your senses, his head pressed against your neck, the softness of his hair against your skin.
After a few minutes, he gently takes your hand and invites you to follow him, seeking safety in a secluded corner of the gardens, away from the world.
Your refuge lasts for hours here.
The sun, a silent accomplice to your whispered exchanges and caresses, slowly sinks toward the horizon.
... I want this moment to last a little longer...
His voice is no more than a whisper.
[font_size=18]... and if someone comes looking for us, we'll just have to say it was.
The last rays of the sun warm your faces as you seem to see the final wisps of smoke, though long since dissipated, gently fading away around you.
oliver_full_romance.prev: The sky is a deep blue today.

lines: The man standing before you brings with him a breeze heavy with mineral and dry scents, a mix of damp reeds and resinous incense.
Your nose, your eyes, your senses take a few minutes to acclimate to this new wind, and to recognize its nature.
But that's exactly it... your former awkward, timid knight is gone, replaced by a calm...and fragranced stranger.
I must say that I feel above all... more fulfilled.
I-I hope that's not a problem, Boss.
Conclusion: he has indeed changed, but in a perfectly reasonable way.
T-thanks... guess that's the smell that wafts through the halls of the Academy.
Conclusion: his scent has indeed changed, but not his knack for getting embarrassed.
That's right, I've officially received my magic certification from the Moonvale Academy.
And by far...my teachers nearly fell out of their chairs when they discovered I'd neglected this discipline all this time, even though I had "all the skills."
... But thanks to your encouragement, they've finally found their place.
From now on, I will be your most loyal mage, Boss.
... Are you familiar with sirens, Yer Grace?
Those mythical creatures, half human, half fish?
Birds with women's busts, singing to intoxicate sailors?
Those bloody alarms that wake me up way too early in the morning?
Those flying she-devils. They've nested on one of our lighthouses. We'd like to move them along, but their songs are.
Do you have any seasoned knights that are not men?
Nothing prevents women from falling under their spell too, you know?
I'll find someone immune to their powers.
pince_harbor_grievance_avian_siren.prev: ... Are you familiar with sirens, Yer Grace?

lines: What do you mean, a [i]HYDRA[/i]?! How can you be so calm?
Unfortunately, her mother was found in our nets, killed by a beast from the depths. We found the little one with her.
I know scholars who are well versed in marine fauna.
I'm sure your merchants will...find a use for it. (In someone's stomach).
I'll commission scholars to assist you.
... I-I understand... right away Yer Grace.
Oh. Thank you very much. [font_size=17](We'll be able to take proper care of this little cutie).[/font_size]
... Well... [font_size=17](small may not be the right word...)[/font_size]
. drawn to the carcass of a whale that washed ashore a few days ago.
It's risky, but I'm sending you some knights.
Let them be. Don't touch the biodiversity.
A giant fricassee? With a big party for all of Southbay?
Domesticate them and train them to fight. It'll be good for tourism.
Make a large barrier of salt. They hate that.
... Well, it gets complicated when the biodiversity comes and pinches your toes.
We're going to need a lot of butter given the size of these things...
... [font_size=17]well, I suppose it will bring people to our beautiful little port.[/font_size]
It'll cost us a lot, but it's possible.
We've got some strange pirates who've arrived at the dock.
PIRATES?! How many men do you need?
They...arrived at the docks. Went into the first bar. Tasted our crepes with a bowl of cider.
. And since they liked it, they decided to steal our recipe.
Some knights will sort this out with a few slaps.
I'll send a few knights over to negotiate.
Invite them to your crepe parties.
Oh... er... go easy on the slaps, will you?
... If we get our recipe back, that's fine by me.
Oh. We could invite other people from around here, too. Friends from Shellington.
... The regional alchemy tournament in Pinemaze is fast approaching.
This year, some of our people decided to open registration to "allies" of the Council of Mages, as if we didn't have enough on our plate already.
Would it be possible to send a scholar *and* a knight to represent the people?
Why don't they make themselves at home whilst they're there?
Whoever you send, make sure they are skilled in [i]alchemy[/i].
There's no point in wasting our time with a mere [i]wizard[/i]...
pinemaze_grievance_alchemy_tornament.prev: ... The regional alchemy tournament in Pinemaze is fast approaching.

lines: ... A Bicorn is spreading terror in Pinemaze.
This cursed creature seems to be targeting attacks on our most capable women as it is completely ignoring any of the men.
My knights are already on their way.
We can easily deal with such an insignificant pest.
... What we need are investigators to find out who sent this beast.
Someone seems to harbour a particularly deep grudge against our witches.
I'll send a knight and our best oracle.
All you get in response is contemptuous silence.
pinemaze_grievance_bigorn_feminicid.prev: ... A Bicorn is spreading terror in Pinemaze.

lines: ...The latest whim of the Council of Mages is sure to delight you, Little Sovereign.
Our Archmages would like to invite your "people" to the next Magic Council of Pinemaze.
Of course. We have much knowledge to share with the council.
I'll send a representative of our mages and a knight.
I'll send a representative of our nobles and a knight.
Let's hope that at least one specimen in the batch is gifted with intelligence.
pinemaze_grievance_council_diplomacy.prev: ...The latest whim of the Council of Mages is sure to delight you, Little Sovereign.

lines: It's as if it stopped flowing... yesterday... or has it been many moons?
An invisible cataclysm seems to have warped the very heart of what keeps our woods alive...
... I hate to admit... but we'll need all your best mages to have any hope of warding off this curse.
We may well need your "help", Little Sovereign.
A gargoyle has taken up residence in the Morpint forest.
We are usually quite capable of dealing with this kind of inconvenience.
. Alas, the beast chose the week of the Avalon Broomsticks Tournament to invade us.
Why aren't *we* invited to the Broomsticks Tournament?...
All you get in response is contemptuous silence.
... I'll send knights and people from Grest. They know a lot about gargoyles.

lines: ... The deepest marshy cave in Pinemaze is currently home to an absurd concentration of will-o'-wisps.
And this pit draws in fools like a magnet. That idiot Ursula got herself lost there as a child, if you need a benchmark for the level of intelligence it attracts.
We now have a surplus of exceptionally stupid will-o'-wisps tainting the vibrations of our woods.
We could, of course, eliminate them ourselves, but we simply don't feel like it.
My knights will exorcise them all with coarse salt.
If Ursula know this cave well, I'll send her.
With a bit of luck, maybe she'll say hello to me.

lines: [rainbow freq=1.0 sat=0.8 val=0.8 speed=1.0]How dare you?[/rainbow]
[rainbow freq=1.0 sat=0.8 val=0.8 speed=1.0]How dare you?[/rainbow]
[rainbow freq=2.0 sat=0.1 val=0.8 speed=1.0]How dare you?[/rainbow]
[rainbow freq=3.0 sat=0.3 val=0.3 speed=0.3]How dare you?[/rainbow]
A Leviathan has attacked the island.
. Usually, we're prepared for this kind of situation.
We fought it at sea using a protective artefact, but it wounded us and caused our ship to run aground in the depths of the ocean...
The Leviathan is regaining its strength in order to unleash a devastating tidal wave. Help us stop it before it's too late... the island won't be able to withstand it!
(Shh... it's alright, sweetheart, I know [i]you're[/i] a real griffon.)
Across all of Popota, griffin eggs are hatching...
and what emerges are these cursed legged serpents!
Iguanas? Turn them into sea mounts.
I will send someone to help you identify them before they hatch.
Make an omelette with the remaining eggs.
Merchants will discreetly infiltrate the black market to find the stolen eggs.
... it won't bring back our stolen griffins...
(... look, sweetheart. Maybe we'll be able to find some of your brothers and sisters...)
Her eyes are piercing like those of a bird of prey. And yet her tone is perfectly monotone.
It's the hatching season for these cute little creatures. Under the repeated pecking of these future little cuties, dozens of eggs will crack open.

Treason it remains. I must banish you from the Tower.
I cannot ignore your noble intentions. You shall be pardoned.
An eye for an eye. Murder shall be met with death.
But it will cost me dearly to be forced to leave my

...Let us resume the audiences of the day, Your Grace.
...B-but no doubt justice demands... a blood price for a crime of this magnitude...
... I suppose it's an ending worthy of a tragic hero.
He is escorted away by your guards.
. I-I suppose that some may find some peace with this resolution.
...At least Your Grace shall be sleeping well tonight.
I suppose...this was the right outcome.
but perhaps we'll finally be able to put this tragedy behind us...
You wished to discuss the results of my investigation into the murder in our private quarters?
I'd very much like to know what exactly is bothering you about the way I handled your little personal requests, Your Grace?
Go on, I'm ready to clarify anything.
You presented testimonies from knights who... contradicted them.
You claimed to see magical traces when there were none.
It seems that you have destroyed some evidence.
Am I  held responsible for the sudden bouts of amnesia from the other fools in this Tower?
Listening to you, one might think you were the one who conducted the investigation.
Which makes me wonder why you wasted my precious time with this stupid request.
And these destroyed pieces of evidence, are they in the room with us?
You wanted to see me, Your Grace?
Hmm. And may I have the privilege of knowing what this is about?
. you are aware that a murder recently took place within the private quarters, aren't you?
The findings of the knight we sent to investigate
. point to you as the culprit.
That's ridiculous. What do you have against me?
And we'd like to ask you a few questions to clear this up.
I'm dying to hear what absurdities you're basing this on.
He practically spat out those last words.
Your name comes up in several testimonials.
You were particularly noisy the night before the murder.
There is evidence of your presence at the crime scene.
And I suppose all the fools living here must be believed on their word alone?
And how does that constitute [i]proof[/i], exactly?
Is it forbidden to suffer from insomnia now?
Does the idiot who conducted this investigation realize that this Tower is also my place of residence?
I fear this is leading nowhere, Your Grace.
Perhaps you should consider another method.
Your behaviour only makes you seem more guilty.
Please tell me the truth. We can find a solution.
I just want to understand what happened.
If it suits you, declare me guilty and let's be done with it. But stop bothering me.
Your sugary airs won't work on me.
I just want you to stop insulting me and accusing me falsely.
I can show leniency if you tell me what happened.
No justice is possible if you aren't honest.
He seems to be weighing the pros and cons.
If that's the only way to end this circus...so be it. But know that it costs me.
. I'd have preferred not to speak of it at all.
Know that for several nights now, my sleep has been troubled by... a [i]voice[/i].
But those incessant whispers followed me right into my bed.
And on one such sleepless night, as I wandered through the private quarters...
I realized that I heard this voice very clearly through the keyhole of Sir
I realized that I heard this voice very clearly through the keyhole of Lady
They threatened me, mocked me, described me in an odious way
. And I believe I lost my footing.
Of course I knew that voice was not rational...
But imagine the state I was in. I even pushed past the deep horror the murders inspired in me, just to try silence it.
In hindsight... I think there was something magical in it.
... That's it. I have nothing more to add.
This remains a serious betrayal. You'll be banished from the Tower.
... This is a serious offence. But you were being manipulated. I pardon you.
I am more than happy, then, to leave this kingdom that condemns an innocent without a shred of proof.
And you have nothing against me. No motive, no alibi, [i]nothing[/i].
He speaks true. It is rather...frustrating not to know more.
I'll give you one last chance to explain.
Your words have hit him hard. He stands there, frozen.
Your guards step forward and hasten to drag him out of the room.
I suppose... that a threat has been averted.
He stops for a few minutes, unsettled.
scriptedquest_traitors_plot_3_gwendan_mu.prev: You wished to discuss the results of my investigation into the murder in our private quarters?

I refused the investigation because I'm the one who killed

. But that voice...it sounded like someone really, [i]really[/i] dear to me.
At first, it was even kinda comfortin'.

... And then it started comin' back every time I got home from a rough quest, completely drained.
What kind of things have you started hearing?
Isn't important for the rest of the story.
But at least let me finish.
. It started talkin' a lot about

And above all, it kept paintin' her as a true enemy of the people.

She seems to shiver at this mention.
.all of that just completely got into my head.

To the point I couldn't sleep anymore.
I don't even know why I ended up listening to it.
My apologies. I should have realised that something was amiss.
You can see it that way, yeah.
Gotta admit, I thought I was tougher than that... harder to mess with.
It's not like I'm great at showing that kind of stuff anyway...
... And in the end, the responsibility's all mine.
I need to know who that voice belonged to.
(Insist) Could this "voice" be linked to the people?

... Don't exactly feel like sayin' more.

... Anyway, that's why it sounded so convincing to me...

... Now that you have this information, what is your wish?
The charges are serious. You must be banished from the Tower.

... No need to spell it out. Honestly, my mind was already made up.
Had no intention of staying here after doin'

But honestly, my mind was already made up.
She leaves the courtroom hurriedly without making a sound.
By the Gods... She's already gone...
But honestly, my mind was already made up.
I can't stay here, not after doin'
And the fact that some occult voice managed to slip inside this Tower's walls
. yeah, that's not exactly comforting either.
You'll achieve more for the people here than you would anywhere else.
She seems to be in the midst of an internal debate.
you're a ruler who genuinely cares about their people. That's rare enough to deserve credit.
Don't count on me to stop feelin' guilty about all this...
She thanks you with a glance, then disappears.
She leaves without saying another word.
But... I suppose that this prevents any threats whatsoever.
It looks like things didn't go quite as planned, Your Grace?
So you chose to use my powers but to do nothing interesting with them? [shake]Curious...[/shake]
You encouraged me to use your powers to prevent this death!
[i]Me[/i]? I would have done such a thing?
Oh, no, Your Grace... you're just looking for a scapegoat.
[i]Me[/i]? Do such a thing? Oh, no...
Using my powers doesn't exactly give you permission to fiddle with destiny as you please
. Without proper information, or at the wrong moment, you might miss some options.
Perhaps you could have saved everyone if you'd taken the time to investigate properly... or come back at another time.
There's only one way to find out, isn't there? [shake]Ehehe...[/shake]
In the meantime, your little favourite was saved, weren't they?
I am utterly appalled to see such scheming take place in our beloved Tower, Your Grace
. Who can one still trust in this wretched world?
If [i]only[/i] there were a way to reverse the course of fate...
You were clearly supposed to ask a question.
[i]How[/i] did I not think of that myself?
A little temporal somersault might help you change things.
There's only one way to answer that uncertainty, isn't there?
But the throes of fate are patient.
Peer carefull before making a move... and give pause for the right moment to intervene, or else disaster will be inevitable.
Eager as I am to see what you will do, how can you change anything if you haven't changed yourself?
scriptedquest_traitors_plot_demon_quest_.prev: It looks like things didn't go quite as planned, Your Grace?

lines: .You didn't manage to find the culprit in this line of destiny.
But fortunately, you can have a second chance.
You want me to use your powers, don't you?
Things are going very well for me as they are.
Except, of course, to spare you a grief you could easily do without.
Which is...surprisingly possible by using my powers. [shake]Ehe.[/shake]
. Well, nice for the knight who perished in that line of destiny.
Your Grace, you have only one thing to do to try again.
And perhaps it will allow you to avoid such unnecessary death.
Well, you've managed to unravel this intrigue, Your Grace. [shake]Ehehehe[/shake].
Well, you've once again managed to unravel this intrigue, Your Grace. [shake]Ehehehe[/shake].
Though I do wonder about your motivations for continuing to kill your knights.
You do know there's an option where [i]no one dies[/i], don't you?
You're still trying to persuade me to use your powers.
Things are going very well for me as they are.
. Don't you think that with the killer's identity in your hands- things could turn out very differently?
I only wish to ensure you don't leave fate too cruel, when you already possess what you need to bend it to your will - [i]me[/i].
. Well, I'm not so sure the dead would agree.
Whatever you decide, my only goal is to elevate you to the greatest of powers, Your Grace...
It would be a shame to deprive yourself of that, wouldn't it? [shake]Ehe[/shake].
Well, my congratulations. You've finally unraveled this intrigue, [shake]ehehehe[/shake].
A shame that it's not enough to bring your knight back...
A shame that it's not enough to bring your knight back...
I found some elements of the culprit knight's testimony *rather* suspicious.
... By any chance, do you have anything to do with this whole thing?
I truly don't see how I could have encouraged [i]anyone[/i] to do [i]anything[/i]...
I'm just a humble demon stuck inside a lock, after all.
. who ardently wishes for your well-being, Your Grace. [shake]Ehehe[/shake].
Nothing would please me more than to offer you a way to avoid suffering the death of your little favourite knight, of course.
How could one doubt that syrupy voice?
Are you trying to get me to use your powers?
[i]Me[/i]? Oh, no, you are attributing very guilty intentions to me...That makes me sad.
Now that you know the name of the culprit in this line of destiny, preventing this murder should really be a piece of cake... if you head back to the right moment.
But of course, you're free to make your own decisions.
scriptedquest_traitors_plot_demon_quest_.prev: Well, you've managed to unravel this intrigue, Your Grace. [shake]Ehehehe[/shake].

lines: The air seems to thin the moment this woman steps in front of you. Her gaze heavy and icy with contempt.
Intimidating doesn't begin to cover the aura she is emanating.
But somehow (with something approaching heroism) you manage to say...
Victoria. I was waiting for you.
How could such a fragile little bird,imprisoned in its cage with no view beyond the bars, have sensed my presence?
Well then, little bird, you must know that I am looking for a wretched insect, a stray mosquito wandering on your lands.
Who would have thought that such an impotent Sovereign could have some bark?
Great Knight of this kingdom and all surrounding realms.
It is a [i]pleasure[/i] to finally meet you.
And be close enough to cut your throat with ease.
This recklessness will cost you. You can't do anything to me here.
Don't you think it would be exquisite to perish between my fingers, like a little fledgling whose suffering is tenderly put to an end?
You're safely tucked away in your gilded cage, little bird.
... Anyway, that's not why I'm here today.
You almost succeeded in making the sweet idea of seeing your life slip through my fingers unpleasant.
I'm hunting down a criminal I almost had within my grasp.
A wretched little insect, a mosquito that's wandered onto your lands.
Have you seen a miserable wretch of that sort?
A pitiful mangy thing to whom I've already had the courtesy of tearing off an arm?
(Lie) I don't know who you're talking about.
Yes, I saw him. But I don't know where he went.
Indeed, I saw this man. He found refuge here.
You have no authority here. What occurs on this land is not your affair.
an attitude befitting a worthy Sovereign.
. I couldn't care less, truth be told.
. I'll have no trouble finding its trail again.
I was simply putting you to the test, in truth.
I have no interest in a pitiful insect that has already flattened beneath my boot.
. [font_size=18]This woman has us completely in the palm of her hand.[/font_size]
If we let her leave she could pose a serious threat.
Would a knight of your caliber agree to join my Round Table?
I shall grant you the mercy of death through honourable combat.
And here I thought you were a sickly little bird.
Turns out you're actually a tiny chick with suicidal tendencies.
Honourable commbat? Your knight will be ground into blood and dust.
Then I'll return to eviscerate you in the dead of night whilst you cling pitifully to your crown for protection.
You voice this desire, while I'm still wondering whether you even deserve the grace of my gaze.
Would this pitiful Round Table you claim to rule be even worthy of just [i]one [/i]of my fingertips?
I know how you defeated the great Dragon Knight by kidnapping his defenseless grandson as bait, then struck him down from behind like the coward you are.
I know how you betrayed that backward little princess of Southbay and how you seized control of her lands while she whimpered for your help.
I know of your cheating in the Kutnar Derby and how you coldly poisoned your opponents to win. Those poor souls sacrificed upon the altar of your petty, sordid victory.
I know what transpired during the Enberg trial. How you tortured those innocent people with such chilling ease, all to extract the merest whisper of information about me.
You are aware that your reputation hasn't gone unnoticed?
Oh, I know you well... The [i]little[/i] well‑behaved Sovereign. Upright, spotless, neatly folded to fit into the mold.
[shake][font_size=35]A craven creature incapable of the faintest spark of boldness.[/font_size][/shake][/b]
... It won't be easy to convince me, little bird.
. how thrilling it would be to watch you struggle for the sole purpose of proving your worth to me.
In my grace, I might even allow myself to be moved.
So much so that if you meet [i]a few[/i] of my demands
I shall consent to join your Round Table.
. But convincing me is no simple task, little bird.
I wish to discover just [i]how far[/i] you're willing to go.
How far you will stretch those boundaries simply to prove your worth to me?
And I shall agree to join you.
... I won't hide the fact that following these little adventures has been rather thrilling.
But I shall require a [i]bit more[/i] before I'm fully convinced.
and I shall agree to join you.
What can I do for you?
A teeny tiny favour, my dear
... Tear off your advisor's royal attributes with your bare hands and make him choke them down.
I shall return to you with my instructions.
In truth, the pitiful creature who came to you is merely a mercenary, some wretched thing who peddles his blade for spare coins.
He proved to be appallingly incompetent to such a disgusting level.
Since the rat is hiding in your walls, it shouldn't be too difficult to catch, should it?
We will take care of him properly. Within our walls.
(Lie) We'll take care of him. (Fake his death.)
No matter where that rat is hiding.
We'll take care of him. (Inside the Tower.)
We will search for him at his mercenary camp and execute him in public.
We will discreetly eliminate him at his mercenary camp.
(Lie) We'll take care of him. (Fake his death.)
You really did try to take me for a fool.
[font_size=32][b][shake]Poor, poor pathetic little bird, so blissfully unaware...[/shake][/b][/font_size]
