I still had a few doubts
That wretched mercenary whose fate I placed in your hands
Those pathetic insects you were meant to eradicate
. [font_size=32][b][shake]Did you truly think you could dupe me with a fabricated demise?![/shake][/b][/font_size]
You could have accomplished great things at my side...
But you chose to make yourself pathetically insignificant.
Shut up. You're a knight in my service now.
Unfortunately for you, this place doesn't allow for the correction I would have so dearly loved to give you...
But fortunately, I was able to find my comfort elsewhere.
With stiff, mechanical steps, your knight comes to stand at Victoria's side.
With stiff, mechanical steps, your knight comes to stand at Victoria's side.
In his eyes, something has undeniably shifted.
In her eyes, something has undeniably shifted.
You'll never again have the chance to see this lovely face.
... And we're going to have so much fun together.
I leave you to your little candaulist pleasures.
... O‑our knight was clearly not in his right mind, Your Grace...
... O‑our knight was clearly not in her right mind, Your Grace...
We cannot possibly allow that demon to take one of our own with her.
We will rescue our knight as discreetly as possible.
We will rescue our knight as discreetly as possible.
Let us challenge Victoria to a duel.
Let's rid ourselves of this harpy of misfortune...
We know where Victoria is hiding, so let's attack her there.
Let's rid ourselves of this harpy of misfortun...
You can do it, Your Grace.
The man steps forward, revealing an injured arm from which drops of blood splash onto the courtroom floor at regular intervals.
Victoria did that to you, didn't she?
Your [i]subtle[/i] attempt to lighten the mood should probably have better timing.
Please help me. I implore you!
He's swaying and on the verge of fainting.
What does she want from you?
The name falls through the air like a heavy blanket.
. The great Lady Knight Victoria is the one who did [i]that[/i] to you??
We'll invite her to come explain herself.
*Victoria*... She's the murderer of the Enberg prefect.
. Her name inspires fear wherever it's whispered.
She's described as the finest in the kingdom, but sadly, her misdeeds echo across every land as well...
... It's common knowledge that it's best not to provoke that woman's anger.
His wide eyes briefly fall on the man's arm.
She'd been keeping a low profile lately, but
.with the events in Enberg, it seems she's taken up her duties again.
.people said she had left Brizh some time ago...
. I know too much, Your Grace. I know where her hideout is.
... She's been hunting me ever since. I hear the whispers. That she'll silence me for good...and tear out my tongue for some kind of vile ritual
. she's a [b][shake]demon[/shake][/b]! A monster wearing a skin like ours...
. [font_size=18]He won't last much longer. Act quickly.[font_size=18]
...And [shake]Victoria...[/shake] We'd better hope she's on our side against the Empire. This may be our chance to gather crucial information.
Tell us where her hideout is and disappear.
Calm down, we're here for you. You're safe.
Tell us where her hideout is. You'll have our protection.
You have to fight back, buddy! Show her!!
He rolls his eyes back and bolts without looking back.
His troubled gaze shifts from right to left. It seems as though he is engaged in an internal debate.
. I-I can't stay here. S-she'll find me and then she'll...
Out of breath, he lowers his voice.
He's hiding... i-in the basement of the old abandoned church in Mana Strala.
He rolls his eyes back and bolts without looking back.
His troubled gaze shifts from right to left. It seems as though he is engaged in an internal debate.
I'll tell you where she's hiding...when you've ensured my safety...
He collapses with a faint. Your guards carry him out of the Audience Room.
His troubled gaze shifts from right to left. It seems as though he is engaged in an internal debate.
He considers the idea for a moment before rushing off without looking back.
N-no matter what you choose to do with this information, Your Grace, we should exercise...caution.
It's likely that Victoria followed his trail all the way here
. W-we should be ready, Your Grace.
... Let us resume today's hearings, please... [font_size=18] I-i'll mop the floor afterward.[/font_size]
So you took care of eliminating that ridiculous little pest from Enberg.
He seems to be holding back tears.
. You managed to prove your worth to me.
Therefore I am now willing to entertain your Round Table.
I could reduce every one of your obstacles to nothing but forgotten remnants...
... And erase from this world anyone who dares to stand against your reign.
I still have a few details to sort out before I can welcome you.
You have a lot of nerve suggesting me to [i]wait[/i].
have you finally fulfilled my desires, my dear little sovereign?
If not, you know what awaits your advisor.
(Lie) Yes, we took care of that man.
Yes, we took care of that man.
I don't care for little birds who lie...
[shake]I tear off their beaks when they chirp too much.[/shake]
What an adorable little pet you make, so obedient and docile.
What will your next whim be?
But clearly, it can't be all that unpleasant for you.
Here I am, come to submit my first demand to you, my dear little sovereign.
And, alas, it still doesn't involve the slightest bit of mutilation of your advisor.
This first request is trivial-child's play.
Far too many flies imagine they can harm me.
Wretched vermin poking around in my private life as if they were worthy of it.
Like that pitiful little mosquito whose arm I tore off.
Such pathetic insects live only among filth, do they not?
So I shall lure them back to their origin... every wretched creature gathered in one place.
all you need to do is exterminate them.
In the most painful way, preferably.
(Lie) They shall be executed. (Scare them off.)
(Lie) They shall be executed. (Let's send someone to pay them off to leave.)
I shall return when their anguished screams have reverberated across the entire realm of Brizh.
It seems you've finally rid this Kingdom of its vermin.
... In any case, I haven't been bothered by the buzzing of those miserable mosquitoes lately.
But if you want to belong to me [i]entirely[/i], my little bird - so obedient to my will.
I have one [b]final[/b] demand that you must satisfy.
She seems to be asking herself what satisfaction you find in stumbling over your words.
And so I have come to present you with my [i]modest[/i] demand, my dear little bird.
Alas, I must admit it still doesn't involve the slightest bit of mutilation for your advisor...
All I expect from you is to be an obediently sweet pet...perfectly docile to my voice.
There is a certain influential figure in Enberg who persists in thrusting their pathetic little nose into my private matters.
He imagines that he can cast me aside yet he is mistaken.
This farce has endured long enough. I require you to dispose of this vermin.
I have the unpleasant feeling that a certain advisor here is very eager to lose his tongue.
(I mean yours, in case that wasn't obvious.)
... Very well. We'll take care of him.
(Lie) Of course, we'll take care of it. (Fake his murder.)
Should you succeed in this, my dear little fledgling
then perhaps you shall finally be worthy to stand beside me.
Your words seem to have struck her in a...particular way.
You're full of surprises, my dear little bird.
Whatever you decide, know that I will remain forever loyal to you.
This man, Yohav, is the Count of Enberg.
W-were we not supposed to assist Yohav in the matter of the Enberg trial?
. is our ally now. We helped them.
They are... they are our friends...
This means we should sever all alliance with that county in the future, not to mention the dire political consequences that would follow...
... And, on a more personal note, I-I have...
... This man is a dear friend, with whom I shared my early years
... Please don't do this, I [i]beg[/i] you.
scriptedquest_victoria_third_trial.prev: It seems you've finally rid this Kingdom of its vermin.

lines: What are you trying to sell me this time? A shell carriage?
Ah, now's probably not the best time, but we did just get a shipment in from the Basalt Isles. Sea urchins, the size of my fist and oysters abso-lute-ly gi...
Y-yes, excuse me. Let me start over.
Our warehouses are on fire. It's a disaster!
The fire is being spread by a salamander.
This little market of ours, the life, the colour, the beauty of it. All of it, up in smoke, if things carry on like this...
I'll send knights to fight the beast.
Ah, thank you, yes, thank you!
Have you visited our night market?
The night market? Is it different?
...I remind you that I still cannot move from this Tower.
YOU MUST SEE OUR BEAUTIFUL FISH ON SALE!
We sell all sorts of things there.
These days, you can even find poison powder there sometimes.
But not great for business. The product's been pulled from the shelves, but we'd like to know where it's coming from. So it doesn't happen again, you see?
I'll send someone to look into it.
I'll send someone to pose as a merchant.
Oh, yes, yes, yes. I'll take it, I'll take it.
shellington_grievance_night_market.prev: Have you visited our night market?

lines: My Noble Grace! We use seaweed as a condiment. Samphire. A real culinary gem, you should try it.
It's one of our flagship products!
But... we used a ton of it for the annual banquet, and now everyone's getting sick one after another...
Do you have any healers available before this food poisoning does more damage?
I have scholars specialising in the ingestion of toxic substances.
I'll call in the local healers.
I suppose so, but still... it's been several days now...
shellington_grievance_odd_salicornia.prev: My Noble Grace! We use seaweed as a condiment. Samphire. A real culinary gem, you should try it.

lines: Tell me, my Noble Grace, do you have any secret passages in this Tower?
You study Moris in silence. Is he aware of... what lives beneath the Tower?
Is he a [i]danger[/i] to the kingdom?
... I'm just asking because we have a strange nobleman who has been digging a tunnel between Pince-Harbour and Shellington.
Now that it's done, after sixty years of toil, he's trying to force people to use it for trade, charging a coin for every crossing.
Do not let all those years of work go to waste. Use this new path.
It may be a good idea to get some tradesmen to check the safety of the tunnel.
...Just like that? You don't want to check it or anything?
At your command, my noble Grace.
At least there's no questions to ask. That's fine with me. Thank you, my Noble Grace!
shellington_grievance_secret_tunnel.prev: Tell me, my Noble Grace, do you have any secret passages in this Tower?

lines: I have a bunch of wonderful snails for you today!
I even have a few crates of them! Nay...
... Well, erm, we're a bit overrun, actually. They're everywhere. In our barns, in our bags, under our feet.
...Did you clean your boots before entering?
Take this and hire people to get rid of them.
Into a frying pan, with parsley, garlic, shallots and butter.
Set up a Song Thrush breeding programme. They love snails.
Errm, uh... you do have someone mopping up right?
Oh yes, yes, yes, please, my Noble Grace.
Slightly different than our recipe for scallops. The parsley will enhance the flavour, and with the right cooking time, they won't be too spongy.
I'll leave you a crateful, my Noble Grace!
... Aren't you afraid that one invasive species will replace another?
shellington_grievance_snails_invasion.prev: I have a bunch of wonderful snails for you today!

lines: SHELLFISH LIKE YOU'VE NEVER SEEN BEFORE.
Fresh! Come try it in Shellington! Just harvested from our waters richest seas.
... Our Grace cannot leave the Tower, Sir Moris.
...Right so... you can't exactly experience it yourself, but maybe you could still do something about the road between Shellington and Pince-Harbour?
I'll have it restored and reinforced.
Fix it yourself. You've got plenty of sand, after all.
Ah, now we're talking. Thank you.
Always looking to please, aren't you! Here's a little something.
... I don't know if you've ever tried driving a horse-drawn carriage on it, but it's not very practical.
Not a sound remains in the training hall. Your guards and knights have already left.
Yet you sense a gaze watching from the shadows.
Is stealth the specialty of the hunters of Groveshire?
How do you manage to move so quietly?
Our hunters are respectable enough, but I'm unquestionably the most agile among them.
I am... also the day... a good hunter, in short.
I apologize if I frightened you, dear Sovereign, it was merely my bad habits. I was born thus, I'm afraid.
With a bow in the cradle?
You're from Beaconsbury, if I'm not mistaken?
How on earth could a baby hold a bow with such small hands?
how shall I put it...training ground. Groveshire is dominated by its vast forests, where countless beasts have long wreaked havoc, making the region hostile.
Our hunting culture was born from this. Every child starts with a bow or spear, remaining vigilant for hours in absolute silence...
... I myself could spend days hidden within a bush, waiting for the clue that would solve my riddle of the day.
And never once did any creature test my patience.
Until... [i]that Beast[/i]. The anomaly. The ultimate enigma...
Annoyed at not having caught your prey?
The Beast will never kill again.
Yes. That's surely the most important thing.
. It haunted my nights. I had never encountered something so elusive. Usually, game reacts on pure instinct alone.
was different. It adapted. It learned.
... Ah, I regret that this hunt ended as it did.
Yet something tells me that at your side, greater challenges await...
An elusive dragon, one day perhaps.
His eyes ignite with a fervor you have never seen in him before.
silgur_affinity_0.prev: Not a sound remains in the training hall. Your guards and knights have already left.

lines: And yet, a man remains there, bent over sharpening one of his knives, lost in thought.
Oh, you're here... my dear Sovereign.
Didn't want to share your skills with the rest of us?
Are you preparing for a hunt?
Restoring a noble blade to its former glory is an intimate affair.
And I don't like the surrounding jabber.
I spent so much time lurking in the forests that heated conversations now unsettle me.
Not this time...although I wouldn't say no to disappearing into one of your forests for a few days to see the monsters that roam there.
He raises the polished blade before his eyes, observing his meticulous work.
All we can do is cry when our equipment fails us in the face of danger, right?
I would like to tell you yes... I'll certainly miss the beauty of the emerald forest.
I made peace with leaving Groveshire long ago. And that is precisely why I presented myself to you.
Part of you is still there, isn't it?
Were you hoping for something greater?
... I couldn't say. If it exists, that part of me is... suffocated beneath contempt.
I gave my heart and blade to Groveshire long ago.
Every order from Guilhelm... I mean, the Count, I executed for the good of our lands.
But that belongs to the past now.
Does that loyalty still weigh on you?
Did he ask you to do things you regret?
My blade is now well sharpened. I leave you to your duties, dear Sovereign.
It seems you have opened a door he preferred to keep closed.
... but don't worry. I'll stay by your side...
... as long as you don't ask me to raise this blade against anything other than a beast.
The air suddenly turns freezing cold.
I hope I can trust you... You seem more decent than most.
Enough talk, you and I have other matters to attend to.
Seated upon an old stump, you glimpse the hunter lying in wait... But this time, he is holding a bottle in his hands rather than a blade.
A drink to help you find peace?
I'd like to tell you it helps, but...
... it's a false lead that takes me further from what I'm really looking for, I'm afraid.
A long sigh echoes through the silent gardens.
I was thinking back on our last...conversation. And my steps led me here.
You mean, what led you to leave Groveshire?
... Yes, you could say that. Or at least, to what pushed me to offer my services to someone else.
... I did what I thought was right back then. Are these really... regrets?
Groveshire had long been plagued by petty crime... bands of thieves who seized control by force in our scattered villages, buried beneath the forest.
Poor men without stature, men Guilhelm had spent years fighting.
... A single order from him was enough and these nobodies were silenced.
I was merely the shadow that carried it out, and no one wept for the dead I left behind.
But... some of them were... terribly young.
... I was just getting to that.
... Ah, that was twenty winters ago now. Time passes so quickly.
Guilhelm asked me to dispose of a noblewoman who was abusing her power to enslave an entire village. An old enemy of the Count.
Methodical work. My blades were sharp. Descending into her manor had been child's play. I proceeded as usual. Clean and precise, no need for suffering on this [i]creature[/i].
Because that's how I saw them back then... creatures.
... Until [i]her[/i] muffled cry echoed from the room next door.
...This child... A secret the woman had hidden from the world, no doubt...
... I stood motionless for several long minutes, watching the child scream with hunger and cold.
What I'm most ashamed of, Sovereign... I can tell you now...
... Guilhelm had already... given me similar orders in the past.
To... [i]take care[/i] of his own bastards—at least some of them... those who weren't of... noble birth.
His voice, usually cutting as a knife's edge, falters for the first time.
It's absurd, isn't it? But facing that child... all my crimes came crashing down on me with a violence I'd never felt before.
... so I took her in my arms. This little bundle of life.
Had her mother been brought to justice another way perhaps she would still care for the child. Or perhaps she would have abandoned her, as so many nobles do with their bastards eventually.
I raised the girl as best I could.
Some means of atonement I suppose.
A huntress without equal. My redemption.
But also my greatest shame. That's why... Groveshire is no longer mine. It's hers now.
I cannot comment on your past actions, but I understand what brought you here.
... Thank you for listening to my story.
Yes. I told her this... her story before I came knocking on your door.
She didn't... take it very well. But we're not exactly talkative, either of us.
However, what I learnt at your side.
is that through dialogue...one may open doors once thought locked.
In time, I will see her again.
She's busy as the new emissary of Beaconsbury, but... I want to talk with her. Properly.
... Thank you for listening to my haunted feelings, dear Sovereign.
You can take this bottle. I.
He speaks no further, silently closing that door that had been, for a fleeting moment, held ajar.
silgur_affinity_2.prev: Seated upon an old stump, you glimpse the hunter lying in wait... But this time, he is holding a bottle in his hands rather than a blade.

lines: Could you possibly require my services?
Then it will be my pleasure.
I have the odd feeling that I might belong here.
You seem content to run me in circles as [i]he[/i] did.
It is said the legendary hunter continues to watch over the Tower at distance.
His kingdom is safe and sound because his watch never ends.
silgur_ending.prev: It is said the legendary hunter continues to watch over the Tower at distance.

lines: I wished to update you on my recent culinary.
I gently seared it in a drizzle of oil with shallots and rosemary, almost confit-style.
Then, I flambéed the lot with a splash of wine to deglaze.
Finally, a pinch of paprika, and it was turned on the hot stone every two minutes, cooked to perfect medium flesh.
As for the effects, well...let's just say they were most...[i]stimulating[/i].
. far more vigorous, to be honest. My strength seems multiplied, much like in my younger years.
That said, I have the feeling that such an effect could have been devastating had I consumed it then.
It also seems that I have acquired a certain mastery
. An occult power I did not possess before, Your Grace.
...  I'm eager to demonstrate this to you.
I offer you [i]some[/i] of my well-meant wishes of success.
Ah, there you are, my Noble Grace !
I've been wanting to meet you for yeeeaaars !
...Even though you haven't exactly been warming the throne for that long...
Come on, Bernard, don't be so shy! Our Noble Grace isn't going to eat you with garlic butter!
The man before you looks like he's trying to sink into the floor.
Matter of fact, we could use a little help down there, your most gracious Grace!
It's regarding an invasion of seaweed.
Burn everything. Our scholars will be able to help.
Would any merchants be interested in it?
[font_size=18]Hard to set seaweed on fire though...[/font_size]
Er...I think we've come to the wrong place, my good Bernard.
...[font_size=18]Not all seaweed is edible, Yer Grace.[/font_size]
What grace! What business acumen! And so quick with a solution!
southbay_locations_grievance_presentatio.prev: Ah, there you are, my Noble Grace !

lines: . [font_size=18]Although a little too saturated with straw bales, uhh.
But you don't have many mounts at the moment.
...Are you looking for new ones, Your Grace?
This Tower that belongs to you.
. Why is it so hard to find any historical artifacts here?
Portraits of your predecessors should line your corridors, their relics displayed in showcases...
How else could you hope to make the most of this fertile soil that is yours.
We haven't had time to decorate yet...
Do not be ignorant, Your Grace, this is not a matter of mere visual distraction...
... But don't get me wrong... I'm delighted to work alongside you and convinced that together we can shape a bolder future.
I'm simply pointing out the need to be [b]inspired[/b] by your surroundings in order to achieve that goal...
... By drawing both from the great victories of history and its most painful failures, so we avoid repeating a fool's mistakes.
What do you think is most important?
Which ruler should I be closer to?
That piques my curiosity... are you lacking courage? Or is it [shake][b]intelligence[/b][/shake] that fails you?
I intend to make good use of Herod's wisdom.
Be a powerful, feared, and respected Sovereign.
Believe me, Your Grace. I'm no advocate of cruelty or subversion.
I merely contend that power must rest on a firm foundation, one the monarch embodies to guide their people toward prosperity. A lighthouse in the dark.
A ruler's decisions must be decisive. Their words, unambiguous and striking. That is the mark of true leadership.
Such a stance ensures a safer worldview; it forges a strong, proud people united around an exemplary leader.
Well, Your Grace, I see you're already well‑informed.
Herod remains the most illustrious ruler these lands have ever known.
Nothing would please me more than witnessing here the resurrection of their reign...
A Sovereign once embodied on this throne the ideal of reassuring stability that I long to see restored.
They ruled with an iron hand and managed to rally all their contemporaries under one banner.
The direct ancestor of the Gavault family line...
Either way, Your Grace, I repeat... with me at your side, I am sure that this ideal can be achieved.
I don't claim to know your true motives. But I'm certain your choice to recruit me was no accident...
... So trust me. Follow where I lead, and the path to prosperity will unfold before you.
... Oh, worry not, [i]dear[/i], I've followed your feats throughout the War of Tarascus.
It seems that you have remained exactly as you were back then.
That's where you're gravely mistaken, old gal.
Although I was already a valiant warrior at the time, I have since taken ample time to question my own motives.
Don't forget either that the tactics you condemned allowed us to triumph over my late father.
Could you have won without me?
Your brutality has no place here and I sincerely lament that you were ever granted the right to set even a toe within this Tower.
Had you not been so soft, you could have become the greatest warrior in Brizh's legends.
... We were reminiscing about the [i]good old days[/i], Your Grace.
But I'm sure Sir Tarcus has plenty more nonsense to share with someone else.
This old maid never recognised the crucial importance of my role in resolving the Tarascus conflict. That's all.
You took part in the war?
My father, Tarascus, was the Count of Gavault at the time
We - Mathilda, my brother and their armies, the nobility of Brizh led by Alwena, and our then ally - the Count of Groveshire, joined forces to depose him.
On the front line with the rest of the nobility from Gavault, Brizh and Groveshire, fighting against the former Count Tarascus.
You declared war on your own father?
What were these *methods* Alwena referred to?
An informative discussion for you I hope.
For the first time, he seems almost uncomfortable.
I was young and convinced his methods weren't the right ones.
Most called him a mad and tyrannical despot, but he was merely a man.
. with grand ambitions for his county.
After failing to be selected by the Tower of Brizh he chose to claim these lands through sheer force without the help of the Gods.
He coveted [i]your[/i] place, all things considered.
anyway, that's the only reason we went to war against him.
Believe me, seeing the county's state afterward was a bitter pill to swallow.
Gavault never regained its former greatness! At the time, we were ruled by a tyrant... certainly feared, but respected and above all united.
My brother, who later reclaimed the throne, quickly proved to be a complete [shake][b]dishcloth[/b][/shake], incapable of governing his kingdom or his armies.
And a people who believe in revolution are ungovernable.
. Thus, our victory over Count Tarascus injected a poison into their minds...a poison that still lingers today.
Fortunately, when her husband fell, Mathilda seized back the reins and reinstated the rigid governance Gavault once knew. Yet the damage was already done.
... Ironically, she too ended up timidly mimicking what she had rebelled against in her youth, [shake][b]bahaha[/b][/shake].
Shortly after the war, those cowards simply broke every alliance without offering any real explanation.
I merely ensured that we achieved our goals with minimal losses, for the good of the people.
In any case, Your Grace, I have certainly matured in my opinion, but my methods have always spoken for themselves... [shake][b]bahaha[/b][/shake].
The gears of power are immutable, don't you think?
tarcus_affinity_2.prev: ... Oh, worry not, [i]dear[/i], I've followed your feats throughout the War of Tarascus.

lines: So, you've finally decided to work with me, right?
I still need to think about it.
I'll take the utmost care of this trust, Your Grace, bahaha.
tarcus_come_back_later.prev: So, you've finally decided to work with me, right?

lines: As soon as the sovereign had surrendered, Sir Tarcus vanished in a cloud of rage.
Si Tarcus replaced Arlin as counsellor to the Sovereign.
. Leading the kingdom with an iron fist.
Sir Tarcus never left the sovereign's side – remaining, right to the end, one of his most controversial knights.
tarcus_ending.prev: As soon as the sovereign had surrendered, Sir Tarcus vanished in a cloud of rage.

lines: I should have known. An idiot ruling a kingdom can only applaud an idiot ruling a county.
What are you doing here again, mutt?
Hey there. Still following me around, huh?
You're plotting something, aren't you? Don't think I don't know.
Well you're probably more loyal than half of this court.
You seem to watch a little "too" closely. Perhaps you see too much.
You're not like the others. You listen.
At least with you, I know where I stand.
Sometimes I wonder... am I feared more than I'm heard?
You'd let me know if something was going on, right?
Sometimes, I envy your freedom. The world seems lighter on you.
You think they respect me? Or do they just fear me?
Perhaps I can trust you a bit more.
Don't look at me like that. You're just a dog.
Belladonna carefully examines your Knight's coat as it stands motionless on an alchemy table.
He doesn't seem to be having a good time.
What are you doing to my good boy?!
...Did you notice anything unusual about this creature, Your Grace?
He's actually a human under a spell...isn't he?
Well, you are surprisingly intuitive, Your Grace.
Ah, you are sorely lacking in intuition, Your Grace...
This Beast that you treat like a mere dog
. Its gaze is sharp, piercing, dare I say...intellectual.
.surprisingly sentient, the first time it brought back one of my stray slippers.
But today, I haven't a single doubt.
She glides her hand over the Beast's body with a mystic touch, sending a long shiver in its wake.
This creature was a human, Your Grace.
A human trapped under a most powerful curse...
... But should you wish to evict them from this furry prison, I could likely undo the spell.
Your knight is now fidgeting nervously, awaiting your verdict.
A...human? Yes, do whatever it takes to treat him.
Impressive. Yes, do whatever it takes to treat him.
No, thank you. He's fine as he is.
. I shall not question your desires.
Staring off into the distance, she tries to soothe the creature, looking truly sorry.
The howl of the Tower's Protector is so terrifying that no enemy of the Sovereign would dare approach it once night has fallen.
No one in the Tower ever realized that he was in fact a man who had been transformed into a wolf, and so it remained until the end of his days...
the_wolf_ending.prev: The howl of the Tower's Protector is so terrifying that no enemy of the Sovereign would dare approach it once night has fallen.

lines: Uh... we've got ourselves a bit of a pirate problem out on the islands.
. they're firing off cannonballs and breathin' fire all at once.
A squad arrives to the rescue.
I'll tell the pirates to mind their manners while we wait.
You wouldn't happen to have a lad with a silver tongue for some union talk?
The griffins of Basalt have had a gutful of workin' for peanuts; they're demanding more in their bowls and hazard pay.
. and rightfully so, if you ask me, Captain.
My knights will lead the talks.
No room for parley. I'm sending someone to shut their traps.
Pirates have a bit of a bad name these days, don't they?...
Yet some of us (like myself) are more into sea-hikin' and alternative tourism than sinking ships and pillagin' villages.
And since we don't choose our crewmates.
the Basalt Pirates' Fellowship would dearly love to have a royal figure up their sleeve for the next pirate summit.
"Negotiate"? No way are we going to encourage these activities. We'll intimidate them.
Don't you reckon their behaviour is just a way of adjustin' to a world that's rigged against them from the start?
Err... we were wonderin' how to teach the recent happenings of Basalt in its history books.
See, there's Rorik's lot-the separatists-who want to turn it into a foundin' myth of the resistance, and then Gotfrig's continent-loyalists who are never bloody satisfied....
Let's focus on the struggle of the independentists.
Let's look more closely at the issue of opening borders.
Neither one nor the other. Let's talk about *my* role in all this instead. *Me*.
Our scholars will strike the right balance.
... so you don't want to take sides.
Aye, [i]you[/i] when you made... your unilateral decision.
tortosa_grievance_political_instabilitie.prev: Err... we were wonderin' how to teach the recent happenings of Basalt in its history books.

lines: One of our quay managers-one of the lads handlin' the traffic with Southbay-has gone and called a strike.
He's systematically blocking every vessel sailin' in from there.
According to his theory, some of the folk from those parts, they're just a bit too.
... Err... he's just not overfond of the colour of their skin.
Translation: The dockworkers are being held hostage by a purebred racist.
Organize a seminar to discuss the issue.
... you're quite sure you're wantin' to hear that sort of talk?
Lock him up in a cargo ship bound for Southbay.
He shakes his head slowly, as if mentally adding you to the "disappointments" section of an invisible notebook.
Don't have to tell me twice.

Our fine shore is completely blocked off by a giant sea serpent that's gone and decided to lounge all along the coast. Naught to see now but a massive curtain of blue scales, shimmerin' there in the sun....
We're at each other's throats - half want the beast dead to save the view, while the rest reckon we just nudge it along to spoil the neighbors' horizon instead.
Let's move it, it doesn't look too dangerous.
Let's scrape off its scales and turn it into a giant slide. For a fee.
But I cannot allow you to do that...
This decision is not yours to make.
You must know that, don't you?
But I cannot let that happen.
Do you know how long we have waited for these doors to open again?
For someone to restore order to this kingdom?!
How many lives were sacrificed in the wars we waged, because we could not rely on its power?
... But even if it's an order from you.
. This one time I cannot accept.
None of this will be easy.
But to rely on this [i]thing[/i] for a prosperous future?
You would rather destroy this edifice out of pure hatred for the very fabric of our society...
That I despise monarchs in all their forms, I will not deny.
But this is not merely about that.
this Tower represents something far darker, Arlin.
For its power draws its roots from that of the demons themselves.
And as long as it stands, the Kingdom will be exposed to a terrible danger.
I have known for a long time.
And I never said a word.
I thought that if it could restore our kingdom to its previous grandeur then.
You knew that the demonic forces fed upon the power of this Tower, and yet you let it grow.
Even worse, you accepted that such power should rest in the hands of a single human being...
... You would sacrifice your entire kingdom for a mere dream of the past.
This folly ends here and now.
There's more to it than that!!
You will die in exchange, Your Grace...
. Too much after everything you have done.
I'm sorry, Arlin. But the time has come for the people to decide their own fate.
Move, Arlin. The age of Kings and Sovereigns is over.
I should be cursing you but.
. it seems I no longer have the will to do so...
Nothing remained but a mere stones, from which not the slightest trace of magic subsided.
As though it had harboured an invisible balance within itself, everything changed when it collapsed.
The inhabitants of the Kingdom had to face many hardships.
The counties were forced to start anew. Some returned to their old traditions, others turned toward Brimwoodian ideologies.
But one thing remains certain, nothing was ever the same again.
History will only remember you as the nameless Sovereign who destroyed the Tower.
your empathy, hopes for the future and sacrifices will remain forever etched in the memory of those who crossed your path.
The repercussions of your actions will echo throughout history, carrying hope to those who will come after you.
It seems to me that you wanted to talk?
Have you noticed anything strange happening in the Tower recently?
. no, that doesn't ring a bell.
[i]hearing voices[/i] in our private quarters fall within your definition of 'anything strange'?
... For example, yes. Be careful not to let yourself be manipulated.
You truly care about your knights' well-being, Your Grace.
I'll keep your advice in mind.
But don't worry... I'm absolutely not the type to let myself be influenced by things like that.
You wished to speak with me, Your Grace?
His voice is tired and sluggish.
Such an unusual concern on your part...
I must confess it's been disastrous.
Every night for several moons now, I've been assailed by relentless dreams and ethereal voices issuing unspeakable commands...
I'll order something from an apothecary to help you sleep. No more incessant dreams.
...I have to admit these sagging dark circles give me a certain charm.
But thank for your consideration, Your Grace.
These sleepless nights are slowly giving me the impression I might be losing my mind...
traitors_plot_omniscient_gideon_murderer.prev: You wished to speak with me, Your Grace?

lines: You wished to speak to me about something?
Have you noticed anything strange in the Tower recently?
[i]Strange events[/i]? Could you possibly be even more vague, please?
Like what? Ghostly voices, monsters hiding under beds?
I do indeed suspect that some *outside force* is trying to influence you.
*Something* that would try to manipulate you, for example.
... Do you take me for a fool?
A mind as brilliant as mine could never be duped by such tricks.
But you gave me a good laugh, so I won't hold this offense against you.
traitors_plot_omniscient_gwendan_murdere.prev: You wished to speak to me about something?

lines: Indeed. Have you noticed anything strange in the Tower recently?
Like [i]somethin'[/i] trying to get a hold on me.
I suspect that some *outside force* is trying to influence you.
... That's what I suspect. Don't let yourself be manipulated.
... Nice of you to bring it up, actually.
To be honest, I was starting to think I was losin' it.
But don't worry, I was already on my guard.
Wasn't about to let some silly voice push me around.
And such was the end of our story...
After defeating Arthur Pendragon, Emperor of Angelor, the Sovereign of the Tower finally achieved their objective.
This display of strength chilled the various counties of the Empire, so much so that none dared to claim the slightest independence any longer.
More powerful than ever, the kingdom of Bretania began its inexorable invasion of the Empire's territory.
In the course of this campaign, one of the Scouts of Brizh sent back the following report:
Amidst the rubble of the former capital of Angelor stands the ruins of a Black Tower... in every way, similar to the one in Brizh.
Any resistance by the few counties of the Empire that did dare to retaliate were immediately crushed.
Upon those lands, wars devasted the earth into ash...
And thus, conquest had become the norm for the Kingdom of Bretania from that day forth.
Through the power of the Golden Key, the Tower of Brizh revealed its full might, granting its knights supernatural invincibility.
What would have been a campaign of years became mere weeks...
Healed of his affliction by this same power, the Sovereign undertook a long journey toward the ancient Black Tower that sat enthroned at the heart of the old capital.
Using the Golden Key, they opened its doors and forever united the powers of the two edifices.
Then, a mighty echo vibrated throughout the Kingdom and the entire Empire
. Slowly, the spirit of the people began to harmonize with the power of the Sovereign.
Immersed in eternal bliss, none could deny it any longer.
Paradise had been born on earth.
. And not even any semblance of individual opinon. Only a sacred silence remained where all minds thought as one.
Deep within the White Tower of Brizh, the demon's laughter could be heard ringing out.
. but there was none left to hear it.
The Sovereign finally achieved a definitive cure for their illness.
And their reign lasted for all eternity.
tyranny_ending_cutscene.prev: And such was the end of our story...

lines: I, the Dragon Knight, dost extend mine salutations unto thee.
Is there any soul amidst this gathering endowed with the power to parley with me?
Stop. I don't want to play your game, Dragon Knight.
I know who you are, and I'll accept your challenge.
Thou art but a paltry insect, and darest thou to curtail my grandiloquent oration?
Indeed. Let's stop here. Go back to your castle.
Sorry, I just wanted to keep it short... I'm listening.
The Dragon Knight falls silent for a few seconds, taken aback by your behaviour.
But after a moment, he slowly raises his sword towards you.
Thou art unworthy of this throne!
Thou seemeth enamoured in courting with life and death against the flame, Stranger.

Thy spirited mettle doth please mine eye, yet 'twill avail thee naught against the Angelor Empire's might. So doth I challenge thee Stranger. Prove unto me thou art indeed the rightful Sovereign that doth sit upon the throne.
I shall claim victory by mustering my most noble allies against you.
I shall claim victory with the scholarly circles to defeat you.
I shall claim victory by rallying the people to my cause.
Hah! Thine words are pleasing to my ears, Stranger.
But art thou truly a lion or a lamb hiding underneath that mask?
You are in the presence of the Sovereign!
Thou art but a mere [font_size=30]child[/font_size] in these realms. How mightest thou lay claim to this exalted throne? And not I?
I, who hath been crowned by the ancient, vintage, limited-edition, true king himself. Hath traversed the domain of Bretania decade by decade and levelled cities in my wake.
So doth I challenge thee, stranger.
Prove unto me that thou art the Sovereign this dominion doth require, that thou canst gather valiant knights, lead thy folk to peace and prosperity, and stand resolute against the Angelor Empire.
Shouldst thou falter, or refuse my challenge, I shall take thy life with mine own hand!
I shall muster my most noble allies against you.
I shall use the mystic forces to defeat you.
I shall inspire the people and rally them to me.
You accept without hesitation, Stranger. These realms doth merit a Sovereign of great might.
Until we meet anon. Thou hadst best be prepared.
I had heard legends about this Dragon Knight, but I thought him long dead...
Let us prepare for battle. I've noted the objectives in terms of resources and support that need to be achieved... Bear in mind that these are not essential to our success.
Hark! We shall curtail it, then.
Until we meet anon. Thou hadst best be prepared.
ultimatum_dragonknight.prev: I, the Dragon Knight, dost extend mine salutations unto thee.

lines: Lo! This is the moment. The hour hath arrived, false Sovereign.
Verily, I shall await thee on the morrow at first light. Where the Sun doth ascend upon the loftiest tower of Drakovic!
Too early. Why not in the afternoon?
Too ear-? Perchance you may speaketh true. Allow me to peruse mine agenda.
Aye, the afternoon will prove suitable. The morrow's weather in mine lands appeareth fair. A splendid plan it doth sound.
Be ye therefore boldly prepared, and dispose thy person in all due reverence.
My best knights will be called upon to fight you.
I will need only my holy trinity to defeat you.
A daring duo shall be sufficient to defeat you.
. exceedlingly naive if you think that sufficient to break me.
I look forward to eradicating that smug smile from thy visage.
I [shake rate=20.0 level=5 connected=1]HOPE[/shake] thy knights art well-prepared!
ultimatum_dragonknight_before_the_storm.prev: Lo! This is the moment. The hour hath arrived, false Sovereign.

lines: Thou and thy knights have faltered, false Sovereign.
And what vile stratagem didst thou dare try to weave, by mingling my bewildered grandson into these intrigues? You sought this just to unsteady me?
And what cowardly ploy didst thou dare try to weave, by thinking to ambush and slay my most faithful companion?
They could not best me in my solitude. And your final meagre machinations now fly as ash in the wind.
Thou art unworthy of this throne and your life shall be forfeit.

lines: Thou art but a mere [font_size=30]child[/font_size] in these realms. How mightest thou lay claim to this exalted throne?

Hark...know ye mine own person, a solitary and aged knight of the erstwhile and mightiest king?
You wanted to challenge me. My noble allies and I will respond.
You wanted to challenge me. I will respond with the help of my knowledgeable allies.
You wanted to challenge me. My people and I will become one.
Ha! I am much delighted to give ear unto these utterances.
Verily, I shall return to thee when...
Don't worry. My knights will be knocking on your door soon.
Oh? I confess, I was not prepared for this turn of events.

lines: I–I... I am Arron, Your Grace!

Victory must be assured at any cost.
...'Tis too late. No endeavour shall bring back my loyal companion nor correct my blindess to this ploy.
An iron-will that may make thee victorious yet it shall bereave thee of all friends in time.
I keep thee in peace and render thee respect for the nonse, young Sovereign

. Nay, by my troth! Wherefore is my head so absent?...
A young man, absurdly fragile next to the towering Dragon Knight, nestles at his side.
Permit me, on this occasion, to present mine esteemed great-great-great-great-great-...
N-nice to meet you, Y-Your Grace.
This feeble wight is in no wise hardy. I dare hope that, beneath thy roof and in thy company, he shall at last become a true man.
The young man barely dares to look in your direction.
I-I would like you to make me a g-great knight, Your Grace.

Calm yourself. Welcome to our Round Table.
No, this will not work out.

The gaze of the Emperor now lights up with sincere respect.
Consensus was not easy to reach, but you have demonstrated your strength to our allies.
They are ready to begin negotiations for a peace treaty.
Whilst the road may present us with obstacles, I hope we can secure a lasting peace.

. We shall begin negotiations in earnest tomorrow.
The old man who appeared as the Emperor's counselor stands before you, hunched.
His weary gaze scrutinizes you in silence.

Hatred silently distorts the old sage's eyes.
Sire Arthur Pendragon, Emperor and Guardian of the Sacred Lands of Angelor, is no more.

in my name, I offer you today the capitulation of our Empire...
His cold eyes never leave yours, unwavering.
... Know, Your Grace, that I had [i]foreseen[/i] all this.

I am reassured you see where we are coming from.
A long silence hangs on your declaration.
He stops, unable to determine whether you've just issued a threat, or a
... Be that as it may, my sole compass is to defend the afflictions of my people and our allies.

... Yet not a hint of surprise colours his voice.
Allow me to offer you my most sincere apologies.

... If you'll allow me... his honesty still seems quite murky to me.
I implore you, exercise the utmost caution...

. I advise you to consider another strategy.

... Then, my dear advisor Merlin conducted in-depth esoteric analyses to reveal your true nature.
. Just in case you were a bit of a disaster in your past lives.
It was an unsettling experience, to say the least.
... Your reign is nothing but a horrific ascent into tyranny, and the majority demands your removal.
... And I can only share that opinion.
Merlin in all his years has never been so lost for words. It's as if you had methodically ensured each of your decisions was more atrocious than the last.
He stares at you with undisguised disgust.
... The implication is that the concerns of my people are perfectly well-founded, and we will not allow them to live in fear of your madness for one second longer.
War will be our only resort.
Prisoner of his loyalty and afraid of this kingdom he himself helped build by placing his trust in your hands.
We can't say it wasn't entertaining.
Next time we want to look into you, we'll consider calling upon political prisoners.
Is that you come across as an erratic leader who seems to seems to prioritize jesting over sound decision-making...
... That said, your choices generally seem to be guided by rather noble intentions.
But it remains unclear where we stand.
You can stand right here beside me forever, if you want.
He stares at you, not with suspicion, but with the disbelief of seeing a petty prankster of your ilk threatening the stability of his empire.
... You are an enigmatic Sovereign, to say the least, but one who does not seem to pose a serious threat.
In other words, due to your.
. unpredictable nature, let's just say we are not confident enough to negotiate a classic peace treaty.

... What emerges from all this is that your reign is commonly described as.

Under these conditions, alas, the war seems already won for our allies.
For no one imagines losing against such a.

He stares at you with a hint of pity.
How can I be more direct with you, Majesty...
They see you as an easy prey.
Therefore, they have no reason not to push me into war.
and I, for my part, have no reason to relinquish my throne.
Your advisor does not dispute it.
Not at all. Don't be so hard on yourself.
... Everything points to you being an admirable, respectable, and shrewd leader, with a record of decisions guided by genuine wisdom.
We can't fault you for much, to the point that it's almost vexing.
... Consequently, I am ready to negotiate without reservation, on equal terms.
His gaze is full of respect.
... We are ready to consider any avenue that might avoid conflict.
We await only to hear your thoughts.
Your advisor puffs out his chest, clearly proud to be by your side.
. we haven't managed to form the [i]slightest[/i] idea about you.
Merlin was speechless... how on earth did you get this far without ever saying anything interesting, without ever taking a side? Neither risk, nor colour, nor flavour?
It's an unprecedented performance in the history of a reign. You embody blandness in its entirety that it is simply impossible to characterize you.
You see, you're doing it again... just [i]that[/i], right there.
... Be that as it may, this attitude has left us with a very poor impression.
Difficult to trust one who simply ceases to exist without any individuality.
A war thus seems inevitable... perhaps finally an opportunity for your reign to experience its very first [i]thrill[/i].
Your advisor doesn't say anything in this turn of events.
... Your decision in this conflict may well seal the fate of your reign forever, Your Grace.
If we have no choice, we'll fight.
I have the Golden Key, but it will serve my own ends.
So be it. We'll crush you.
We'll crush you without mercy, then impose our empire on the rest of the world.
I have the Golden Key, but it will serve my own ends.
Surprise: I feel like fighting. Unpredictable, huh?
I have *the* solution to all this chaos... let's get married.
I have the Golden Key. I'd exchange it for lasting peace.
I have the Golden Key, but it will serve my own ends.
I'll prove you wrong. We'll show you.
You will undoubtedly rule better than I, and I want to avoid conflict... we surrender.
I have the Golden Key. I'd exchange it for lasting peace.
I have the Golden Key, but it will serve my own ends.
Alas, I believe you remain a threat. We'll face you.

To offer our wisdom to the world, we'll defeat you before conquering it.
I have the Golden Key. I would exchange it for lasting peace.
I have the Golden Key, but it will serve my own ends.
They swears in silence that he will do everything in his power to see you perish, even risking his own life if necessary.
Anger and bitterness intertwine in his voice.
. May history remember you as the destructive Sovereign, whose unparalleled cruelty hastened the ruin of their own empire.
Surprise and disappointment mingle in the Emperor's gaze.

... This jest will be your last.
. May history remember you as the derisive Sovereign whose levity decimated the only people who ever held them in high regard.
. And may history remember you as the simpleton Sovereign, whose wounded pride in the face of truth condemned all those they cherished.
A silence settles, the Emperor seeming utterly dumbfounded.
... You still wish to confront me, when so many other outcomes were available to you...?
Bitterness and surprise intertwine in his voice.
. May history remember your name as that of a false strategist, whose absurd prudence condemned everything they had built.

Bitterness and surprise intertwine in his voice.

Know that this artifact is what matters most to me.
If you yield it, I am ready to hear your terms.

His eyes shine at your words, unable to believe what he has just heard.
He looks at you with solemn gravity.
... you have made the wisest choice possible.
And my gratitude will be eternal.
We shall discuss the details very shortly.
His every step is full of determination.
Although my trust in the Empire remains fragile, I must admit that this resolution is... moving.
Now, it is time for you to rest.
He pauses, assessing what is appropriate to reveal.
. That object would allow me to unlock my own Tower. The ancient Tower of Angelor.
Thus, we would henceforth be equals. My people would have less reasons to fear your influence.

. our union would, naturally, be sealed by a peace treaty.

... I dare hope that was merely a trick and that the Key is not actually in your possession.

. for you to speak this way.

...  Yes. I fell in love with you at first sight.

... now, it is time for you to rest.

lines: Actually, I was reminiscing a little bit about my county... and its little culinary eccentricities.
Leaning against a table, she crushes a strange mixture with a mortar.

Rum, cardamom and syrupy spider porridge, in that order, otherwise you'll ruin everything.
We call it the [i]Firetwig[/i], and it lives up to its name.
She crushes the carcasses of the poor animals with a disturbing level of enthusiasm.
There are plenty of these spiders on the walls of this Tower... so I thought why not give them a refreshing end?
These little creatures have infested Brimwood, too.
The [i]Firetwig[/i] from Brimwood, a lil' gem of mixology. Cardamom, rum and syrupy spider porridge. In that order, otherwise you'll ruin it.
Saw quite a few of these little creatures crawling on the walls of your Tower, so I took the liberty. [font_size=18]It made my mouth water.[/font_size]
She crushes the carcasses of the poor animals with a disturbing level of enthusiasm.
There are plenty in Brimwood too...it made me feel a bit nostalgic.
So, I decided to catch them and give them a new home in my throat. Warms me up and gives me courage.
Oh, you're a connoisseur! That's right, the true taste of Brimwood, pure and raw, prepared by a local. Not like the bland plonk you find at the market.
Rum, cardamom, and syrupy spider porridge. In that order, as you know.
She crushes the carcasses of the poor animals with a disturbing level of enthusiasm.
Brimwood is swarming with these little spiders, made me feel a little nostalgic.
Feeling nostalgic? Why did you leave?
. I had some wonderful years living there.
I've been wanderin' around for a while now.
You sure do ask a lot of questions.
Let's just say I've always liked dragging my carcass around...
... And after rotting in the same spot for a while, you've got to do something so you don't die of boredom.
You were wandering too, before this, weren't you? Bet you can understand.
'Dragging your carcass'... Looking for something? Or running away?
She ignores your question and vigorously stirs her mixture as she pours it into two glasses.
She smiles mischievously as she pours her mixture into two glasses.
She pours the mixture into two glasses, stirring it vigorously as she does so.
You're going to do me the favor of tastin' it, aren't you?
This is unworthy of a Sovereign, and of a knight in my service as well.
But you sure know how to kill the mood, huh?
You clink glasses, then raise yours to your lips.
Bitter and strong, the liquid sets your throat ablaze and twists your gut. You flail
choke and finally spit it out in a panic.
I admit, it's hard when you're not used to it. But.
You should come to Brimwood one of these days, you'll give my comrades a laugh.
She walks away with her drink.
You clink glasses and raise yours to your lips.
The liquid is full-bodied and strongly spiced, but the burning sensation in your throat soon gives way to a syrupy flavour that delightfully hits your taste buds.
You should come to Brimwood one of these days.
My comrades would welcome you warmly.
The young woman is facing away from you, leaning slightly forward. Her shoulders move gently as if she is following an soundless rhythm.
You hear confusing sounds, somewhere between humming and dissonant squeaking.
Eh, hi. [font_size=18]Didn't hear you come in.[/font_size]
Eh, hi. [font_size=19]Didn't hear you come in.[/font_size]
Don't sneak up on me again.
You hum along, trying to match Ursula's rhythm.
... Except that you're completely off beat.
... Sorry, but you'll need lil' more practice before our first jam session.
And... I'm not sure if I could match your.
You hum along to Ursula's rhythm, to the tune of [i]Where's my Lullaby[/i].
As if you've heard it before.
Gradually, your voices become more harmonious until she notices your presence and raises her voice slightly.
She turns around, half surprised, half amused.
Well, that was just a warm-up version, er.
She turns around again before facing you once more, holding a lute.
Was taking care of this little chick.
She taps the instrument's wood as though it were an old friend she has just met again after a long time apart.
I kind of let it rot in a corner, but...now that I'm settled here... Think it's time to fix it up.
She slides her fingers along the strings.
Don't you have anything better to do?
A Brimwood ballad, [i]Where's my Lullaby[/i], by the Vultured Crooks. Well.
. let's say it was a try. Still retuning my old lute.
And how long have you been practising?
As much as you are at being Sovereign.
Pretty cool that you know it. it's pretty.
She smiles and plucks a string, producing a slightly out-of-tune sound.
Have you been spying on me or something?
Have you been practicing for a long time?
I hope that one day I'll have the opportunity to hear you play it in its entirety.
Could play the whole thing for you... one of these days.
I mean once I've... got back into it a bit more.
We can talk about it again later.
Why not one of these days?
I mean, once my muscle memory has returned properly.
I think I'll be comfortable enough to play in front of you.
But with all the traveling...haven't had much opportunity lately.
But I learned in Brimwood, with a friend. We even had our own little group.
Brimwood's defining sound. From the gut, crafted by its outcasts.
A style of music where lutes spit out frantic symphonies, over vocals.
.by vocals I mean mostly just screaming.
Doesn't surprise me. People with terrible taste usually don't even realize it themselves.
Really? Wouldn't have guessed. Just goes to show, life is full of surprises.
That's *really great*. You forget I didn't hire you as a musician.
I hope I'll have the opportunity to hear you play again soon.
But I'm not very comfortable performing in front of...anyone just yet. Sorry.
You just looove killing the vibe before it's even born, huh?
Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a lute that needs tuning.
