lines: ... So, have you made up your mind?
We have lots of quests that might interest you. Welcome.
I don't want to work with you anymore.
... and you summoned me here just to bore me with that?
What remained of Lady Ursula wandered the Kingdom for years, an open wound that would not heal. They called her the Cursed Knight, for misfortune followed her relentlessly wherever she went.
She walked through ages, watched nations collapse beneath their own weight, tyrants rise and fall in endless, pointless succession.
But there was no one left behind her eyes to remember any of it.
The love Lady Ursula bore for the sovereign curdled over time into a sweet curse, her desires irreconcilable with the narrow order her station imposed upon her.
Yet, years after our story, upon the sovereign's death, she was still there.
A prisoner of tender memories, locked inside what could have been and never would be.

And there she remained, for years and centuries on end, watching each of her memories turn to cold ash. Condemned to outlive everything she had ever loved, until the last face, until even her own name was forgotten.
In search of new adventures, Lady Ursula finally left the Tower.
She returned later to Brimwood, where the Assembly opened its doors to her.
She became an important figure there, working to restore peace between the Guild and the Assembly.
ursula_ending.prev: What remained of Lady Ursula wandered the Kingdom for years, an open wound that would not heal. They called her the Cursed Knight, for misfo

lines: Your Knight carries with her a deathly silence that fills the air as she approaches.
Every spark of life seems to have left her.
And yet, she stands before you.
The icy silence of her lifeless eyes is your only answer.
It seems Lady Ursula is... no longer truly among us.
. Uh? No, was nothing more than a scratch, Your Grace.
But now that you mention it, that quest was [b][shake]DEADLY[/shake][/b] BORING.
Fine... wasn't exactly planning on bringing it up but I can't keep giving the poor gravediggers a heart attack each time this happens...
... Where did you get such skill?
Might have some in a week.
Ursula's gait is unusually heavy, even more sluggish than usual.
... That last quest washed me out.
Might have some in a week.
Like someone who's just come back from the dead, I guess.
Did you come to enjoy this beautiful weather too?
The sky is bright white, and a light drizzle moistens the air.
I just needed some fresh air.
Is the coffin of power starting to feel a bit tight already?
Better not stay outside too long, then.
With this drizzle, you might end up rotting away...like everything else that gets lost in the Pinemaze Forest.
Pinemaze is a place you know well?
You're implying that my decisions are rotten, is that it?
The moldy Sovereign, accompanied by his moldy lovely Knight.
It paints a pretty picture, doesn't it?
It's the little village of Moonvale where I was born.
She lets out a little laugh.
You would feel right at home in Pinemaze, then.
It's the little village of Moonvale where I was born.
A place where the only bit of sky you can see through the high treetops is often like it is today... bone-white.
And where the dampness can rot just about anything left behind in the woods.
It seems like a lovely place to live.
Pinemaze seems like a lovely place to live.
Do you go back there from time to time?
But I don't have many fond memories of that place.
.Left the second I was old enough, truth be told.
.a bit complicated for me to go back there.
She seems reluctant to reveal more.
I don't like dwelling on my past either.
Would you like to talk about it?
I imagine you prefer Brimwood, the place that welcomed you?
.Nobody knows a thing about where you came from.
I can't help but wonder what drove you to wander all the way here?
. That beautiful grey sky made me think about all that again.
She pauses for a few minutes, embarrassed, before speaking again.
.she's a powerful witch from Moonvale, and.
. she was obsessed with sheltering me from danger.
.Without getting into the gritty details, when a witch steeped in the dark arts tries to "enchant" you for your own protection.
She points to her left shoulder.
Hope you're not compiling info on your knights in a lil' notebook or something...
.the first place where I actually felt like I belonged.
The first place I found people who actually had my back...
You know, there are plenty of cursed people out there with marks like mine.
The "marked", they get pushed around in the far reaches of the kingdom... We're treated like [b]vermin[/b], really.
But in Brimwood, not only are people like me accepted... they actually wear our marks.
Almost everyone there has gotten them tattooed.
Because of that, people don't even know if you're cursed these days... They just assume you're from Brimwood.
Heh... guess it's a curse in its own right, isn't it?
But for the cursed of my kind, it's almost... a salvation.
. I'll probably never go back to Pinemaze.
The first place I made real friends. Friends who even went as far as getting the exact same ink as the shameful marks I carry...
No, Your Grace. Unfortunately I'm not a gang leader...
Well, can see you're dying to know more, so I'll lay it out for you. My mom isn't a tattoo artist.
They're the result of a curse that she brought upon me.
Opening up in this way seems to be a struggle for her.
... Why would anyone do such a thing?
I see... And so you fled to Brimwood.
I understand better now. Thank you for opening up to me.
...I'm sorry you had to go through that.
Thank you for opening up. You can count on me to keep your secrets safe.
Only a sad smile greets her last words.
That's...not really something to be proud of, Your Grace.
Only a sad smile greets your last words.
She seems to have said too much already.
At the back of the library, Lady Ursula is deep in thought, focused on drafting a document.
...Lately, it feels like I'm losing track of.
Wake up wondering what even happened the day before...
I'm having more and more blackouts
It's starting to freak me out, so...
She holds out her notebook, visibly filled with scribbled notes trying to reconstruct the last few days.
All heavily cluttered with crossed out lines.
Perhaps Belladonna would have a...remedy for such a problem?
I forbid you to tell my sister.
And...magic certainly won't be what helps me.
If anything, magic is what's condemned me in the first place.
She stops, visibly trying to hide her emotions.
It all started the first time I died, you know.
The first time I died, Your Grace.
I don't know what to do, it seems to be spiralling out of control.
I'm sure we'll find a solution.
Do you need to leave the Round Table?
I had no idea... I'll do everything I can to protect you from this.
Yes, being a knight is a risk, but
And if things end up going south.
...At least I'll have killed some time, I guess.
. But I'm afraid it's a little too late.
Your gaze falls upon her notebook, and before your eyes remains nothing but the chaos of frantic black scrawls.
ursule_affinity_4_if_died.prev: At the back of the library, Lady Ursula is deep in thought, focused on drafting a document.

lines: Ursula stands upright, leaning out of one of the windows in the hallway.
A few minutes pass as you silently observe your knight.
Until you eventually catches her attention.
. Hey, are you spying on me?
...Just going to act like you weren't standing there behind me the whole time without saying a word?
She doesn't move away as you draw close. You realize this is the first time you've mutually shared such proximity.
You lean over next to her.
A brilliant crescent moon pierces the cold blue of the sky through the window.
Its hypnotic whiteness is veiled by a thin mist, blurring its colour into an almost surreal glow.
just when you think the spectacle is over,
a few shy flakes begin to fall to the ground below.
Thank you for showing me this... I would have missed it otherwise.
Does it remind you of a familiar landscape?
Im not really the type to lounge around windows, uh.
. But this daytime crescent moon...it called to me.
The flakes thicken, falling faster now, right before your eyes.
...The sky always looks like this back in Moonvale.
A sharp crescent drowned in the mist...
... and if you go up to Avalon in the dead of winter, it dresses itself in snow white.
A single flake drifts through the window and, as she watches it, settles gently in Ursula's hair.
It comes to rest within a lock of white, a strand bleached pale by her curse.
It comes to rest within the curve of a lock, a lone trail of white amidst her raven hair.
(Gently remove the snowflake from her hair)
...Guess I'll just have to start wearing a wig, then.
She lets out a small sigh.
...have to say...seeing the snow fall like this stirs something in me.
.everything will be white, just like in Avalon.
Her voice seems tinged with regret.
You watch in silence as flakes, silvered by the crescent moon's soft glow, drift slowly down to the earth.
...I would love to go back to Moonvale with you, and...create new memories there.
The snow is falling in rapid cascades now.
As the lands of Brizh drape themselves in white, a shared fascination slowly takes a hold of you.
Then, like a silent thanks, a faint smile touches Ursula's lips.
. a smile that warms your heart.
. don't know if you'd have actually managed to wipe away the bad memories, but.
.would have liked to see you try.
Anyway...even if you were being serious.
You have never seen her so...shaken.
She takes a deep breath before finding her voice again.
your restrained proximity suddenly feels terribly cruel.
It won't be a problem (Take her hand).
On contact, she seems to stiffen.
With silent apologies brimming in her eyes, she gently pulls her hand away from yours.
The snow continues to fall steadily outside the window.
. I've thought of you in a certain way too, you know.
it's such a strange feeling, to be in your service and feel.
You could send me to die at the kingdom's farthest reach if such was your wish.
You wield the power to command what fills me with the deepest revulsion, to bend my very desires to your will.
. but the truth is, you're in charge. And that.
You're right to be fearful... but I want you to believe that I see you as my equal.
And yet I will never be the one who issues orders to you...
. Can we ever truly be equal, chained as we are by power?
Nothing is set in stone. I don't want to be just a Sovereign with you...I'm offering you something more.
Outside, the dance of the falling snow finally seems to ease.
A hush falls over the room.
...Then, with a shy, faltering step, she leans in and rests her head gently against your chest, her eyes still lost to the world outside.
Her scent fills your senses as you welcome her into your arms.
. we'll talk about this tonight, won't we?
Slowly, you lift your mask to catch the scent of her hair.
A kiss placed there, and a tender lethargy washes over you, numbing the embrace of your two bodies.
Without a word, you watch the last flakes fade away, joining the white mantle that drapes your lands.
Amid the silence and the cold's sharp bite, you stay nestled against each other, sheltered from the world.
Until nothing lingers in the air but a soft and fragile comfort.
the crescent moon seems to offer you its own gentle protection
ursule_full_romance.prev: Ursula stands upright, leaning out of one of the windows in the hallway.

lines: ... May our path be paved with glory, then.
You find Victoria absorbed in the '[i]History[/i]' section, searching with meticulous focus.
Upon drawing near, her vexation becomes apparent, her eyes narrowed with evident disdain.
Is there a single book in your damned library that isn't a rag of nonsense?
I'm looking for a single book, just [i]one[/i], that is not a rag of nonsense in this cursed library of yours.
You need a far richer collection of knowledge if you wish to call yourself a Sovereign worthy of the name. To be greatness is to be steeped in history, my little bird.
Yet not a single volume here offers a worthy account of Sovereign Herod's reign.
Your library is overflowing with absurdities and ridiculous nursery rhymes for simple-minded children regarding the other idiots who have succeeded one another on this throne...
I don't know much about Herod. Who were they?
That's unacceptable. I'll mention it to Sir Arlin.
I don't think I have much to learn from such a ruler.
Surely then you agree it is incomprehensible that no records exist here concerning the Sovereign who was undoubtedly the mightiest ruler these lands have ever witnessed.
Never has a monarch exerted such a hold, capable of bending all enemy territories to his will.
Fallen from the nest and so much to learn, you poor little bird.
In ages past, Herod was the Sovereign who brought true prosperity to these lands.
An iron fist whose grip crushed all opposition, no matter how slight, conquering half the Empire's territory in the process.
Herod's knights were all renowned for their ferocity on the battlefield.
Dagon of Drakovic and his brother Drarcus of Gavault, Almor the First or even William the Marksman...
Some of them sound familiar? They all earned the titles and lands that are now occupied by their descendants.
... Herod and his men were so strong that no one since has been worthy to stand in their shadow.
You must dismiss the incompetent fool who assembled such a pathetic collection.
What a tragedy to witness a royal library so lamentably biased...
What could your wretched little knights possibly glean here, I wonder?
A Sovereign worthy of the name must be steeped in the legacy of his predecessors.
Even if you elect to remain a second-rate Sovereign,
a pitiful wretch cowering with his tail between his legs,
it is nonetheless instructive to draw wisdom from those who are your very antithesis.
Do you wish to be a worthy Sovereign, little bird?
I already am. I have no need for your petty prerogatives.
The hesitation in your voice disgusts her to the highest degree.
If you carry on addressing me in that whiny little tone, I won't be staying here much longer...
That is exactly what I expect from you, my little fledgling.
You still have a long way to go...
She pauses for a few minutes, sizing you up with her eyes.
And I must emphasize, little bird
.that you made a strong impression on me during the grueling trials I put you through...
For all that, I must acknowledge, little bird
you have left a lasting mark upon me throughout the grueling trials I put you through...
You heeded me with commendable obedience, making no attempt at deception...which would hardly have suited you.
Not to mention that such foolishness would have been utterly reckless. My powers of clairvoyance are legendary
. Nothing escapes my sight. You know this full well, do you not?
But do you understand, little bird
And do you understand, little bird
...Being a ruler worthy of the name also implies not lying with impunity to your most dangerous warrior?
My powers of clairvoyance are legendary
. Nothing escapes my sight. You know this full well, do you not?
Her voice becomes hypnotic to your ears.
I... I hope you can forgive me.
(Lie) I don't know what you're implying.
... I wouldn't dare lie to you.
Why would I do that? With you by my side, I fully intend to be the most feared leader.
Know that I hold grudges for a lifetime, little bird.
As I said, you still have a lot to learn...
I feel that we will share a grand destiny together, my dear little bird.
victoria_affinity_1.prev: You find Victoria absorbed in the '[i]History[/i]' section, searching with meticulous focus.

lines: Victoria stands motionless, her focus absolute.
In front of her a throwing target.
Your knight tenses, her arm raised high and rigid as a pike, and then.
With a swift, whip-like motion, she embeds a throwing knife right in its heart.
A perfect shot, as it should be.
Imagine if it had been your throat instead of that plank of wood
She bends down to pick up a new blade and then returns to her previous state of concentration, holding her head high.
By all the demons, are you actually [i]trying[/i] to make conversation?...
... Do you truly believe I became the finest knight in all this kingdom by pure [i]magic[/i]?
Leaning slightly forward, she narrows her eyes to focus her shot.
... You should impose this same routine on those incompetents who pass for my colleagues.
Not a single one here, at this Table, is up to the task.
Her knife strikes the target once more with a sharp crack.
Is there a single warrior in this entire kingdom who is your equal?
You get only a long silence in response.
...A new knife hits the centre of the target.
I find it hard to believe that you've become so strong through training alone.
What's the greatest danger you've faced?
A few seconds pass amid a heavy silence.
. There is indeed another warrior who once earned my respect.
A new knife joins her hand.
... Indeed, that is not the whole truth.
... I have traveled the full breadth and length of this kingdom.
I sincerely doubt that even half these fools gathered in your court have collectively covered a mere fraction of the ground I have crossed.
... Or faced half the dangers I have overcome.
...You should know that I've already managed to kill.
... A struggle that has left its mark.
The deep wounds inflicted by demons are.
I did the only thing left to do to ensure my survival...
The target splinters as a final blade buries itself deep within the wood.
From the far side of the grounds, the weapon master's harsh voice exhorts Victoria to treat the equipment with proper regard.
Enough questions for today, little bird.
What a rare privilege it is to have a Knight of your caliber join my cause...
And you don't even have the slightest idea how many ways I can make your eyes sparkle...
Her gaze is filled with disgust for your quivering, little voice.
She turns away without paying you any more attention.
victoria_affinity_2.prev: Victoria stands motionless, her focus absolute.

lines: Trapped face-to-face with Victoria in this confined space, you have the sensation that the walls are closing in and that the air is growing thin.
Get out of here right now.
I'm curious to see how those frail little arms intend to stop me...
Her suave voice is now nothing more than a breath against your ear.
Well now, are you having trouble opening your little sparrow's beak?
Her voice, now a mere breath against your ear, is filled with amusement.
You fail to stop a shiver running down your spine.
A demon dwells within these walls, or has dwelt here
I can yet sense the foul miasma of its presence.
How do you explain this, little crowned lamb?
. You're aware of everything that breathes within your walls, are you not?
(Lie) I don't know anything about a demon.
. But don't waste your time playing dumb with me by [i]lying[/i].
Is its presence similar to that of the demon you fought long ago?
The demon I faced dwelled within the depths of Anveld's darkest dungeon
Something about it called to me.
I could discern nothing, yet I followed its pulsations.
It is that same poison now thrumming within these walls.
You're a curious little bird, aren't you?
... The poison finally dragged me before this thing
. A putrid creature whose blood-red eyes were the only light piercing the darkness.
... Its drawling whisper began to infect my mind, depositing words like maggots burrowing through flesh
Your vision flickers, and the last glimmers of light in this tomb seem to slip away.
My body was the only prey that demon coveted.
... And you already know the end of the story, don't you?
You killed it and devoured its heart.
... What does a demon taste like?
The only way to heal my wounds.
A bit of butter and cream wouldn't have gone amiss to help it go down.
... Still, you ought to take heed of this presence I discern lurking here, little bird
... It would grieve me greatly if one of those creatures stripped your wings bare.
The creature does not frighten me... I have an appetites far more dangerous.
... May we satisfy our appetites together, then.
Will you finally do me the honour of welcoming me to your miserable court?
Oh, you poor little foolish bird.
[shake]Do you really think I'm going to stay here, patiently waiting for you?![/shake]
Consider yourself fortunate I am not in a fouler mood.
Long after our story had ended, the Great Knight Victoria continued to inspire absolute dread across the lands of Bretania.
Having become a close advisor to the sovereign, the terrified screams of the Kingdom's enemies became the grim anthem that branded its legacy in iron and blood...
victoria_ending.prev: Long after our story had ended, the Great Knight Victoria continued to inspire absolute dread across the lands of Bretania.

lines: Victoria stands fixated on a rose bush.
This sight, as mundane as it may be, leaves you with a strange impression.
Our gardeners do a wonderful job, don't they?
I don't care for those idiots.
Take a look at this instead...
You slowly approach and stand beside her.
She shifts slightly, surprised that you thought you could approach her so casually without saying a word.
At first glance, nothing catches the eye.
A few crimson rosebuds peek tentatively through the thicket, while others bloom in full splendour.
you discern a pair of praying mantises,
delicately perched upon a frail branch extending from the bush.
Then you see that one mantis is slowly devouring the other's head.
Nature's beauty and brutality in one dance.
Is love not, at its essence, the art of surrendering oneself to be devoured?.
For the male, the price of union is merely his head.
A female thus nourished by her mate will bear far superior offspring.
This capacity to surrender entirely, until nothing of oneself remains...
In the bush, the mantis has finished devouring its mate's head. Yet the mating continues.
You desire the vertigo of the abyss, but you lack the courage to lose yourself in it entirely.
...And yet you covet it in silence, unable to admit your own sordid desires...
That desire which drives you to my side today.
... I have tested many suitors, yet none have proved capable of such self-sacrifice...
Your gaze returns to the branch, but the pair of mantises have vanished.
.Nothing but men and women who ultimately ended up boring me.
... Not my idea of a healthy relationship.
...Nothing is healthy when it comes to love.
To think you can tame what obsesses you... is a sweet and dangerous illusion.
Devotion is the purest form of love. You deserve it.
...And who might offer it to me?
Despite their dismal failure, I must say the experiences at least taught me how to... really have a good time.
... That's the most important thing... I guess.
A cruel amusement takes shape in her eyes.
She sizes you up from head to toe.
Is this truly what you desire?
Within your core, fear intertwines with a strange excitement, much as prey must feel.
With a sharp movement, she seizes you by the throat to plunge her eyes into yours.
After a brief journey punctuated by a struggle of burning caresses, you arrive at your private quarters.
She pins you brutally against the door and lifts away the top of your mask without hesitation.
...Is it already too much for you, little fledgling?
You spin her around against the door and your lips meet in a devouring kiss.
An impact that triggers a symphony of new sensations within you.
Her eyes grow hazy... a mixture of astonishment and lust.
She bites your lips softly in return.
... Little bird, I appreciate your strong temperament...
The door gives way with a crash and then swings back on its hinges.
Brutally forced down, you find yourself on your knees, with only the floor in your line of sight.
She coils herself against you, and her hand instinctively finds the curve of your neck to pin you to the ground.
What unfolds now is...hard to express in words.
...Let's say we are watching a joust of courtesies between two adults, where each one tries to take the driver's seat.
All in perfect and warm harmony, of course
It takes its own sweet time.
An eternity appears to have transpired within the intimacy of this chamber when you open your eyes once more.
Judging by your labored breath and the beads of perspiration upon your skin, anyone would conclude that you have indeed have had a good "laugh" alongside her.
In the distance, the sound of life swarming within the walls of the Tower slowly brings you back to reality.
victoria_full_romance.prev: Victoria stands fixated on a rose bush.

lines: At the last weekly market, between the carrot and cheese stalls, some.
. utterly [i]hideous little scoundrels[/i] were selling [shake][b]cursed amulets[/b][/shake], in the likeness of all kinds of [shake][b]humanoid articles[/b][/shake]...
Eyes, fingers, misshapen mouths, all cast in resin... [font_size=18]DO NOT let me get started on the organs...[/font_size]
Sounds cool. One of my knights will fetch these little wonders.
Do not delay before these trinkets corrupt our children.
By the Gods...As long as you keep them away from my dear Gwendoo.
She looks at you with an air of superiority.
And here YOU are. Villador's *FAMOUS* emissary.
Already heard of me have you

Were you trying to surprise me, Boss?
Very good, Boss. You've learnt it's in your best interest to not [i]accidentally[/i] startle me.
I admit I only sensed you some mere moments before you arrived.
Your footsteps were soft, as if you were trying to make as little noise as possible. Admit it, you're a bit sneaky, aren't you?
Why of course. Aren't we all?
Not very honest, at the very least.
I was thinking of you, anyway.
Here, In the *temple* of wisdom and knowledge?
I'm surprised not to see you in training. Or in the intendancy.
I appreciate dusty scrolls as much as a good sweat in training.
I'd like to say it's out of conviction that knowledge is power.
But truth be told, it's mostly nostalgia. These pages describe landscapes I was lucky enough to behold.
Moments shared between certain writers and my own travels. Across the seas and the oceans.
Oh dear, have you seen the time? I'm expected.
My dearest memory lies beyond the lands of Angelor.
endearing smile there that I never got to see anywhere else.
The air suddenly seems less charged with static electricity.
A little urchin who followed me around. An orphan girl... my disciple.
Enough for her to discover the world on her own.
And that memory is something I wouldn't swap for anything in the world.
[shake][b]Anyway, I could also tell you how I swam across the southern bay and met the local mermaids![/b][/shake]
I'm always up for hearing your stories, Lady Zolta.
A touch of sentimentality. I see.
And I could edit some of the books in this library. These writers have never lifted a finger from their armchairs, I tell you!
Or ever touched grass in their lives.
Ha ha ha! I don't see what you're on about.
You asked me about my best memories, and I answered, didn't I?
[shake][b]I'm a woman of action, after all!
... Stories aren't really your thing, are they?
I still need a little more time.
I don't want to do business with you anymore.
... There was no need to call me in for that.
Some years later, Zolta's contract ended.
She left the Tower in search of new, more exciting (and profitable) adventures.

lines: It's been a pleasure doing business with you.
